title: CI: run the gates workflow as four parallel jobs; the identifier controls skip the kernel replay
description:
The gates workflow takes about 32 minutes on the public runner: one job, every step in series. The owner
decided on 2026-10-02 to run it as four parallel jobs and to stop the two identifier controls
from paying for a kernel replay they do not use. The design below is settled; no consultation is needed.

## Measured (2026-10-02, commit 28bae18, ubuntu-24.04 public runner, 4 CPU)

- Job: 32.5 min.
- `Run all gates`: 285 s. Inside it: dev shell 22 s, Lean build 73 s, then the index, the
  `leanchecker --fresh` replay, render and values in about 185 s, then the other eight gates in 3 s.
- The 71 controls: 1655 s in series.
- `Prove the identifier gate rejects a tag naming a withdrawn id` and `... an undefined id`:
  196 s and 193 s. Each runs the whole formal gate only to get `.lake/index.jsonl`, and the
  replay is most of that time.
- Per-step GitHub times: `/var/tmp/ctl/gh-steps-28bae18.tsv` (number, name, start, end).
- On this machine, four controls at a time peak at 11.7 GB. Each job runs its steps in series,
  so memory is not a constraint.

## 1. `tools/check_formal.sh --no-replay`

- The flag skips only the `lake env leanchecker --fresh BtcPolicy` block. Everything else runs
  unchanged and in the same order: the greps, the build, the import walk, the index, render and
  values. When skipped, it prints one line saying the replay was skipped.
- Any other argument is an error that exits 2.
- `tools/check-all.sh` still calls it with no argument, so the full gate always replays.
- The two identifier controls above pass `--no-replay`. No other control changes its call: the
  other eleven expect a failure before the replay is reached.

## 2. `.github/workflows/gates.yml`: four parallel jobs

- Strategy: `fail-fast: false`, `matrix: shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]`.
- Job name: `specification gates (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})`.
- Checkout and install-nix run on every shard, with no `if:`.
- `Run all gates` gets `if: matrix.shard == 0`. Its body is unchanged.
- A new step right after it, `if: matrix.shard != 0`, runs
  `nix develop --command bash tools/check_formal.sh --no-replay`. It builds the `.lake` that the
  controls copy, including the index, regions and values that the citation, copies and regions
  controls read.
- Every control step gets exactly one `if: matrix.shard == N` in that literal form, with N in the
  matrix list. Do not reorder, rename or edit the control bodies. The two `--no-replay` edits
  are the only body changes.
- **Balance the shards from the measured times.** Shard 0 carries `Run all gates` (285 s).
  Every other shard carries the formal setup step, estimated at 130 s. Each identifier control
  is estimated at 196 s minus 150 s for the replay. Assign controls longest first (LPT) so the
  four estimated shard totals sit within 10% of their mean. Record the estimated totals in the
  report, not in the repository.

## 3. A guard that every step runs on the shards it should, with its own negative control

Write a small check (a Python script under `tools/`, run in the dev shell) and run it from a step
on shard 0. It fails, with a message naming the step, unless all of these hold:

- The matrix shard list is exactly `[0, 1, …, N-1]`.
- Checkout and install-nix have no `if:`.
- `Run all gates` has `if: matrix.shard == 0`, and its body is exactly
  `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`.
- The formal setup step has `if: matrix.shard != 0`.
- Every other step has exactly `if: matrix.shard == N`, with N in the list.
- `tools/check-all.sh` does not contain `--no-replay`.

Following this repository's rule that every gate is proven able to fail, add a control step. In a
scratch copy it deletes one control's `if:` line and asserts the guard exits nonzero with the
exact expected message. It also asserts the guard passes on the untouched copy.

## 4. Prose

Grep `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/` for any sentence that the new layout makes
false: one job, steps in order, or every step running on every push. Fix only those sentences.

- `README.md` lines 25 and 40 stay true. CI still runs `check-all.sh`, now on shard 0, and
  still breaks a document on every run.
- `AGENTS.md` keeps "`.github/workflows/gates.yml` holds the list".

No ADR is needed. This is CI layout, not a specification decision.

## Done when

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` passes, run unpiped and alone in the checkout.
- `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py <steps>` passes on the working tree
  for the new guard, its control and the two identifier controls. Split the steps into chunks
  that each finish within 10 minutes.
- Each shard is replayed after the commit, in a clean worktree. That replay is the maintainer's
  job, not this one's.
- The guard's control is measured at its exact message.
- One commit. No commit message, and no added line in any file, names a model, a review tool or
  an adviser, or carries a Co-Authored-By trailer. This repository is public.
close_reason: Workflow runs as four shards; identifier controls skip the replay; tools/check_shards.py guards the layout with its own control

title: Citation gate: a word between `X` and its speech verb (`X` now says "…") leaves the quote never held to X
description:
The citation gate never holds a quote to `X` when a word stands between `` `X` `` and its speech
verb, so a false quote written "`X` now says "…"" passes.

`ATTRIB` in `tools/check_citations.py` reads `` `X` `` (or `` `X`'s ``), then optionally "own",
then the verb. Any other word between them ("now", "still", "also", "no longer", "previously")
leaves the phrase unread as an attribution. Its quote then belongs, by the gate's ownership rule, to
the last attribution starting before it in the chunk, or to no one; and an unquoted
"`X` no longer says …" is never counted.

Measured at `7f8dee2`, against `find()` in memory:
- `` `DOM-1` now says "a phrase DOM-1 has never contained anywhere". `` and the same with
  "also states" are green: nothing checked, nothing counted.
- `` `OVR-1` says "<OVR-1 text>"; `DOM-1` now says "<OVR-1 text>". `` is green: both quotes are held
  to `OVR-1`, none to `DOM-1`.
- `` `OVR-1` no longer says the rule applies. `` is green and uncounted.
- On the tree, `ADR-0023` carries `` `DUR-4` still says "Ingress never arms" ``. The quote is in
  `DUR-4`'s body today, but no check holds it there.

Not a regression: `ATTRIB` has had this shape since before `bps-2jz`. That bead removed the
history-marker exemption from the unquoted rule; its brief put `ATTRIB`'s forms out of scope. With
the exemption gone, a word between the id and the verb is the shortest way to write an attribution
the gate neither checks nor counts. The module docstring declares the README's `once said` form as
unread, but not this general shape.

Done when: the owner has decided whether a quote after "`X` <word> <verb>" is held to `X`, or the
shape is refused, or it is declared a limit in the module docstring; any quote the change newly
checks on the tree passes or is corrected; `tools/citation-baseline.json` stays byte-identical; and a
`gates.yml` case plants a false quote in the decided shape and asserts the decided result.

comments.text:
Decision, 2026-10-18: REFUSE. Between `` `X` `` and its speech verb the gate reads one word from a
known list like the bare verb, leaves the exempt words (`once`, passive auxiliaries) unread as today,
and refuses any other single word, naming `X` and the word.

Review panel, two rounds, four readers (A-D). Evidence, letter-named: round 1 in
`/var/tmp/cite-evidence/68a-panel/`, round 2 in `/var/tmp/cite-evidence/68a-panel/r2/`.
- Round 1 split 2-1-1: A and B a fixed list with every other word skipped as today (LIST); C read any

- Round 2: 4-0 for REFUSE; A, B and C changed their votes. Each reader built both options with one

Corrections to the triage comment above:

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Between `` `X` `` and its speech verb the citation gate reads one word from a known list

title: Citation gate never checks a quotation longer than 400 characters; two WTC-14 quotations in Watchtower.lean go unread
description:
The citation gate never checks a quotation longer than 400 characters, and stays green when one is
wrong.

`QUOTE` in `tools/check_citations.py` pairs quotes only for spans of 8 to 400 characters. A longer
quotation is no span: its text is read as prose, and nothing compares it with its owner's body.

Measured at `4ddca43`: `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Watchtower.lean` carries two `WTC-14` colon-form
quotations, "A pass whose tip is below the newest anchor MUST return without advancing; … resets the
cursor to genesis", of 497 and 496 characters. Neither is checked, and the verified count does not
include them. Their words inside read as prose: before `bps-mmt` the "no longer" in them exempted both
chunks as history.

Done when: a quotation over the cap is either checked whole or refused (the choice is the owner's;
splitting into shorter quotes with `…` is one remedy the gate already supports); every quotation
the change newly checks passes or is corrected; and a `gates.yml` negative control corrupts one word
inside a quotation longer than 400 characters and asserts the refusal.

`reads` with no quote is a consult, so the false quote is green. Round 2: all four chose S over
refusing long quotations (R) and over keeping the cap with an uncapped match at direct openers only
(O).

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** The citation gate checks a quotation of any length, and pairing restarts at the explicit
opener after every attribution, so a stray quote mark before an attribution cannot swallow its
quotation.

**Current behavior:** `QUOTE` pairs only spans of 8 to 400 characters. Three attributed quotations
are longer (two `WTC-14` in `Watchtower.lean`, one `WTC-24` in `Package.lean`) and are never
checked, so a wrong word inside them is green. Two further shapes are green at today's cap, verified
at `1e1fadd` against the S prototype: `` `OVR-1` reads "<false phrase plus about 450 characters>" ``
(no span, so `reads` is a consult), and `` A 6" field and the node reads it, and `OVR-1` reads "<false>" ``
(the near stray mark takes the opener). `ANCHORED_QUOTE`'s re-scan repairs pairing only after a
direct opener (colon or possessive).

**Desired behavior:** `QUOTE` has no upper length bound. Every attribution outside a quotation an
earlier attribution introduced restarts pairing at its explicit opener, as direct openers do today,
so a quote mark before it cannot pair across it. All three shapes above go red naming `OVR-1`, and
the three long quotations in the tree are checked and pass. The known cost, accepted: a stray quote
mark after an attribution and far from its quotation can pair with that quotation's opener and fail
the chunk blaming the prose between; that is a red, never a green.

**Key interfaces:** `QUOTE`, `ANCHORED_QUOTE` and the pairing repair in `find()`; the module docstring,
which must state the new pairing, drop every statement of the 400-character limit, and state the
accepted false red.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] No length bound on a quotation; the three long quotations are checked (the verified count rises
      by three on an otherwise unchanged tree) and pass.
- [ ] The three shapes in "Current behavior" fail the gate naming `OVR-1`, each as a `gates.yml` case.

      comment with the reason.
- [ ] `tools/citation-baseline.json` byte-identical; `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`
      exits 0, run unpiped.

**Out of scope:** quotations that run past a sentence end (`bps-` follow-up filed with this decision);
the teaching phrases (`bps-mxm`); a word between an id and its speech verb (`bps-68a`); the quoted and
unquoted rules otherwise.

title: Operator program: bps-w8a review fixes: balance total, one retry limit, IBD refusal, batch outcomes, one home per rule
description:
The 2026-10-07 two-axis review of `bps-w8a` (commits `ed1798d` and `48a4c4b`) found behaviour gaps and duplicated rules. The owner decided the behaviour after a four-reader review. Nothing in `bps-w8a`'s accepted design changes.

## Decisions (the owner's, 2026-10-07)

1. **`balance`'s total.** It sums `OPR-62`'s population, the confirmed chain UTXO set. A coin a mempool transaction spends still counts until that spend confirms, and eviction changes nothing. There is no per-coin mark and no mempool-inclusive read in `balance`. The figure is labelled a confirmed-chain total, never an available-to-spend total, and the help text says so. `OPR-66`'s "the program's own chain view shows every predecessor coin named by the sweep as spent" means absent from that confirmed population, so a mempool-spent coin is not spent. Do not call such a coin "pending": `CONTEXT.md` reserves *Pending spend* for a spend waiting out its Hold.
2. **Retry limit.** `OPR-82` owns one limit for every caller: at most three brackets per invocation, "no sleep, backoff or scheduler". Running out is a local refusal, exit `1` under `OPR-4` (not "inconclusive", which `OPR-4` reserves for a watch). Running out MUST NOT read as a no-nag-due maturity result (`OPR-62`, `OPR-63`). `OPR-33`'s "at most three passes …" then cites `OPR-82` instead of restating it. `WTC-28` (node) is unchanged.
3. **Initial block download.** `OPR-82`'s coherent-view rule gains: the chain info MUST NOT report initial block download, for every caller. `OPR-33`'s "refuses during initial block download" cites it. A backend that is behind but not flagged still passes, so `balance` and the maturity report print the accepted tip's height and MTP.
4. **Batch outcomes.** `refresh` exits `0` only when every batch the accepted pass composed was sent and observed, or for `OPR-65`'s zero-eligible no-op. Batches go one at a time: batch k+1 is sent only after batch k's watch observed it. The first batch not observed stops the run and leaves later batches unsent: a refusal, a definite no-delivery, or an inconclusive watch. Each batch's outcome is reported (observed, refused, no-delivery, inconclusive or unsent), with no outpoints (`OPR-8`). Widen `OPR-65`'s "On a refresh refusal, the program MUST report it and stop" to cover every unobserved batch. Scope `OPR-51`'s "the earlier pre-ingress warning does not apply to this invocation" and "the one nonzero result that does not demand an independent chain check" to the batch, not the invocation. Adjust `OPR-4`'s `0` and `OPR-2`'s success sentence only as far as this needs.
5. **No speculative recovery sequences.** Delete `OPR-62`'s "An actual recovery transaction choosing a larger sequence delay can mature later" and `CNF-125`'s `L + 1` input-sequence case. `CHN-10` says "MUST set every input's `nSequence` to `4224679` exactly".

## Cleanup (standards axis; every item is a rule with two homes or a house rule broken)

- **`OPR-82` is the one owner** of the bracket and evidence rules, including the retry rule, tip agreement, the supplied-field list and the "before its closing tip read" timing. `OPR-33` cites it instead of restating them. `OPR-82` stops repeating itself ("all evidence reads MUST belong to that bracket" / "All evidence belongs inside the same tip bracket").
- **The predecessor `P` is defined once.** It lives either in `OPR-62` (maturity's concept) or in `OPR-82`, and the other cites it.
- **Rename `T` (tip) in `OPR-62`.** `CONTEXT.md` defines `T` as the duress deadline, and `OPR-65` writes `MTP(tip)`. Use `tip` consistently.
- **No bare "anchor"** (`CONTEXT.md` avoid list) in `OPR-62` or `CNF-125`.
- **`OPR-50`** stops counting `OPR-32`'s list ("the eight ordinary backend reads"). Cite the list and let it hold the number.
- **`OPR-62`'s BIP68/BIP112 text** cuts to the link plus the inclusive formula and the one fact the set relies on: the predecessor's MTP. Drop the walk through `CalculateSequenceLocks`/`EvaluateSequenceLocks` and the BIP112 checklist, which BIP68 and BIP112 own. `CNF-125` keeps its numeric cases.
- **`OPR-65` cites node rules** instead of restating them as its own MUSTs: `SPN-44`'s 24-input limit, and `CHN-18`'s `0xfffffffd` sequence and input order (the old text cited `CHN-18`). Write the constant 24 once.
- **The no-manifest network question becomes a finding.** `OPR-58`'s "remains open and unverified" paragraph becomes an `F`-numbered OPEN finding in `16-open-findings.md`. `OPR-58`, `OPR-62`, `OPR-72` and `CNF-126` cite the finding instead of quoting the paragraph.
- **Conformance items stop duplicating each other.**
  - The no-op, refusal-and-stop and eligibility cases each live in one `CNF` item; the others point to it.
  - `CNF-151` loses the cases that belong to other items, and keeps age selection, header faults, genesis, reorg, batch order and dust.
  - Drop `CNF-151`'s `OPR-49` "later acceptance after an earlier endpoint refusal" case, which belongs to delivery.
  - `CNF-151` gains its closing `(…)` id list.
  - Add exhaustion, IBD and mixed-outcome cases for decisions 2–4. Add the mempool-spent, then evicted, then confirmed sequence with an unchanged total to `CNF-124`.
- **No change history in normative text.** Remove "moving the evidence contract" (`OPR-33`), "With `OPR-82` integrated, still" (`CNF-93`), "the unchanged `OPR-2` boundary" (`CNF-116`) and "existing node rules" (`OPR-65`).
- **Archive.**
  - `docs/archive/closed-findings.md` preserves the blocks at `916d921` (`docs/archive/README.md`). Restore the reworded historical row and narrative, and append one undated pointer line instead.
  - Remove the dated tags "**2026-10-06 amendment:**" and "(extracted from `OPR-33` on 2026-10-07)".
  - If restoring the old "eight calls" text trips the bead's grep, scope that grep to normative files, since `docs/archive/` is outside every gate glob.

## Out of scope

- Node rules: `SPN-43`–`SPN-47`, `WTC-2`, `WTC-3`, `WTC-28`, `WTC-30`, `OPR-9`, `CHN-10`.
- Answering the no-manifest network question itself.
- Concurrency between batches beyond decision 4.

## Done when

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0 unpiped.
- `tools/check_ids.py` accepts any new ids.
- `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py` passes every `gates.yml` step that reads `17-operator-program.md`, `15-conformance-checklist.md` or `16-open-findings.md`.
- A grep shows each rule above with one home.

title: DUR-14's update reads the candidate registration stores, never the request's own pair field
description:
`DUR-14`'s update reads the candidate registration stores, never the request's own `pair` field.

## What is wrong (found reviewing `bps-1mm` at `6ce5d96`; reproduced twice)

`Kernel.shrunkDeadline` asks `Kernel.inHotDomain` about `Kernel.shrinkTarget r env n sp`. On a fresh
pair `shrinkTarget` returns `born n.id n.armed env.mono sp`: the REQUEST's record, with its incoming
`pair` field as the requester sent it. `Kernel.register` stores a different record,
`{ sp with pair := some (sp.id, es.id) }`. Since `bps-1mm`, `inHotDomain` applies the role test
`Kernel.entryActs` under the current rule, and `Cand.isEscape` reads `pair`. So at this one site a
requester-supplied field decides the role, against `Cand.pair`'s own docstring ("Incoming metadata
is ignored").

Counterexample (`/var/tmp/cross-evidence/request-pair-trace.lean`, `Kernel.current`, `runHold 300`,
every step admitted by `Silence.wfEvent`): after `reusedIdTrace`'s pruned selected id 61 and an arm at
510 with `T = 700`, a hot spend arrives at 520 under id 61 with `fire_at` 400 (its window `[400, 440]`
already shut).
- Request record `pair := none`: `T` stays 700.
- Request record `pair := some (0, 61)`: the armed run's `T` becomes 520, below `SEC-37`'s floor of
  700 on that trace, and the selected Escape's window moves with it. The reviewer measured 700 for
  both records at `4616432`; re-measure it.

It has no instance in the text: a request carries no role (`SPN-32` registers it), and a fresh hot
spend's `fire_at` is `SPN-30`'s, never already past. But the kernel is wrong against its own stated
boundary, and two sentences added by `bps-1mm` are false of it: `DUR-10`'s formal scope ("so that a
spend carrying a selected id is read by its own window") and `ADR-0028` decision 5 ("a spend carrying
a selected id is read by its own window").

## The fix (no decision changes)

`Kernel.shrinkTarget` returns the candidate `Kernel.register` leaves under the spend's id: the resident
on a repeat, and on a fresh pair the born record carrying the registration-owned pair `(sp.id,
es.id)`. Prefer deriving it from `register` itself, so the two cannot part again (an earlier review
noted the preserve test is written out in three places). `shrunkDeadline`, `traverses`, `accept` and
`Silence`'s readers take whatever extra argument that needs.

## Acceptance

1. On the counterexample trace `T` is 700 under the current rules with either request record, and
   the two request records leave the same registry. An exhibit in `Exhibits.lean` pins it.
2. A theorem, if it proves — otherwise say why and keep the exhibit: `Kernel.shrunkDeadline` does
   not depend on the incoming spend record's `pair` field.
3. A planted-mutation control in `gates.yml`: the born target keeps the request's `pair`; the new
   exhibit goes red in `Exhibits.lean` only, count measured, owning proofs stubbed as `AGENTS.md` says.
4. Audit, listed in the closing comment: every use of `Kernel.entryActs`, `Cand.isEscape`,
   `Silence.selEsc` and `Cand.pair` in `Kernel.lean` and `Silence.lean`, and for each whether the
   candidate it reads is a registered one. Fix any other site that reads a request's own record.
5. **Hard stop.** If the fix needs (a) any new clause in `Silence.NodeInv` or a change to the type of
   a remaining field, (b) any new hypothesis on `Silence.silence` or `Silence.silence_initial`, (c)
   any change to `Silence.wfEvent` — in particular, do NOT close this by making `wfEvent` refuse a
   request whose `pair` is set — or (d) a `sorry` or an axiom: STOP, commit nothing, and report
   BLOCKED with what the proof needs. Show both statement diffs against `99d545b` in the closing
   comment (`silence_initial`: none; `silence`: only the rule threaded into `Coupled` and `NodeInv`).
6. Every existing exhibit keeps its verdict and its figures; a changed figure is a finding to report,
   not a number to re-measure. Existing controls keep their counts or the change is explained.
7. `DUR-10`'s formal scope and `ADR-0028` decision 5: the two sentences above are true of the kernel
   as landed (verify by the exhibit, not by reading); `shrinkTarget`'s docstring says what it returns.
8. The gate is green unpiped; the workflow steps that touch `Kernel.lean`, `Silence.lean` or
   `Exhibits.lean` replay green.

## Not in scope

No requirement sentence outside a formal scope changes. `EntryTarget`, `HotDomain` and `AcceptRead`
keep their values and meanings.

Commit 5ba1811. The closing comments hold both statement diffs, the controls, the audit and two cosmetic notes left.

title: Registration keeps an Escape record's incoming fire time, which SPN-37 says an Escape does not have
description:
Registration keeps an Escape record's incoming fire time, which `SPN-37` says an Escape does not have.

`Kernel.born` and `Kernel.register` store an incoming record's `fireAt` as the event gives it, for
both members of a pair. `SPN-37` says "The Escape member of a pair is registered with **no** fire
window". `Silence.wfEvent` refuses an incoming `windowClose` on either member, and its docstring
says neither member arrives carrying a window, but it does not look at the Escape record's `fireAt`.

Measured at `b203177` by the reviewer of `bps-860` (`Kernel.current`, `runHold 300`, the same under
both enrolment tables; `/var/tmp/cross-evidence/request-fields/Traces.lean`,
`escape_fireAt_reaches_release`, by `decide +kernel`): pair (60, 61) at 10 with Carrier 71 live to
900; a prune at 450; pair (59, 60) at 460, whose Escape record carries `fireAt` `none` in one run of
the trace and `some 0` in the other; Carrier 71's receipt at 470 opens id 60 and selects 61; a fire
pass at 480. `wfEvent` admits every step of both. With `none` the pass has no effect; with `some 0`
it queues a partial for candidate 60 on a node that is not armed. `T` is 670 in both.

It has no instance in the text. A request's Escape carries no fire window (`SPN-37`), and the trace
also needs one id in the spend role of one pair and later in the Escape role of another, which
`CHN-24` excludes: "Two distinct transactions MUST never share a commitment". Without that reuse the
holder decision overwrites the field. The definitions involved are unchanged since before `bps-pxp`,
so the published tree has it too. `bps-860`'s audit lists `fireAt` among the fields "stored on the
born record as the event gives them", which is true of a spend's and is this gap for an Escape's.

Direction, not decided: have registration clear the Escape member's fire time, so the kernel
enforces `SPN-37` where it now assumes it. The other shape, `wfEvent` refusing such a request,
changes the boundary `Silence.silence` is stated over and needs the owner's word first.

Done when: an Escape member is registered with no fire time whatever the incoming record carries
(or the owner has chosen the other shape); an exhibit runs the trace above with both records and
shows the same effects; a planted-mutation control restores the old registration and goes red in
`Exhibits.lean` only; `Silence.silence` and `Silence.silence_initial` keep their statements; the
gate is green unpiped.

comments.text:
Audit: every place a step reads the incoming Escape record (the `es` of `Event.accept` and of `Silence.Input.request`), at `cb6927e`. By the Implementer, from a grep of every `es` binder and every `(sp es : Cand)` parameter in `Kernel.lean`, `Silence.lean`, `Ledger.lean` and `Trace.lean`; Reviewer A checked it against a grep of its own, and the Manager read each body below. One line of the Implementer's list was wrong and is corrected here: `Kernel.due` does not read the release gate; `Kernel.firePass` tests `Kernel.releaseAuthorized` beside it.

RESULT. One site kept a field of the incoming Escape record that `SPN-37` says an Escape is registered without: `Kernel.register`, the Escape member's `fireAt`. It is fixed. No other reader reads the incoming Escape record's `fireAt`, and `Kernel.accept_ignores_escape_fireAt` proves the acceptance does not depend on it.

== Readers ==

`Kernel.pairAdmits`: `es.id` (distinct from the spend's, residency, the pair a resident must carry), and against a resident under that id `es.tx`, `es.hot` and `es.expiry`. Not this gap: it compares the request with state the node holds, which is `SPN-32`'s compatibility test.
`Kernel.register`: `es.id` for the pair stamp. On a birth it hands the record to `born` with `pair` overwritten and, since this change, `fireAt` cleared. THE FIXED SITE. Where it keeps the registry it reads nothing more of the record.
`Kernel.born`: reads `hot`, for `frozen := armed && hot`. Overwrites `quorum`, `frozen`, `terminal`, `settled`, `released`, `packageOk`, `broadcast`, `heldSigners` and `acceptedAt`. Keeps `id`, `tx`, `hot`, `expiry`, `fireAt`, `windowClose` and `pair` as handed to it.
`Kernel.logRegistration`: `es.tx.id`, as the sibling on the spend's entry; and `es.hot`, `es.id`, `es.tx` and `es.expiry` for an entry of its own when the Escape slot is hot, which `Silence.wfEvent` refuses. No `fireAt`.
`Kernel.shrinkTarget`, `Kernel.shrunkDeadline`, `Kernel.traverses`: `es.id` alone, the pair stamped on the born spend.
`Kernel.accept`: `es.id`, for the Carrier's pair and for a refusal's staged pair; it forwards the record to the readers above. `Kernel.step` forwards it.
`Ledger.refusedByBudget`, `Ledger.hotRequest`, `Ledger.admitted`, `Ledger.afterEvent`: the spend alone. `Ledger.budgetRefusal`, which `Ledger.sysStep` calls on a budget refusal: `es.id`, for the staged pair.
`Silence.Input.event`: forwards both records. `Silence.wfEvent`: `es.hot` and `es.windowClose`, with `sp.windowClose`; the request-shape boundary, with no test of `fireAt`. `Silence.respond`: the Escape record through `pairAdmits` alone; its accepted arm reads the spend's `fireAt`, which is `bps-svf`. `Silence.work`: through `traverses` and `register`, then the registered ids.
`Trace.KernelEvent.toKernel`: converts both records field by field and leaves `pair` absent.

== Fields of the Escape record: where each ends up, and what bounds it ==

`id`: the born record's id, the pair stamp, the Carrier's pair, a refusal's staged pair. Abstract in the kernel.
`tx`: stored; compared with a resident's; its id is the sibling on the spend's pending entry; a later release signs over it. Taken as given.
`hot`: stored; compared with a resident's; read by `born`'s freeze and by the pending log. Taken as given (`SPN-28`'s kernel paragraph); `wfEvent` requires it clear on an Escape.
`expiry`: stored; compared with a resident's; read later by the prune pass and by a window with no installed close. Taken as given, apart from the spend's and from the Carrier's `E` (the closing record's further traces).
`fireAt`: cleared on a birth since this change. Not read on the incoming record.
`windowClose`: stored as given; `wfEvent` refuses a request carrying one on either member.
`pair`, `acceptedAt`: overwritten by `register` and by `born` (`Kernel.accept_ignores_request_pair`, `bps-860`).
`quorum`, `frozen`, `terminal`, `settled`, `released`, `packageOk`, `broadcast`, `heldSigners`: overwritten by `born`.

`Kernel.withWindow`'s write of `fireAt` and `windowClose` is `DUR-20`'s install on a registered candidate, not a read of the request. On a hot acceptance it runs over the registry `register` returns, so a born Escape whose id is already selected gets its window in the same step: the clear is a property of what `register` births.

The spend record's own `fireAt` is stored as given and is not this ticket: `SPN-30` computes it in the text, and the kernel takes it.

Docstrings follow: the `Kernel` module scope, `Cand.fireAt`, `Kernel.register`, the theorem and the exhibit. No requirement sentence outside a formal scope changed. No finding was opened: the text has no instance of the trace, and `16-open-findings.md` records design state. The published tree has the defect, since the definitions involved predate it.

With 400 both members stay and the repeat is accepted. With 100 the prune removes the Escape alone, the spend is left without its sibling, and the repeat answers `PSBT_INCONSISTENT`. `wfEvent` admits every step of both. title: M6.1 Membership.lean: POL-4 scan with derive as the boundary; CNF-15 theorems; kindOf discharges Classification.member
description:
Milestone 6, ticket 1. tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Membership.lean: POL-4's scan as structure, with
key derivation as the named boundary. A descriptor is `definite` (one script) or `wildcard`
(scripts by index), with BIP389 multipath expanding to a list of single-path descriptors
(`expand`). `derive : SinglePath → Nat → Script` is a parameter (BIP32 + script construction are
outside Lean, decision 3). `indices max d := if wildcard then 0..=max else [0]`;
`matches derive d max s := ∃ p ∈ expand d, ∃ i ∈ indices max p, derive p i = s` as a Bool over
lists. Theorems (CNF-15): a script derived at `max` matches and one derived only at `max + 1`
does not (given derive injective on the index, as a hypothesis); both chains of a multipath
descriptor are scanned; a definite descriptor ignores the bound. Then discharge milestone 2's
`member`: `kindOf derive vault escape allow max script : Classification.Kind` decided by
`matches` (escape first, then hot, vault change is the vault descriptor — read CHN-30 / POL-10
for the order), and the statement that Classification's theorems hold with `kind := kindOf …`.
State the coverage boundary in the docstring: what of MAN-39's grammar `derive` abstracts
(every script context), what the structure covers (wildcard/definite × multipath × bound).
Tags POL-4, CHN-30. Done when check-all is green. One commit + beads close.
close_reason: Membership.lean landed: POL-4 scan structure, CNF-15 theorems, kindOf discharges member; check-all green

title: M8.1 Delivery.lean: OPR-49's sticky delivery reducer, OPR-51's reissue predicate and watch target, DEF-8 and F56 as twins
description:
Milestone 8, ticket 1 — the operator's delivery knowledge and the watch target, as a bounded state
machine (ADR-0023 decision 10 item 8: "the delivery reducer and watch selection (`DEF-8`, `F56`)").
The first of milestone 8's tickets; the reorg cursor (WTC-11..14, DEF-6), the cache and wallet
anchor (WTC-5..10, DEF-21), the watchtower classification and ancestry rules (WTC-17..25) and the
trace adapters stay on the epic until each is planned.

New module `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Delivery.lean` (namespace `BtcPolicy.Delivery`), imported from
`BtcPolicy.lean`, with its theorems over `current` in `Exhibits.lean` and one CI flip per guard
parameter in `.github/workflows/gates.yml`:

- OPR-49's sticky delivery state as a reducer over a list of per-endpoint attempt outcomes:
  "definitely not sent" → "possibly delivered", advanced by every outcome that is not `NotSent`,
  never moved back. Outcomes distinguish pre-connect `NotSent` (connect failed, or OPR-48's
  endpoint reached at or after the aggregate) from every post-connect outcome: `accepted` with a
  `commitment_id`, `NONCE_REPLAYED`, `400`, `413`, any other status, and a timeout, partial write,
  read or framing failure.
- The loop's stop rule: stop on `accepted` whose id equals the locally computed one; stop on
  `NONCE_REPLAYED` only when the state entering that attempt was already possibly-delivered;
  everything else continues (a mismatched `accepted` keeps its possible delivery and continues).
- OPR-51's reissue predicate: authorized exactly when EVERY endpoint was `NotSent`, proved
  equivalent to the reducer ending at "definitely not sent"; a single endpoint's `NotSent`
  authorizes nothing.
- OPR-51's watch target by request kind: output 1 of the primary for `spend`, output 0 for
  `clawback` and `refresh`.
- Two guard parameters with twins: DEF-8 (a post-connect failure read as `NotSent` authorizes a
  reissue after every endpoint failed post-connect; refused under `current`), and F56 (the watch
  fixed on output 1 has no output to watch on a one-in-one-out `refresh`; `current` watches
  output 0).

Done when `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green unpiped, each new flip is red
in `Exhibits.lean` and nowhere else and measured locally as the workflow runs it, and every
existing flip is still red at its count. No Markdown owner changes; the Run's
brief (2026-09-23) has the detail.

title: M8 spec-owner decisions: settled depth 10 for the wallet import, WTC-14 tip at the captured height, chunked delta commit; Markdown + Lean + ADR in one commit
description:
Land the settled-depth amendment and the three reorg readings the spec owner decided on
2026-09-27..29, in the Markdown AND the Lean model in one commit (AGENTS.md: "Change the
declaration and the Markdown together"), plus one ADR. Every choice below is SETTLED by the
maintainer after four consultation rounds (advisers B, C, D; A timed out on three); no
Consultation is needed. This answers bps-8s0.11.7 items 1-2 and bps-8s0.11.8 items 1-2.

## 1. The Markdown: apply it verbatim

`git apply .context/settled-depth-markdown.patch` (git-ignored, in this checkout). It amends
WTC-6, WTC-7, WTC-8, WTC-9, WTC-11, WTC-14 (10-watchtower-and-chain.md), OPS-71, DEF-21, CNF-89,
CNF-91 and adds six CONTEXT.md entries (Cache anchor, Scan anchor, Settled depth, Settled block,
Birthday, Completion marker). Do not reword it. If a Lean-side fact shows a sentence false,
stop and say so in the report instead of editing the sentence. After applying, the citation gate
reports 13 Lean docstring quotations that no longer match (Chain.lean 1, VaultUnspent.lean 9,
Watchtower.lean 3); every one moves in this commit.

The decisions the patch encodes, in plain terms:
- WTC-14: the tip check compares the ACTIVE HASH AT THE CAPTURED TIP HEIGHT after the scan (the
  reference's reading); a block arriving on top is the next pass's range; a panic anywhere in a
  pass, the tip comparison included, resets to genesis. Rationale: the chain-tip reading can
  never finish a genesis re-scan (WTC-13) on mainnet.
- WTC-6: the wallet read is discarded unless the tip captured before the listing is still the
  tip after the reconciliation (the reference's bracket); the delta walk commits a walk that
  completes even below the tip and continues next refresh (the reference's behaviour); a walk
  failing any proof is discarded whole; WTC-5 refuses a cache below the tip at fire time.
- WTC-7: SETTLED DEPTH 10. Scan anchor A; settled block S = 10 below A, or genesis when A's
  height is below 10. The cold scan plus a WTC-12-proven walk of the blocks above S ending at A
  itself form one result; a failed walk refuses the import. Birthday = LOWEST HEIGHT among S and
  the CREATING blocks of every output the scan found live or the walk found spent. The import is
  bracketed by re-proving S before the descriptors AND before the marker. A repair never starts
  later than the wallet already covers: if its birthday is not below the lowest birthday a held
  marker carries, it imports only a new marker; otherwise it re-imports from its own birthday.
- WTC-8: a marker carries S's height and hash AND the import's birthday; the wallet is usable
  while ANY held marker's anchor is active.
- WTC-9 / WTC-11: repair latches only when NO held marker's anchor is active; a shallow reorg is
  caught by the read's tip bracket.

## 2. The Lean model

- `Watchtower.pass`: replace the chain-tip comparison with the active hash at the captured
  height (Chain.lean's `Anchor.active` on the after-view); restate `pass_tip_changed` and
  `pass_completed`; add an exhibit where a block arrives on top and the pass is KEPT.
- `VaultUnspent`: `settledDepth : Nat := 10` tagged `WTC-7` beside `deltaWindow`; REGISTER BOTH in
  `Render.values` / `check_copies.py`'s owner registry so WTC-7's "10 blocks" and WTC-6's
  "32 blocks" are held (32 is tagged but unregistered today). Model spentness: the cold scan
  yields outputs live at A; the walk of (S, A] yields spends with their creating heights;
  `birthday` = min height over S and those creators (today `birthdayFrom` confirms any vault
  output and `coldScan` includes all confirmed outputs; neither survives). The import bracket
  re-proves S at both points. `Wallet` holds a list of markers `(settled anchor, birthday)`;
  `usable` = some marker active; repair is marker-only or re-import per WTC-7; the birthday never
  rises. `deltaFrom` drops the pre-walk `tip ≤ anchor + deltaWindow` gate and the
  `c'.anchor = v.tip` acceptance, walks through min(tip, anchor + 32) and commits; `served_at_tip`
  becomes a statement about what WTC-5 refuses; the exhibits
  `delta_walk_short_of_tip_refused` and `delta_walk_empty_below_tip_refused` invert.
- Guard parameters (AGENTS.md: "Every semantic choice a dated amendment changed is a guard
  parameter with a `current` value"): at least (a) WTC-7's marker anchor, `settled | scanTip`,
  whose withdrawn value's twin is the hole the amendment closes — an output created below S,
  spent inside the settled depth, resurrected by a shallow reorg that leaves the old anchor
  standing; (b) WTC-14's tip test, `capturedHeight | chainTip`; (c) WTC-6's delta commit,
  `partial | tipOnly`. Each with theorems over `current` in Exhibits.lean and a measured CI
  negative control in gates.yml. The Manager may argue a value is not a dated semantic change and
  drop its parameter, in the brief, with the reason.
- `Trace.lean` wallet/ledger adapters and `Exhibits.lean`'s `def21Birthday` trace follow the new
  shapes. The 13 quotations re-quote the new text.

## 3. The ADR

`docs/adr/0024-the-wallet-import-settles-ten-blocks-below-the-scan.md` (or the next free number):
the decision; the rejected alternatives — anchor at the scan tip (the reference; repairs on every
shallow reorg), trust only the newest marker (the model; refuted as a necessity by the regtest
run, and not recoverable from the wallet since import order is not stored), a full scan whenever

title: SEC-50 overstates the cold-scan cost: WTC-6 falls to the delta walk, not to the full scan
description:
`SEC-50` says of the cold full UTXO-set scan: "on a node whose backend cannot serve the descriptor
wallet, every refresh pays it, and Bitcoin Core serialises it process-wide." `WTC-6` orders three
sources, and the middle one is not the wallet: "a bounded delta walk of at most 32 blocks from a
cached anchor whose block is still active". Read by `WTC-6` alone, a node that cannot serve the
wallet falls to the delta walk, not to the cold scan, so it pays the cold scan once to seed a base
and then only when the base has moved or the walk is discarded.

`WTC-6` now says when a walk is discarded and what it costs: "A walk that covers less is discarded
whole, as is one that fails any proof (`WTC-12`), and the refresh falls through to the cold scan."
And it says a walk that cannot reach the tip does not fall through: "A walk that completes becomes
the cache even where it ends below the tip, and any later delta walk starts from that cache". So
under `WTC-6` the cold scan is the price of a discarded walk or a moved base, not of every refresh.

`WTC-9` states the latched case, and as amended on 2026-10-02 it no longer makes `SEC-50`'s "every
refresh" true there: "From the latch setting until a cold scan has replaced the cache, every refresh
with no attempt in progress starts a repair attempt from a cold scan, whatever cache it holds, the
scan replacing the cache before the re-import begins (`WTC-6`); thereafter, while the latch holds,
the cache is advanced by delta walks or their cold-scan fallback (`WTC-6`), and a wallet read never
replaces it." And of an attempt that fails: "one that ends without rebuilding the wallet leaves any
latch set; the next attempt starts only from a cold scan `WTC-6` itself reaches with none in
progress, and starts no scan of its own." So a latched node whose repair keeps failing pays the
cold scans its cache needs and none for the repair. A backend that cannot serve the wallet at all
is not latched: "A wallet holding no completion marker is not latched, `WTC-8` already keeping it
out of use: its first build, and any retry after a failed one, starts the same way, from a cold
scan `WTC-6` reaches with no attempt in progress." That was the open question bps-8s0.11.22
recorded, settled by the owner on 2026-10-02 and landed with bps-8s0.11.25. `WTC-9` states the
consequence itself: "A failed build or repair is therefore not retried while delta walks succeed;
the cache does not depend on the wallet." With that answer `SEC-50`'s "every refresh pays it" is
what neither `WTC-6` nor `WTC-9` says of either case.

(Rewritten 2026-10-01: the earlier text of this bead quoted two sentences the catch-up amendment
removed from `WTC-9` and `WTC-6`, the cost clause for a repair that keeps failing and the clause
on continuing a walk at the next refresh. The quotations above are the text as it stands. Updated
2026-10-02 with bps-8s0.11.25: the paragraph on `WTC-9` quotes it as amended that day.)

Scope: reword `SEC-50`'s cost sentence so it names the source `WTC-6` actually falls to in each
case, and cite `WTC-6`'s and `WTC-9`'s own words for the cost rather than restating a stronger one.
`SEC-50` is a security-residual note, not a normative MUST, so nothing else moves; no Lean
declaration owns it and no gate holds the sentence today. Owner: the specification repository.

Done when: `SEC-50`'s sentence carries the delta walk and the latched case, the citation gate
verifies whatever it quotes, and `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green.
close_reason:
Implemented in 3821cc4f5d4aabf53ea9dfdc84b8bffa46683943. Only SEC-50 and this bead's claim changed. Acceptance checks cover the ordinary delta fallback, completed walks below the tip, the latch's initial cold scan and subsequent delta advancement, the unlatched unbuilt wallet, and failed-attempt retry costs. The availability residual, process-wide scan serialization and need to measure mainnet cost are retained. No normative requirement, formal declaration, gate, baseline or later bead changed.

Verification: nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh ran unpiped before editing and after the final edit, both exit 0 with every summary entry PASS; final log /tmp/bps-8s0.11.14-gates.log. nix develop --command python3 tools/check_citations.py exited 0. Each quoted span in SEC-50 was checked for exact owner text and separately corrupted in memory through the citation gate entry point; every corruption returned 1 and named 12-security-requirements.md and its WTC-6 or WTC-9 owner, with no source or baseline mutation; evidence /tmp/bps-8s0.11.14-citation-probe.log. nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py 'citation gate' exited 0, every selected workflow step passed, and its final summary was DONE 0 failed of 12; evidence /tmp/bps-8s0.11.14-controls.log. git diff --check passed and the complete diff was inspected for scope and acceptance. No further gap found in this bead.

title: CONTEXT.md's Settled depth gloss states a latch condition WTC-9 does not state
description:
`CONTEXT.md`'s **Settled depth** entry, added verbatim by the 2026-09-29 settled-depth patch
(`ADR-0024`, `bps-8s0.11.13`), says:

"How far below the scan anchor a wallet import treats the chain as settled: a reorg no deeper
leaves every completion marker in force, and a deeper one latches a repair (`WTC-7`, `WTC-9`)."

`WTC-9` latches on a different condition: "If no completion marker the wallet holds has an anchor
on the active chain the node MUST latch a repair". The Lean model reads `WTC-9`, not the gloss:
`BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.observe` sets the latch exactly when `someMarkerActive` is false.

So the entry's second clause is false as a universal about the wallet. A reorg deeper than the
settled depth unseats the marker of *that* import; whether the wallet latches depends on whether
any other held marker's anchor is still active. A reorg of 11 blocks can unseat a marker anchored
at height 12 while an older marker anchored at height 2 stays active, and no repair latches.

`ADR-0024`'s decision 1 carries the same shorthand ("A reorg no deeper than 10 leaves every
completion marker in force and costs no repair; a deeper one latches one").

The sentence is the specification owner's: it arrived in a patch the implementing brief required be
applied verbatim and explicitly forbade rewording, so it was not touched when the amendment landed.
Rewording it is a spec-owner call, which is why this is a bead and not an edit.

Note that the *behaviour* is not in doubt — `WTC-9` owns the latch rule and is unambiguous, and
`CONTEXT.md` is the vocabulary file, not a normative source (`AGENTS.md`: "Vocabulary, overloaded
and banned words → `CONTEXT.md`"). This is a precision defect in a gloss, not a contradiction that
leaves behaviour undetermined.

Scope: reword the entry's second clause so it describes what the settled depth does per import (a
reorg deeper than it unseats that import's marker) and cites `WTC-9`'s own words for the latch, and
make the same correction in `ADR-0024`'s decision 1. Nothing normative moves.

Done when: the entry and `ADR-0024` decision 1 no longer state a latch condition `WTC-9` does not
state, the citation gate verifies whatever either quotes, and
`nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green (all nine, unpiped).

## Third site, found in the 2026-09-29 review (editable here)

`tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Exhibits.lean`, the marker-anchor section docstring:

"The reorg to `C` is no deeper than the settled depth, so it leaves `S = (2, 102)` active and
every completion marker in force."

The second clause is the same overbroad gloss. A reorg no deeper than the settled depth below one
import's scan anchor leaves *that* import's settled block active; a marker whose settled block sits
above the reorg's fork point is unseated. Chain `C` forks at height 5, so a marker anchored at a
settled block of height 5 or above — an import with scan anchor 15 or above — is not left in force.
True of the markers this trace holds, not of every marker.

Unlike the `CONTEXT.md` entry and `ADR-0024`'s decision 1, this line did **not** come from the
specification owner's verbatim patch: it was added by commit 8d69be3 during the 2026-09-29 rounds.
So it is editable without a spec-owner call, and can be fixed in the same change as the other two or
ahead of them.
close_reason: Scoped the gloss at four sites to what WTC-9 says: a reorg deeper than the settled depth can unseat that import's marker, and a repair latches only when no held marker's anchor is still active. CONTEXT.md Settled depth, ADR-0024 decision 1, ADR-0024's context paragraph on the scan-tip anchor (a fourth site the rounds missed), and the Exhibits.lean marker-anchor section, which now says the trace's wallet holds one marker. Nothing normative moved; all nine gates green.

title: WTC-7's covering claim is exhibited, not proved: state the universal over views that leave S active
description:
`WTC-7` claims of the amended birthday: "so the import covers every output a reorg that leaves S
active can make live". The formal model establishes two weaker things:

- `BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.settledBirthday_le` proves only the floor, `settledBirthday ≤ S.height`;
- `BtcPolicy.Exhibits.VaultUnspentCache.settled_covers_resurrection_with_current` is a single
  trace on one ledger and one reorg.

The covering claim itself is a universal and is not proved. The natural statement: for any view
`v'` agreeing with the scan view at every height at or below `S.height`, with `S` active on `v'`,
`unwatched L v' (settledBirthday L scanView S s) = []`.

Worth having for two reasons. It is the sentence `WTC-7` actually asserts, and an exhibit is not a
proof of a universal. And it would give `CNF-91`'s first clause — "The wallet birthday covers every
output a reorg that leaves the settled block active can make live" — a proof rather than an
instance.

Raised by the reviewer panel on `bps-8s0.11.13` as a suggestion beyond that bead's scope, which
required only that the amendment land green.

Scope: state and prove the universal in `VaultUnspent.lean`, with the instantiation over `current`
in `Exhibits.lean` per `ADR-0023` decision 6. No Markdown changes; `WTC-7` already says it.

Done when: the universal is proved (no `sorry`, no new axiom — `tools/check_formal.sh`'s axiom
policy holds), it is tagged `@[req "WTC-7"]`, and
`nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green (all nine, unpiped).

title: Watchtower.lean docstrings misstate what they cite: carry the signature check across tools/formal
description:
Five rounds of prose correction on `bps-8s0.11.13` each rewrote sentences that cite a Lean
declaration, and each rewrite introduced a fresh misstatement about the declaration it cited. The
final round's method — read every such sentence against its declaration's signature, hypothesis by
hypothesis — was applied to `VaultUnspent.lean` and `ADR-0024` and fixed them, but `Watchtower.lean`
was not covered. Three sentences there still misstate what they cite. All were verified against the
signatures, and none is caught by a gate: the citation gate checks quotations of requirements, not
claims about declarations.

## 1. `pass_tip_changed`'s docstring is wrong under one of the two guard values

`tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Watchtower.lean`, above `pass_tip_changed`:

"A scan whose captured tip's hash is no longer the active hash at that height, under either test."

The hypothesis is `tipChanged tt tip s.after = true`, and `tipChanged` branches on the guard:

    | .capturedHeight => !tip.active after
    | .chainTip       => after.tip.hash != tip.hash

Under `.capturedHeight` the docstring is right. Under `.chainTip` it is wrong: a block arriving on
top makes `after.tip.hash != tip.hash` true while the captured block is still active at its height,
which is precisely what `def14_discarded_with_chainTip` exhibits. Describe the selected test
returning true, not one value's reading of it.

Introduced by commit 8d69be3 (2026-09-29), which added the `TipTest` guard; the pre-amendment text
read only "A scan whose captured tip hash changed."

## 2. `tipChanged_capturedHeight_iff`'s docstring promotes a fact about the test into one about the pass

Same file, above `tipChanged_capturedHeight_iff`:

"Under `capturedHeight` the test is exactly `WTC-11`'s first site on the captured tip: the pass
discards its candidate iff the hash the chain now has at the captured height is not the captured
one."

The theorem has no hypotheses and concludes
`tipChanged .capturedHeight tip after = true ↔ after.activeAt tip.height ≠ some tip.hash`. It says
nothing about `pass`, and the iff is false of `pass`, which also discards when `belowNewest c tip`
holds or when `candidate` yields none. Scope the iff to the tip test.

Introduced by commit 8d69be3, with the theorem.

## 3. `pass_completed`'s docstring omits the hypothesis that decides its conclusion

Same file, above `pass_completed`. The signature carries five hypotheses — `hb`, `ht`, `hp`, `hr`,
`hl` — and the docstring carries four: `ht` as "whose tip test found no change", `hp` and `hr` as "a
proven scan of the cursor's range", `hl` folded into "the last scanned block". `hb : belowNewest c
tip = false` is missing, and it is what decides the conclusion, since `pass` is
`if belowNewest c tip || tipChanged tt tip s.after then c else …`: with `belowNewest` true the pass
returns the cursor unchanged and `next = last.height + 1` fails.

**Pre-existing**, unlike 1 and 2: the text at 54adc47 omitted `hb` too. Bounded by
`pass_below_tip_never_advances` sitting in the same section with its hypothesis named.

## 4. Two wording points from the same review

- `VaultUnspent.lean`'s marker-anchor section, and `ADR-0024`, say "no declaration runs `repair`
  under `scanTip`". `cleared_only_by_rebuild` takes `ma : MarkerAnchor` and so does state something
  about `repair .scanTip …` for every `ma`. The accurate claim is that no declaration *evaluates* it
  on that trace — "no exhibit runs `repair` at `.scanTip`" survives a reader who greps.
- `ADR-0024`'s "neither exhibited nor proved" sentence gives two reasons for one claim, where
  `VaultUnspent.lean` now pairs each claim with its own reason. The ADR could take the same shape.

## Scope

Prose only. Fix 1, 2 and 4; fix 3 or record it as pre-existing, whichever the owner prefers. Then
carry the signature check across the whole of `tools/formal/`, not one module: for every sentence
that says what a declaration proves, requires or asserts, read the full signature — every hypothesis
and every conjunct — and check the sentence clause by clause. Change no declaration.

Done when: the three sentences match their signatures; no two places in the repository disagree
about what a declaration requires; the report names, for every sentence checked, the declaration and
the hypotheses read; and `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green (all nine,
unpiped). No negative control should move — none of these sentences is a control comment.
close_reason: Covered by bps-8s0.11.18's sweep: pass_tip_changed, tipChanged_capturedHeight_iff and pass_completed now state their signatures (hb named), the section-4 wording points are fixed in VaultUnspent.lean and ADR-0024, and the signature check was carried across every module under tools/formal with each misstatement found corrected. No declaration's statement changed for this bead.

title: M8 catch-up: full-range delta walk, one cache slot, repair attempts start from a cold scan; trace format v2; review sweep (closes bps-8s0.11.17)
description:
Land the catch-up amendment decided 2026-09-30..10-01 in the Markdown AND the Lean model in one
commit, and sweep the 2026-09-30 code review's findings. The wording is SETTLED by the spec owner
after two consultation rounds (all four advisers answering both rounds; no safety
break found in either). No Consultation is needed. This also closes bps-8s0.11.17 (the
Watchtower docstrings), which the sweep in section 3 covers.

## 1. The Markdown: apply it verbatim

`git apply .context/catchup-markdown.patch` (git-ignored, in this checkout). It amends WTC-6 and
WTC-9 (10-watchtower-and-chain.md) and ADR-0024 (decision 8, the "full scan whenever more than 32
blocks behind" alternative, and Consequences). Do not reword it. If a Lean-side fact shows a
sentence false, stop and say so in the report instead of editing it. After applying, the citation
gate reports 9 Lean quotations that no longer match (VaultUnspent.lean 7, Exhibits.lean 2); every
one moves in this commit.

What the patch decides, in plain terms:
- WTC-6: a delta walk must cover EVERY height above the cache's anchor through the lesser of the
  tip captured when the walk starts and 32 blocks above the anchor. A walk that covers less is
  discarded whole, as is one failing any WTC-12 proof, and the refresh falls through to the cold
  scan. A walk that completes becomes THE cache (one slot) even below the tip; any later delta walk
  starts from it; WTC-5 refuses a cache whose anchor is not the current tip.
- WTC-9: a refresh that finds the latch set and NO repair attempt in progress starts one from a cold
  scan that replaces the cache before the re-import begins; while an attempt is in progress the
  cache is advanced by delta walks or their cold-scan fallback; while latched a wallet read never
  replaces the cache. This is the Rust reference's behaviour (`chain::refresh_vault_unspent_cache_mode`
  refuses the slot as a delta base when a repair is pending with no attempt running).
- The old WTC-9 cost clause ("one cold scan per repair attempt and not one per pass") is deleted:
  a discarded walk during a repair still costs a cold scan.

## 2. The Lean model (`tools/formal/BtcPolicy/`)

- ONE cache slot. Collapse `State.last` and `State.scanDerived` into a single cache; WTC-5's
  fire-time read, every source and every delta walk use it. Model "a repair attempt in progress" as
  you judge best (a flag, or each `repair` call being one attempt), but the following must be
  theorems, not prose: (a) a refresh with the latch set and no attempt in progress serves a cold
  scan, whatever the cache holds; (b) while latched, no wallet read replaces the cache; (c) a failed
  attempt does not leave delta walks running forever with the latch set: the next refresh with no
  attempt in progress starts a new one from a cold scan (the liveness gap round two found).
- FULL-RANGE WALK. `deltaFrom` (or `deltaWalk`) requires the walk's blocks to be exactly the heights
  anchor+1 .. min(tipAtWalkStart.height, anchor.height + deltaWindow); an empty walk is complete
  only when the anchor already is that tip; anything shorter is a failed walk that falls through to
  the cold scan. Define the tip captured when the walk starts as a specific view and say which.
  Note: requiring the anchor active on the served view does NOT close the empty-walk case, since
  every walk check holds vacuously on an empty block list.
- SERVED-CHAIN TIE. A committed walk's anchor must be active on the served view, not merely at or
  below its tip height.
- `Exhibits.delta_walk_empty_below_tip_committed` asserts the defect as current behaviour: invert it.
  Add exhibits for: a short walk falling through to the cold scan; the latched-no-attempt refresh
  cold-scanning; a latched walk advancing the one cache that fire-time reads.
- Keep the `DeltaCommit` guard (`partialWalk | tipOnly`) and the others; RE-MEASURE every CI
  negative control in gates.yml that the change touches (delta commit, import bracket, marker anchor,
  tip test, cursor shape), at exact counts, each run alone in a scratch copy.
- TRACE FORMAT: bump `Trace` format `version` from 1 to 2 (the byte layout changed in 8d69be3:
  LedgerRow.vaultSpends, the wallet's marker list, vaultRepair's atMarker and Scan) and re-render
  the published trace vector/digest through the gates that hold it; update any gate control that
  references the old hex.

## 3. The sweep (the review of 54adc47..HEAD; list at .context/code-review-54adc47.md)

Method, which converged last time: check EVERY sentence in tools/formal/, CONTEXT.md and ADR-0024
that cites a Lean declaration or quotes a requirement against that declaration's signature or that
requirement's current text; sweeping is the task, the list is a starting point, not a promise of
completeness. Items the review named: 5 (Chain.lean's stale "captured tip hash" quote and
Watchtower.lean's pass docstring), bps-8s0.11.17's three Watchtower.lean docstrings
(`pass_tip_changed`, `tipChanged_capturedHeight_iff`, `pass_completed`), 6 and 7 (ADR-0024 context
and decision 6 rationale), 8 (CONTEXT.md "Completion marker" must state all of WTC-8's conditions or
point at WTC-8 without claiming sufficiency), 10 (the module header's guard count), 11 (Chain.lean's
"wallet anchor"), 12 (factor the WTC-12 walk check into one helper used by Watchtower.proven,
deltaWalk and settledWalkProven, only if no theorem statement changes), 13 (register ADR-0024's
inline 10 and 32 in check_copies.py's owner registry, as ADR-0014's figures are).

## 4. Done when

All nine gates green, unpiped, alone in the checkout; every touched CI control measured at an exact
count; the citation gate verifies the re-quoted text; bps-8s0.11.17 closed with this bead. NO commit
message in the Run may carry a Co-Authored-By trailer or any tool attribution. Out of scope: SEC-50 (bps-8s0.11.14), the universal
coverage proof (bps-8s0.11.16), tracker records that name advisers (owner's decision: leave them).
close_reason: Landed in the working tree for one commit: WTC-6/WTC-9 and ADR-0024 amended verbatim from the settled patch; VaultUnspent.lean has one cache slot, an attempt flag, the full-range walk (coversRange/walkEnd) and the served-chain tie, with latched_no_attempt_serves_cold, latched_refresh_never_wallet_read and failed_attempt_restarts_from_cold_scan as theorems; Trace.version = 2 with the vector and digest re-rendered; delta-commit control re-measured 3 -> 2, the other flip controls unchanged, and the DEF-12 marker control corrected 3 -> 4 (stale at HEAD); review sweep items 5-8, 10-13 applied across tools/formal, CONTEXT.md and ADR-0024. All nine gates pass.

title: CNF-91 does not ask for the full-range delta walk or the latched-no-attempt cold scan
description: WTC-6 and WTC-9 were amended under bps-8s0.11.18: a delta walk must cover every height through the lesser of the tip captured when it starts and 32 blocks above its anchor, a shorter walk falling through to the cold scan; and a refresh that finds the latch set with no repair attempt in progress starts one from a cold scan. ADR-0024's Consequences records that CNF-89 and CNF-91 grew rows for the earlier amendment, but no conformance item demonstrates either new behaviour, so an implementation that commits a short or empty walk, or keeps delta-walking under the latch after a failed attempt, passes the checklist. Decide whether CNF-91 grows rows or a new item is appended, and add them. Done when: each behaviour has a conformance item, and the coverage gate is green.
close_reason: Delivered by bps-8s0.11.21: CNF-91 asks for the full-range walk, the latched-no-attempt cold scan and the attempt lifecycle

title: M8.2 watchtower cursor and scan proofs: WTC-11..14, shared backend-view vocabulary, CursorShape -> DEF-6
description:
Milestone 8 ticket 2 (ADR-0023 decision 10 item 8: "Reorg cursor and cache model (DEF-6, DEF-21)").
Planned 2026-09-24 by the maintainer after a three-adviser consultation; the
split, boundaries and guard are SETTLED, so no Consultation is needed.

WHAT TO BUILD. The watchtower cursor of WTC-13 and WTC-14 as a transition system, with the
scan proofs of WTC-12 and three of WTC-11's four detection sites. Owners, to quote in
docstrings: WTC-11 ("A node MUST detect a reorg at every point where it binds a result to a
chain"), WTC-12 (the three checks, "any failure discarding the whole result"), WTC-13 (anchors
"at most 101, contiguous", "reconciled", "walks newest to oldest for the highest still-active
anchor", "clears and re-scans from genesis rather than wedging or silently advancing"), WTC-14
(below-tip pass "MUST return without advancing", changed tip "MUST discard its candidate
cursor", errored pass "keeps the unadvanced cursor", panic "resets the cursor to genesis").

MODULES. Two modules for cursor and cache were decided (not one): the cursor's proofs need no
cache state, and the cache's need only active-at-height and snapshot facts. This ticket owns
the SHARED backend-view vocabulary, defined once: a block reference (height, hash), the
active-chain read `activeAt : Height -> Option Hash`, the captured tip, and previousblockhash
linkage. Put it where .11.3 can import it without importing the cursor's transitions (a small
`Chain.lean`, or a clearly separated section). Do NOT enlarge `Kernel.ChainView` ({mtp, seen},
an environment input) or `Coverage`'s `Pass.read` to share types; neither carries height ->
hash. Keep this cursor apart from `Cursor.lean`, which is SPN-38's RELEASE cursor (CONTEXT.md
has both terms).

GUARD PARAMETER. `CursorShape := anchored | bareHeight`, `current := anchored`. `bareHeight` is
DEF-6's twin: "The watchtower cursor was a bare monotonic height that never rewound, so a
recovery-path or unrecognised spend re-landing below it after a reorg was silently missed". The
twin trace: a spend confirmed at height h, a reorg that drops it and re-lands it below the
cursor, the anchored cursor rewinds and re-scans it, the bare cursor advances past it. Exhibits
over `current` go in `Exhibits.lean`; the CI negative control flips `current` and requires the
named theorem red. Do NOT claim this closes all of DEF-6: its prohibition also covers DUR-31's
re-broadcast and SPN-25's prevout verification, which stay out.

THEOREMS, universal over the shape where the statement allows: (1) anchors are at most 101 and
contiguous on every reachable cursor; (2) an in-window reorg is detected by the single hash read
at the newest anchor and the cursor rewinds to the highest still-active anchor, dropping
everything above; (3) a reorg deeper than the window resets to genesis; (4) WTC-14's four pass
outcomes, each as a theorem over the pass function; (5) WTC-12's three checks as NECESSITY
exhibits, not flips: for each check, a trace that passes the other two and would bind a result
to an abandoned fork -- the fork below the range that rebuilt taller, the mixed-fork straddle,
the scan that ran entirely on an abandoned fork and returned to the captured tip. Coinbase
inputs skipped; "a missing one is an error, never a silent negative" as a refusal, not a
default.

WTC-11's fourth site, "a wallet anchor no longer active", is .11.3's; say so in the docstring
and point at it rather than proving half of it here.

DONE WHEN. Gate green unpiped; the DEF-6 flip measured locally with its exact error count in
`gates.yml`; the five necessity exhibits and the twin trace present; no Markdown requirement
body changed; CONTEXT.md's two cursor entries still true.
close_reason: Landed as 02e6c55 and ef8b256; gates green unpiped (616 tagged declarations), DEF-6 flip red at 4 in Exhibits.lean only; four reviewers clean in Round 2

title: The full-range walk and the latched-no-attempt cold scan have no guard parameter, CI control or off-branch exhibit
description: AGENTS.md: 'Every semantic choice a dated amendment changed is a guard parameter with a current value', and green is evidence only because the workflow breaks something on every run. bps-8s0.11.18 added three rules to VaultUnspent.lean as unconditional definitions: the full-range walk (coversRange / walkEnd), the latched-no-attempt cold scan (deltaBase reading attempting), and the served-chain tie (c'.anchor.active v in deltaFrom). None has a withdrawn twin or a negative control in gates.yml; the DeltaCommit guard now distinguishes only the cache more than 32 blocks behind. Hand mutations during review turned the build red for each (1-2 errors), so the theorems do catch a regression, but CI does not prove it on every run. Also from the same review: (1) no exhibit shows a walk that links from the anchor and covers its range but ends on a block not active on the served view being refused (held only by deltaFrom_some's conjunct); (2) repair takes scanView as a free argument, so nothing proves the re-import uses the cold scan WTC-9 says the attempt starts from; (3) refresh never produces latched = false with attempting = true, but no theorem states it. Owner to decide which of these merit guard parameters and controls. Done when: each rule the owner keeps as a guard has its twin trace and a measured gates.yml control, and the off-branch exhibit exists.
