title: M8 attempt lifecycle and review fixes: WTC-6/WTC-9 latch wording, the walk's own tip, guard controls (delivers bps-8s0.11.20 and bps-8s0.11.19)
description:
Land the attempt-lifecycle wording decided 2026-10-01 together with the Lean model, and resolve
the 2026-10-01 code review of 3a74f89..cb14e72 (findings below). This also delivers
bps-8s0.11.20 (guard parameters and controls for the catch-up rules) and bps-8s0.11.19 (CNF-91),
which close with this bead. The wording is SETTLED by the spec owner after a four-adviser
consultation (all four answered); no Consultation is needed.

## 1. The Markdown: apply it verbatim

`git apply .context/latch-wording.patch` (git-ignored, in this checkout). Two additions:
- WTC-6 ends: "While the repair latch is set or a repair attempt is in progress, `WTC-9` restricts
  this order." (closes the review's finding that WTC-6's "MUST be served, in order of preference"
  had no latch exception).
- WTC-9 ends: "At most one repair attempt is in progress at a time. An attempt ends however it
  stops, whether or not its re-import began — a cold scan or wallet call that fails or overruns
  its `WTC-4` timeout ends it as a failure — and one that ends without rebuilding the wallet
  leaves the latch set, so the next refresh starts another." (closes the review's finding that
  WTC-9 said when an attempt starts but never when a failed one ends; the reference clears its
  in-progress flag on success, error, panic and spawn failure, and admits one attempt with an
  atomic compare-exchange).
Do not reword. If a Lean-side fact shows a sentence false, stop and say so in the report.

## 2. The Lean model (`tools/formal/BtcPolicy/VaultUnspent.lean` and its exhibits)

a. THE WALK'S TIP (review finding 1, the most important). WTC-6 says the walk covers "through the
   lesser of the tip captured when the walk starts and 32 blocks above that anchor". The model
   takes that tip from `serve`'s `v`, the view captured when the REFRESH starts, before the wallet
   read. If a block lands during the wallet read, the bracket discards the read, the node captures
   the new tip when the walk starts (as `chain::advance_confirmed_scan` does with `tip_height()`),
   and the model refuses that walk twice (`walkEnd` and the served-chain tie both use `v`) and
   cold-scans. Give the walk its own view captured when the walk starts; `coversRange`, `walkEnd`
   and the served-chain tie read it. Add an exhibit: a block arrives during the wallet read, the
   walk covers up to the new tip and is committed, no cold scan.
b. ATTEMPT LIFECYCLE per the new WTC-9 sentence: at most one attempt in progress; an attempt ends
   however it stops, including a cold scan or wallet call that fails or times out before the
   re-import; one that ends without rebuilding leaves the latch set and the next refresh starts
   another. `repair`'s "ends the attempt either way" now has a Markdown home; cite it. Model a
   failure before the re-import as ending the attempt.
c. `repair` takes `scanView`, `atDescriptors`, `atMarker` as free arguments (review finding 5,
   bps-8s0.11.20 item 2): tie the re-import to the cold scan that started the attempt.
d. Theorem (b) `latched_refresh_never_wallet_read` is proved by `rfl` and adds nothing over
   `latched_never_wallet` (review finding 8). Restate it so it has proof content and would go red
   if `refresh` stopped honouring the latch.
e. bps-8s0.11.20: guard parameters with `current` values, theorems over `current` in
   Exhibits.lean, and a measured gates.yml negative control each, for the rules the catch-up
   amendment (387505f) added as unconditional definitions: the full-range walk (`coversRange` /
   `walkEnd`), the latched-no-attempt cold scan, and the served-chain tie; an off-branch walk
   exhibit; and `attempting ⇒ latched` after a refresh stated as a theorem if it holds under the
   new WTC-6 pointer (an attempt can be in progress with the latch clear only on a first wallet
   build; say how the model treats that). AGENTS.md: "Every semantic choice a dated amendment
   changed is a guard parameter with a `current` value"; a value you can argue is not a dated
   semantic change may be dropped with the reason in the report.
f. Re-measure every gates.yml control the change touches, alone, in a scratch copy, at exact
   counts.

## 3. Records

- bps-8s0.11.19: CNF-91 (15-conformance-checklist.md) asks for the full-range walk, the
  latched-no-attempt cold scan and the attempt lifecycle, so an implementation lacking any of
  them fails the checklist.
- ADR-0024 decision 8 (review finding 6) still justifies committing below the tip by "A walk
  bounded at 32 blocks cannot always reach a tip that moved while it ran". Under the full-range
  rule the range is fixed by the tip captured when the walk starts, so the partial commit exists
  for a cache more than 32 blocks behind. Correct the rationale.
- ADR-0023 (review finding 7): the "Published exhibit, 2026-09-24: the trace format" section must
  record that the exhibit was re-published on 2026-10-01 as format version 2 (387505f), why (the
  wallet's marker list, LedgerRow.vaultSpends, vaultRepair's atMarker and Scan; then the single
  cache slot and attempt flag), and that a version-1 trace is now refused.
- bps-8s0.11.14 (review finding 9) quotes two sentences 387505f deleted ("a repair which keeps
  failing costs one cold scan per repair attempt and not one per pass"; "committing a walk that
  completes even where it ends below the tip and continuing on the next refresh"). Update its
  description with `br update --description-file` to cite the current WTC-6 and WTC-9 text.
- If you confirm that a wallet holding no marker (a first build that failed) satisfies WTC-9's
  latch condition vacuously and so retries a cold scan every refresh, where the reference
  deliberately does not latch an unseeded wallet, file it as a bead; do not change WTC-9 for it.

## 4. Done when

All nine gates green, unpiped, alone in the checkout; every touched CI control measured at an
exact count; bps-8s0.11.20 and bps-8s0.11.19 closed with this bead. NO commit message may carry a
Co-Authored-By trailer or a tool attribution. Out of scope: bps-8s0.11.16 (the universal coverage proof), bps-8s0.11.12.
close_reason: WTC-6/WTC-9 wording applied verbatim with the model, guards, controls and records; nine gates green and the six VaultUnspent controls pass at exact counts

title: A wallet holding no completion marker latches a repair vacuously and cold-scans every refresh; the reference does not latch an unseeded wallet
description:
`WTC-9` latches a repair on this condition: "If no completion marker the wallet holds has an anchor
on the active chain the node MUST latch a repair, keep the wallet out of use until a cold scan and
re-import have rebuilt it". A wallet that holds no completion marker at all — the wallet before its
first build, and the one a first build that failed leaves — satisfies that condition with nothing
to check. The formal model reads it that way: `BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.no_marker_latches` proves
`observe` latches every wallet whose marker list is empty, on every view.

With the attempt lifecycle `WTC-9` now carries, the consequence is a cold scan on every refresh.
`WTC-9`: "A refresh that finds the latch set and no repair attempt in progress starts one from a
cold scan that replaces the cache before the re-import begins (`WTC-6`)", and of an attempt that
fails, "one that ends without rebuilding the wallet leaves the latch set, so the next refresh
starts another." So on a backend where the wallet build cannot succeed — `WTC-3` lets a node run
with no usable wallet RPC: "The probe warns and does not refuse: a slow node is a live node" — every
refresh that finds no attempt in progress cold-scans, and the delta walk never becomes the source.
`BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.failure_before_reimport_restarts` and
`BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.failed_attempt_restarts_from_cold_scan` are that loop in the model. That is
the shape `DEF-9` records as a defect: "every restart and every periodic refresh repeated it."

The reference implementation deliberately does otherwise. `vault-node`,
`chain::refresh_vault_unspent_cache_mode` sets the repair latch only when the wallet handle carries
an anchor and that anchor is no longer active; a wallet it never had is seeded after the cold scan
without the latch, and when that seed fails the next pass finds a warm cache and a clear latch,
takes the delta walk, and does not retry the build until a later reorg or a restart. Its own
comment gives the reason: re-entering the cold-scan branch every pass would turn one transient
failure into a scan storm.

So the specification and the reference differ on an unseeded wallet, and the specification's
reading is the expensive one. Three ways to settle it, for the owner:

1. Keep `WTC-9` as worded and accept the cost: a node with no usable wallet cold-scans every
   refresh. Then `SEC-50`'s "every refresh pays it" is right as it stands and bps-8s0.11.14 closes
   with a citation fix only.
2. Scope the latch to a wallet that holds at least one marker, as the reference does, and say
   separately when an unseeded wallet's build is retried. Then `WTC-9`'s first sentence, `observe`
   in the model, and the first-build treatment in `BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.refresh` move together,
   and a first build becomes an attempt with the latch clear.
3. Keep the latch but bound the retry — a failed first build is not retried every refresh — which
   needs a rule `WTC-9` does not have today.

Not changed by bps-8s0.11.21, which landed the lifecycle wording as settled and recorded this
question. Related: bps-8s0.11.14 (`SEC-50`'s cost sentence), `ADR-0024` Consequences.

Done when: the owner has chosen; `WTC-9` (and `WTC-3` or `SEC-50` if they move) say which wallets
latch and when an unseeded wallet's build is retried; the Lean model and its exhibits agree; and
`nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green.
close_reason: Delivered by bps-8s0.11.25 in 325c7bc.

title: repair's scan tie pins the scan's tip and outputs, not the settled block rebuild reads from the scan view
description:
`BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.repair` ties the re-import to the cold scan its attempt started from by
comparing scan results: it rebuilds only when `coldScan L scanView` equals the scan the state
recorded (`State.repairScan`), which is the scan's outputs and its tip. `Chain.View` is a map from
heights to hashes with a tip, and nothing in the model makes a tip's hash fix the blocks beneath
it, so a `scanView` with the same tip and live outputs but a different block at the settled height
passes the tie, and `rebuild` then reads that view's settled block. A probe in review (2026-10-01,
Run 20261001T222811) had `refresh` record a scan on hashes `[100, 101]` and `repair` accept
`[200, 101]`, clear the latch and install a marker anchored at hash 200. `repair`'s docstring
states the limit ("the tie is as strong as the model's standing assumption that a block's hash
fixes the chain beneath it"); `rebuild_is_of_the_attempts_scan` proves equality of scan results
only. A real hash chain rules such a view out, so no conforming node is affected; the question is
whether the model should hold it.

Options for the owner: (1) accept the limit as stated; (2) have the state record what `rebuild`
reads from the scan view (the settled block, or the view as the trace's hash list) and drop or
bind `scanView`; this changes `State`'s encoding and so the trace format version. Done when: the
owner has chosen, and under (2) the mismatched-view case is an exhibit that is refused.
close_reason: Delivered by bps-8s0.11.25 in 325c7bc.

title: The served-chain tie on a delta walk's result has no sentence in WTC-6 and no conformance row
description:
`BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.ChainTie` (`tied` as current) refuses a delta walk whose resulting anchor
is not active on the view captured when the walk starts, even where the walk links from the cached
anchor and covers its range (`off_branch_walk_refused`). `WTC-6` has no sentence for that test: it
says "from a cached anchor whose block is still active" of the base, and "as is one that fails any
proof (`WTC-12`)" of the walk. The guard cites `WTC-11`'s "a block hash at a height that no longer
matches". ADR-0024 records that the reference implementation's `vault-node`,
`chain::advance_confirmed_scan` captures only a height when the walk starts and makes no such
test, and CNF-91 does not ask for it, so an implementation without the tie passes the checklist
while the model holds it as a rule.

Owner to decide: (1) the tie is `WTC-12`'s "the last is active after the loop" or `WTC-11`'s rule
applied to the walk's result, and the guard's citation and CNF-91 should say so; or (2) it needs
its own sentence in `WTC-6`; or (3) it is not required and the guard's current value is wrong.
Done when: the tie has a quoted Markdown home and a conformance row, or is withdrawn.
close_reason: Delivered by bps-8s0.11.25 in 325c7bc.

title: M8: unbuilt wallet not latched, retries only at cold scans already needed, served-chain tie dropped, ancestry premise on views (delivers bps-8s0.11.22, .23, .24)
description:
Land three spec-owner decisions of 2026-10-02 in the Markdown and the Lean model in one commit.
Each was put to a four-adviser consultation (all four answered) and then
decided by the owner; no Consultation is needed. Delivers bps-8s0.11.22, bps-8s0.11.23 and
bps-8s0.11.24, which close with this bead.

## 1. The Markdown: apply it verbatim

`git apply .context/unbuilt-wallet.patch` (git-ignored, in this checkout). It amends WTC-6 (its
pointer now reads "While the repair latch is set or a build or repair attempt is in progress"),
WTC-9 (rewritten lifecycle, below), WTC-11 (the wallet site: "a wallet that holds completion
markers none of whose anchors is still active") and CNF-91. Do not reword it; if a Lean-side fact
shows a sentence false, stop and say so in the report. The citation gate will report about 18
Lean quotations to move (VaultUnspent, Exhibits, Chain).

What WTC-9 now decides (bps-8s0.11.22):
- The latch applies only to a wallet that HOLDS a completion marker and none of whose markers is
  active. A wallet holding no marker (never built, or a first build that failed) is not latched;
  WTC-8 already keeps it out of use.
- STATE-BASED first scan: from the latch setting until a cold scan has replaced the cache, every
  refresh with no attempt in progress starts a repair attempt from a cold scan, whatever cache it
  holds. (A consultation found that "the first refresh after the latch sets" let a refresh after
  a failed first scan delta-walk from the pre-latch, possibly wallet-derived, cache.)
- Thereafter, while latched, the cache is advanced by delta walks or their cold-scan fallback, and
  a wallet read never replaces it.
- After a failed attempt, the next attempt starts ONLY from a cold scan WTC-6 itself reaches with
  none in progress, and starts no scan of its own. An unbuilt wallet's first build and its
  retries start the same way. Stated consequence: a failed build or repair is not retried while
  delta walks succeed; the cache does not depend on the wallet. (Owner's choice over a retained-
  scan retry and over reverting built wallets to retry every refresh.)

## 2. The Lean model

a. `observe` latches only a wallet with a non-empty marker list none of whose anchors is active;
   `no_marker_latches` inverts (an unbuilt wallet is not latched).
b. State records whether a cold scan has replaced the cache since the latch set (or equivalent).
   `refresh`: latched, no scan yet since the latch, no attempt in progress -> cold scan, start an
   attempt, whatever the cache; latched and scanned since -> delta walk with WTC-6's cold-scan
   fallback, and a fallback cold scan reached with no attempt in progress starts one; unlatched
   with no marker -> an attempt (first build) starts only from a cold scan WTC-6 reaches. A failed
   attempt starts no scan of its own.
c. Theorems: (i) a latched refresh before any post-latch scan cold-scans whatever the cache holds;
   (ii) after a failed attempt no refresh cold-scans unless WTC-6's own order reaches one (no
   storm); (iii) an unbuilt wallet never latches; (iv) an exhibit of the stated liveness
   consequence: a failed attempt followed by succeeding walks starts no new attempt.
d. Guard parameters, per AGENTS.md ("Every semantic choice a dated amendment changed is a guard
   parameter with a `current` value"), for: the latch's scope (`scoped` | `vacuous`) and the
   retry trigger (`neededScan` | `everyRefresh`), each with its twin trace, theorems over
   `current` in Exhibits.lean and a measured gates.yml control. Re-examine `LatchedBase`; merge or
   retire it if the new parameters subsume it, with the reason.
e. bps-8s0.11.24: `ChainTie`'s `current` becomes `untied`. All four advisers: WTC-12's "after the
   loop the hash at the last height still equals the last scanned hash" is the rule, compared with
   the chain after the walk, and the extra test against the view captured before the walk only
   discards a correct walk on a branch that reorged in just before it; WTC-5 already refuses any
   cache not at the current tip. Keep `tied` as the documented alternative with its exhibit;
   re-measure its CI control (the flip direction changes).
f. bps-8s0.11.23: in `Chain.lean`, beside `View`, a `Prop` on a pair (or an admissible family) of
   views: each view's tip is active in that view, and two views sharing an active block at height
   h agree at every height at or below h (a block hash commits to its ancestry). A HYPOTHESIS,
   never an axiom. `rebuild_is_of_the_attempts_scan` keeps its unconditional conclusion; add a
   corollary carrying the premise that proves the settled blocks of the recorded scan view and
   `scanView` are equal, so `rebuild` reads the attempt's settled block. `State`, `repair`,
   `rebuild` and the trace encoding do not change for this item. Keep the review probe (a scan on
   hashes [100, 101], a repair accepting [200, 101]) as an exhibit showing the premise excludes it.
g. If item b changes `State`'s encoding, bump the trace format version and record it in ADR-0023
   beside versions 2 and 3, with the reason.
h. Re-quote every broken quotation; re-measure every gates.yml control the change touches, alone,
   in a scratch copy, at exact counts.

## 3. Records

- ADR-0024: record the three decisions and their rejected alternatives briefly (a retained-scan
  retry; reverting built wallets to retry every refresh; recording the settled block in the
  attempt's state; keeping the served-chain tie as a new WTC-6 rule). Consequences: the reference
  does not latch an unseeded wallet (matches) but retries a failed latched repair on every pass
  (now diverges); the reference makes no served-chain tie (now matches).
- bps-8s0.11.14 (SEC-50): if its description quotes WTC-6 or WTC-9 text this patch changes,
  update it with `br update --description-file` to cite the current text.

## 4. Done when

All nine gates green, unpiped, alone in the checkout; every touched CI control measured at an
exact count; bps-8s0.11.22, .23 and .24 closed with this bead. NO commit message may carry a
Co-Authored-By trailer or a tool attribution. Out of scope: bps-8s0.11.16, bps-8s0.11.12.
close_reason: Delivered in 325c7bc. Nine gates green (Manager's own run, alone, unpiped, RC=0); gates.yml steps 37-42 pass at exact counts; four-reviewer Panel returned no findings.

title: M8: the first build has no scan-tie theorem, and latched-and-attempting-implies-scanned is not stated as an invariant
description:
From the review of bps-8s0.11.25 (commit 325c7bc). Two properties the model has by construction
but no theorem states, so a later edit could break either with every gate green.

1. The first build has no scan-tie theorem. `BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.rebuild_is_of_the_attempts_scan`
   and `rebuild_reads_the_attempts_settled_block` both take `st.latched = true`, so they cover a
   repair only. Since 325c7bc an unbuilt wallet's first build is an attempt that runs with the
   latch clear (`refresh` starts it at a served cold scan where `st.wallet.markers.isEmpty`), and
   `repair` holds it to its scan in code, but nothing proves it. Wanted: the sibling theorem keyed
   on `st.wallet.markers = []` and the wallet gaining a marker, with its corollary under
   `Chain.Ancestry`.

2. `failed_attempt_starts_no_scan` assumes `st.scanned = true`. Every latched attempt a refresh
   starts has it (`cold_scan_starts_attempt` sets it; `refresh`, `repair` and a latched
   `State.observe` keep it), but no theorem states `latched ∧ attempting → scanned` as an invariant
   preserved by `refresh`, `repair`, `endAsFailure` and `State.observe`. Wanted: the one-step
   preservation lemmas, so the "no scan storm" theorem's premise is discharged for every reachable
   state and the unreachable corner `latched ∧ ¬scanned ∧ attempting` (where `deltaBase` walks from
   the cache) is excluded rather than merely not produced.

No Markdown change; no guard parameter; no trace-format change. Done when both are proved, the
nine gates are green and any gates.yml control whose count moves is re-measured.
close_reason: Implemented in 3b272c5b3810628b9a1eb74f00f19a13023165a2; acceptance evidence, review dispositions and formal-scope boundaries are recorded in the closing comment.

comments.author: implementer
comments.text:
Implemented in 3b272c5b3810628b9a1eb74f00f19a13023165a2.

VaultUnspent.first_build_is_of_the_attempts_scan proves scan equality from an initially marker-free wallet, no running attempt, and marker gain after refresh then repair, for arbitrary Rules, MarkerAnchor and ImportBracket. The refresh and import walks are independent. first_build_reads_the_attempts_settled_block adds the explicit Chain.Ancestry premise; it does not claim an imported-marker anchor under arbitrary marker-anchor values.

title: M8: attempt invariant over every reachable state; a first-build ancestry instance that says something; the .vacuous observation counterexample
description:
From the two-axis review of bps-8s0.11.14–.26 (range 2e044d4..7e2a98e). bps-8s0.11.26 landed the
attempt invariant as a base and four one-step lemmas, and its own closing comment states the
boundary: "not a new trace-level reachability theorem". Its description asked for the one-step
lemmas so that

> the "no scan storm" theorem's premise is discharged for every reachable state and the
> unreachable corner `latched ∧ ¬scanned ∧ attempting` (where `deltaBase` walks from the cache) is
> excluded rather than merely not produced.

Three gaps, each a statement no gate can fail on today.

1. No reachability theorem. `BtcPolicy.VaultUnspent.attemptInvariant`'s docstring: "no
   trace-level reachability theorem is asserted here". The pieces exist:
   `attemptInvariant_of_no_attempt`, `attemptInvariant_refresh` (every `Rules`),
   `attemptInvariant_repair`, `attemptInvariant_endAsFailure`, and `attemptInvariant_observe`
   (scope `.scoped` only). Wanted: a reachability predicate over the states those operations
   produce from a no-attempt state, with observation under `.scoped`, and the theorem that every
   such state satisfies `attemptInvariant`. Then the corollary that discharges
   `failed_attempt_starts_no_scan`'s `st.scanned = true` for every reachable latched attempting
   state, so the corner is excluded by a theorem.

2. The first-build ancestry corollary has no instance whose conclusion says anything.
   `Exhibits.first_build_provenance_with_current` instantiates `first_build_is_of_the_attempts_scan`
   and `first_build_reads_the_attempts_settled_block` with `scanView = v = deltaView`, so its last
   two conjuncts are `x = x` and its `Ancestry deltaView deltaView` is reflexive. Its first three
   conjuncts (marker-free, no attempt, marker gained) do show the premises are satisfiable.
   Wanted: an instance in which the repair's scan view is not the refresh's view. If `View` admits
   no such pair that is not artificial, drop the two reflexive conjuncts and say in the docstring
   that the exhibit shows the premises are satisfiable, not the conclusion.

3. Nothing shows the `.scoped` restriction on observation preservation is needed.
   `attemptInvariant_observe`: "observation under `.vacuous` can latch a running first build".
   The latch-scope flip makes `Exhibits.attemptInvariant_observe_with_current` fail to prove, but
   no declaration exhibits the invariant breaking. `unbuilt_wallet_latches_with_vacuous` latches
   an unbuilt wallet that is not running. Wanted: beside it in `VaultUnspent.lean`, a running first
   build whose observation under `.vacuous` latches it, clears `scanned` and leaves it attempting,
   so `attemptInvariant` is false after the step. This follows the precedent of
   `mismatched_scan_view_excluded_by_ancestry` for the ancestry premise.

Scope: `VaultUnspent.lean` and `Exhibits.lean` only. No Markdown change, no new guard parameter,
no trace-format change. A theorem in `VaultUnspent.lean` names values (`.scoped`, `.vacuous`),
never `current`.

Done when: all three are landed (no `sorry`, no new axiom), each new declaration is tagged
`@[req "WTC-9"]`, `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green unpiped, and every
`.github/workflows/gates.yml` guard-flip control whose count moves is re-measured and updated.

title: M8.3 vault-unspent cache and wallet anchor: WTC-5..10, WTC-11's fourth site, ImportBracket -> DEF-21
description:
Milestone 8 ticket 3 (ADR-0023 decision 10 item 8: "Reorg cursor and cache model (DEF-6, DEF-21)").
Planned 2026-09-24 by the maintainer after a three-adviser consultation; the
split, boundaries and guard are SETTLED, so no Consultation is needed. Blocked on .11.2, whose
shared backend-view vocabulary (block reference, `activeAt`, captured tip) this module imports.

WHAT TO BUILD. The vault-unspent cache and the wallet anchor: WTC-5..WTC-10, plus WTC-11's
fourth detection site, "a wallet anchor no longer active". Owners, to quote in docstrings:
WTC-5 (the cache "of the confirmed outputs paying the vault" and its refusal), WTC-6 (the
serving order), WTC-7 (private keys disabled, blank, descriptor-based), WTC-8 (the completion
marker), WTC-9 ("If the wallet's completion anchor is no longer on the active chain the node
MUST latch"), WTC-10 (the sweep's read "MUST take one consistent snapshot"). Read each in
10-watchtower-and-chain.md before writing; the quotes above are fragments.

MODEL. A separate module from the cursor (decided): its proofs need only active-at-height and
stable-snapshot facts, never cursor transitions. State the cache as a function of a proven scan
(a .11.2 scan result) plus the wallet anchor; the completion-anchor latch of WTC-9 as a sticky
state; WTC-10's snapshot as one captured (tip, read) pair that the sweep consumes whole.
Connect the accepted snapshot to `Coverage`'s `Pass.read` (Coverage owns the denominator; this
module supplies what a pass reads) without enlarging Coverage's types.

GUARD PARAMETER. `ImportBracket := reProve | unbracketed`, `current := reProve`. `unbracketed`
is DEF-21's twin: "A reorg landing between the cold scan and the wallet import could import a
birthday proven on an abandoned fork, leaving an output permanently unwatched and inflating
apparent coverage", against the prohibition "the import MUST be bracketed by re-proving the
scan's own anchor (`WTC-7`)". Twin trace: cold scan on fork A, reorg to B between scan and
import, the bracketed import re-proves the anchor and refuses, the unbracketed one imports a
birthday B never had and one output is unwatched forever. DEF-9 is NOT an honest twin here (its
only difference is timing, which Silence.lean already excludes); do not add it.

THEOREMS: (1) WTC-5's refusal: an understated denominator is unreachable, i.e. every confirmed
output paying the vault on the proven chain is in the cache; (2) WTC-9's latch is sticky and
set exactly when the completion anchor leaves the active chain; (3) WTC-10: the sweep's read is
a single snapshot, so no interleaving of a chain advance between capture and use changes the
value the sweep sees; (4) the DEF-21 twin theorem over `current`, with the flipped refutation.

DONE WHEN. Gate green unpiped; the DEF-21 flip measured locally with its exact error count in
`gates.yml`; no Markdown requirement body changed; the CONTEXT.md entries for Coverage and
Vault unspent (if present) still true.
close_reason: Landed as 503da85 and ca4f964; gates green at 685 tagged declarations; DEF-21 flip red at 3 in Exhibits.lean only; four reviewers clean in Round 2. Residue in bps-8s0.11.8.

title: M8.4 watchtower recognition and alert queue: WTC-17..22, Recognition guard (ADR-0001 -> ADR-0012), Silence WTC-20 debt
description:
Milestone 8 ticket 4 (ADR-0023 decision 10 item 8). Planned 2026-09-24 by the maintainer after
a three-adviser consultation; the split and the guard are SETTLED, so no
Consultation is needed. Blocked on .11.2: WTC-21 takes the alert lock "only after the scan has
been proven (`WTC-12`)", so the queue's transitions consume a proven scan.

WHAT TO BUILD. Watchtower recognition and the alert queue: WTC-17..WTC-22. The watchtower is a
DUTY of every node, not a deployment (ADR-0001, "Vault nodes are the watchtower"; CONTEXT.md's
entry). Owners, to quote in docstrings: WTC-17 (scan "every 10 seconds, first pass immediate";
the precedence: empty branch selector is a `RECOVERY_PATH_SPEND` "even if the txid is in the
authorized set", otherwise not in the vault-authorized set is an `UNRECOGNIZED_SPEND`,
"otherwise no alert"; "The recovery exit is never swallowed"), WTC-18 (recognition "by
validation and acceptance, never by co-signing and never by evaluation"; the two refutations;
the authorized set as "the txids of every spend, Escape, rung, refresh and claw-back this node
accepted (`SPN-33`)"), WTC-19 (witness not script; fewer than two elements "reads as
non-recovery"), WTC-20 (RAM-only, "capped at 1 024 events with the oldest evicted first,
sequence-numbered from 1"; dedup on `spend_txid:outpoint`; "an evicted entry's key is released
so a later scan may re-alert it"), WTC-21 (snapshot the authorized set and release the lock
BEFORE the slow chain read), WTC-22 ("Watchtower duty continues during Lockdown").

GUARD PARAMETER. `Recognition := validated | coSigned | evaluated`, `current := validated`.
This is a dated semantic change (ADR-0001 revised by ADR-0012), so AGENTS.md requires the
parameter. Two twins, both from WTC-18's own sentences: `coSigned` -- "Only `t` of `n` nodes
sign a legitimate spend, so 'I did not sign it' false-alarms on `n − t` honest nodes" -- the
exhibit is a legitimate spend that alerts on n − t nodes under coSigned and nowhere under
validated; `evaluated` -- "a spend a node REFUSED was evaluated, so 'I evaluated it' would let an
attacker fanning a theft to honest nodes suppress its own alert" -- the exhibit is a theft fanned
to every honest node, refused by all, alerting everywhere under validated and nowhere under
evaluated. The CI control flips `current` to each and requires the named theorems red.

QUEUE MODEL. A RAM-only bounded sequence with a dedup key set: theorems that the length never
exceeds 1 024, that the sequence number is strictly increasing from 1, that a re-scan of a
retained spend enqueues nothing, that eviction releases the key so the same spend can re-alert,
and that WTC-17's precedence is total (every spend classifies to exactly one of three outcomes).
Alert shape: `kind`, `spend_txid`, `outpoint` as `txid:vout`, `script` as lowercase hex.

SILENCE DEBT. `Silence.lean`'s docstring says the kernel emits no alert, "so there is nothing here
to project (`API-18`, `WTC-20` are milestone 8's)". Pay it: either extend `Obs` with the queue's
observable (count and shape) and re-prove the coupling, or state in both docstrings, with the
argument, why the queue adds no observable divergence between the two PINs. WTC-22's "duty
continues during Lockdown" is a theorem over the lockdown state, not prose.

LOCK ORDER. WTC-21 as an ordering theorem over the pass: authorized-set snapshot, release, chain
read, WTC-12 proof, then alert lock; STO-9's lock order is the owner of the general rule -- cite
it, do not restate it.

DONE WHEN. Gate green unpiped; both Recognition flips measured locally with exact error counts
in `gates.yml`; the Silence debt paid one way or the other with the docstrings agreeing; no
Markdown requirement body changed. Package ancestry and replacement (WTC-23..25) are .11.5's,
not this ticket's.
close_reason: Landed as a8a87da: Alerts.lean (recognition guard, WTC-17 classification, WTC-20 queue, WTC-21 duty and lock order, WTC-22 lockdown theorem), Exhibits.lean WatchtowerAlerts section, two Recognition controls in gates.yml, Silence debt paid by route (b). Four reviewers PASS, no findings; residue filed as bps-8s0.11.9.

title: M8.6 language-neutral trace format: alphabet record, round trip, decided synthetic trace, negative exhibits; adapter lives in btc-policy-lean
description:
Milestone 8 ticket 6 (ADR-0023 decision 10 item 8: "implementation trace adapters — the boundary
at which btc-policy-lean's runtime evidence meets the model"). Planned 2026-09-24 by the
maintainer after a three-adviser consultation; SETTLED, no Consultation
needed. Blocked on .11.2..11.5 because the format names every event they define. NOT blocked
on bps-8s0.7: the FORMAT is a specification this repository owns; the replay ADAPTER is
implementation and lives in btc-policy-lean, whose first commit depends on this repository's
formal layer, so the block runs the other way.

WHAT THIS IS. The language-neutral trace format that btc-policy-lean and any other
implementation replay against the model. AGENTS.md: "Nothing that implements the specified
system belongs here" and ADR-0023: "No implementation, verifier or shadow node ever lives
here". So: no runner, no CLI, no collector, no adapter, no schema file. The repository already
owns encoders (WIR-18..27, `Encode.lean`); this is one more codec plus fixtures.

THE SMALLEST CHECKABLE SPECIFICATION (unanimous): (1) the event alphabet as a versioned Lean
record -- the union of the events the milestone 8 modules and the kernel step on, each with its
explicit mapping to a model input or effect; (2) `decode ∘ encode = id` and a length theorem in
the `Encode.lean` pattern; (3) at least one published synthetic trace whose replay verdict
(final state and effects) is `decide`-proved, in the `check_vectors.py` pattern so the digest of
the published preimage is recomputed by the vector gate; (4) rejected malformed traces as
negative exhibits (wrong version, unknown event, truncated entry). No guard parameter: ADR-0023
says a codec round trip "needs no twin".

SECRETS. STO-11: the listed secrets "MUST never appear in a ... trace ... or replay entry"; hold
it BY CONSTRUCTION -- the record has no field that can carry a PIN, preimage, key, KDF output
or request body. STO-12: no synthetic identifier may be a derivative that lets memory capture
"cheaply test the plaintext PIN". The project rule "synthetic traces only" is stronger than
STO-11 requires; state it as the project's rule, not as STO-11's.

CONFORMANCE. Rows for the adapter's obligations go to 15-conformance-checklist.md (the
implementation records its own status per OVR-17); AGENTS.md: "Never put a `CNF` identifier in
`tools/formal/`".

DONE WHEN. Gate green unpiped, including the vector gate recomputing the trace digest; the
round trip and the decided verdict present; the negative exhibits present; no Markdown
requirement body changed; the conformance rows added.
close_reason: Landed in b5748aa and bd3a517: Trace.lean (alphabet, codec, round trip, replay, decided published trace, negative exhibits), traceVector region in ADR-0023, CNF-147/CNF-148, two gate controls; nine gates green on bd3a517

title: M8.2 review residue: WTC-14 clause precedence and tip-hash reading for the spec owner; spend and anchorless-cursor notes for .11.3/.11.4
description:
Residue from the bps-8s0.11.2 reviews (Rounds 1 and 2: four reviewers), verified on
ef8b256. None is a defect in what landed; each is a note for the ticket named, or a spec-owner
question, so it is filed rather than lost.

1. WTC-14 clause precedence has its home only in a Lean docstring. 10-watchtower-and-chain.md
   states the below-tip clause and the panic clause side by side; Watchtower.lean's `pass`
   resolves a panic below the newest anchor as a reset to genesis (a panic can happen anywhere
   in a pass, the tip comparison included), and its docstring says so. A reimplementer working
   from the Markdown alone could order the two either way. Spec owner's call: a clause in
   WTC-14 ("a panic anywhere in the pass, the tip comparison included"), or nothing.

2. WTC-14's "captured tip hash changes" is read literally: `pass` discards a scan whose
   after-view tip hash differs from the captured one, so an ordinary extension during the scan
   discards the pass (retried next pass; WTC-14 says the redundant re-scan is harmless). A
   reviewer read it as "the block at the captured height changed" and asked for an
   extension-accepting exhibit; rejected as the weaker rule the text does not state. Worth the
   spec owner confirming the reference implementation compares the tip hash, not the height.

3. For bps-8s0.11.4 (recognition and the alert queue), where spends stop being opaque:
   - an empty proven scan still binds its spends: `result .anchored genesis { blocks := [],
     spends := [7], … } = some (genesis, [7])`;
   - nothing asserts the DEF-6 trace binds its spend; `result current genesis def6Scan` yields
     `some [1]` by #eval, and one conjunct on `def6_rescanned_with_current` would carry it (the
     DEF-6 flip count in gates.yml stays 4 if added there);
   - `headerAccepted` and `Anchor.active` share one body; kept as WTC-11's two named sites.

4. For bps-8s0.11.3 (cache and wallet anchor): under `anchored`, an anchorless cursor with a
   non-zero next height reconciles to genesis (`next := 0`). Unreachable from genesis, so no
   theorem depends on it; pin `anchors = [] → next = 0` in `wellFormed` if the cache's proofs
   ever need it.

Done: whichever of 1 and 2 the spec owner takes is a Markdown edit with its own citation and
gate run; 3 and 4 are folded into their tickets or closed as not needed.
close_reason: Spec owner decided 2026-09-27: item 1, WTC-14 states a panic anywhere in the pass, the tip comparison included, resets to genesis; item 2, the tip check compares the active hash at the captured tip height (the reference's reading, panel unanimous). Items 3-4 were folded into bps-8s0.11.11 (closed). The Markdown and the model land together in bps-8s0.11.13.

title: M8.3 review residue: modelling choices for the spec owner (one marker, no birthday without outputs, walk-to-tip reading); docstring and delta-exhibit notes for VaultUnspent.lean
description:
Residue from the bps-8s0.11.3 reviews (Rounds 1 and 2: four reviewers), verified on
ca4f964. None is a defect in what landed; each is a note for a later edit of VaultUnspent.lean,
or a modelling choice worth the spec owner's eye, so it is filed rather than lost.

1. Modelling choices the Implementer flagged, accepted by every reviewer, worth the spec owner
   confirming against the reference implementation:
   - the Wallet record holds one completion marker, the one the last import left; WTC-8's "at
     least one marker whose anchor is still active" is that marker's anchor;
   - a vault with no confirmed output has no birthday, so `rebuild` imports nothing (WTC-7 names
     no birthday for that case);
   - block time is modelled by height; WTC-7's birthday is used only as an order;
   - WTC-7's "blank" and "descriptor-based" are creation-time duties the record does not carry
     (route (a) of the Round 2 brief; the alternative was reading them in `usable`).

2. WTC-6's delta walk is read as a walk from the cached anchor to the tip: `deltaFrom` accepts
   the walk's result only when anchored at the served view's tip, else falls through to the cold
   scan (Round 2 item 1). The Markdown says "a bounded delta walk of at most 32 blocks from a
   cached anchor whose block is still active" and does not say "to the tip" in words; the spec
   owner may want those words in WTC-6, as with WTC-14's clause precedence (bps-8s0.11.7 item 1).

3. Docstring and exhibit notes for the next edit of VaultUnspent.lean (reviewer B, Round 2):
   - `deltaFrom`'s docstring says the walk "reads the scan and the ledger only"; it also reads
     the cache it walks from. "takes no view" is the fact being argued.
   - `deltaFrom`'s bound `v.tip.height ≤ c.anchor.height + deltaWindow` is now entailed by the
     tip equality plus `rangeFrom` and `length ≤ deltaWindow`; a half-sentence saying so would
     stop a reader deleting the wrong one as duplication.
   - No exhibit in Exhibits.lean's VaultUnspentCache section walks a delta: the Round 1 regression
     (`chainOf [100, 101, 102]`, base at (0, 100), empty scan → cold scan now) and a walk stopping
     one short live only in the reviewers' probes. `served_at_tip` guards the rule universally;
     a concrete exhibit would make it legible.

4. bps-8s0.11.7 item 4 (pin `anchors = [] → next = 0` in Watchtower.wellFormed if the cache's

title: F65: candidate possession — Cand.heldSigners, the shape everything else reads
description:
Land the possession field the rest of F65's open half reads. No behaviour change:
nothing consumes it yet.

WHAT TO BUILD.

    structure Cand where
      ...
      heldSigners : List Nat     -- DUR-28's "distinct valid partials", as this node holds them

`born` overwrites it with `[n.id]`: SPN-36 says a candidate is "born fully signed and fully
withheld" and SPN-32 that "The node MUST sign the spend, the Escape and every rung at
ingress", so this node's own signer is a member from registration. Do NOT add a separate
`ownSigned` bit -- `node.id` distinguishes self, and `born` always signs.

An idempotent insert helper, mirroring `addSender` but WITHOUT its self-refusal: NCH-25 says
"The store holds at most one partial per (rung, input, signer). A duplicate is an idempotent
ACCEPTED and never displaces the first", and self is a member here rather than excluded.

SHAPE, decided unanimously by a three-reader panel (.context/f65d-*). A bare `List Nat` of
signers, NOT `List (input, signer)` and NOT `List Exp`. This kernel collapses the input and
rung dimensions already -- `finalizable` filters `e.input == 0`, `firePass` emits
`queuePartial (sighash c.tx 0) 0`, and `Exp`'s docstring says "Input 0 stands for every
input" -- so a pair whose left component is permanently zero mimes DUR-28's "on every input"
rather than modelling it, and costs a pair's DecidableEq inside `decide +kernel`. `Exp` is
refused because `cid` and `hot` are diagnostic exposure metadata and CONTEXT.md says exposed
authority "outlives everything node-local", so hanging it on a prunable Cand fights the term.
State the deferred input and rung dimensions in one docstring sentence, as `Exp` already does
for one of them.

Read the field with `.eraseDups.length` wherever it is counted, so the count is total over
arbitrary Lean values rather than resting on a reachable-state invariant. This is deliberately
the OPPOSITE of the `relaySenders` decision in d0245f7/2e0c190, and the difference is why:
`holderCount` uses bare `length`, so it needed `relaySenders_nodup`; nothing counts increments
here.

`pubCand` MUST preserve `heldSigners` exactly -- a `pubCand_held` lemma plus a set congruence.
It is pin-uniform state; erasing it makes `packageAccepted_pub` unprovable later, because the
two runs' counts must be equal. `inv_frame` needs NO new component: `NodeInv` reads only
sweepActive, armed, frozen, hot, fireAt, windowClose and `hotBoundAt`'s fields, none of them
possession. (Verified against Silence.lean at 2e0c190.)

ALSO IN THIS TICKET. Rename `Exhibits.finalizableNodeLocal` to `releasedResidentQuorum`. It is
decision 9's retained WRONG model -- "the count a node-local history pruned with the candidate
would give" -- and leaving that name beside a real possession predicate puts two incompatible
notions of node-local finalizability in one file.

DONE WHEN. `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, the field exists and is
preserved by the projection, and no predicate reads it yet.
close_reason: Landed in db9983e. Two additions past the ticket's letter, both in its direction: addHeld_of_held, so the NCH-25 tag names a declaration a theorem exercises, and a docstring on Exhibits.cand recording that a directly seeded registry (twinNode, soloNode) holds no possession, which bps-8s0.14's exhibits must route around. The field, born's seed, addHeld, pubCand_held, pubCand_set_held and the releasedResidentQuorum rename are as specified; nothing reads the field yet.

title: F65: split finalizability — exposedQuorum (POL-18) beside heldQuorum (DUR-28)
description:
Split finalizability in two and give each half the requirement it actually renders. No
behaviour change: `packageAccepted` still reads the world-level predicate at the end of this
ticket.

WHAT TO BUILD.

Rename `Kernel.finalizable` to `exposedQuorum` and retag it `@[req "POL-18"]`. POL-18 is the
sentence it renders: "A partial that has left the node is finalizable authority in `t - 1`
compromised hands". It was tagged `@[req "DUR-28"]`, which is a misattribution -- DUR-28 is
"Finalization takes the highest rung at or below the latch with >= t distinct valid partials
on every input", a statement about what a node finalizes FROM. DUR-28 does not lose a Lean
home: `Cursor.finalized`, `Cursor.finalized_reaches`, `Cursor.split_finalizes_lower_latch` and
`Exhibits.dur30_split_finalizes_lower_latch` all carry it.

Add `heldQuorum (t : Nat) (c : Cand) : Bool`, tagged `@[req "DUR-28"]`, reading
`c.heldSigners.eraseDups.length`. Name chosen to pair with `exposedQuorum` and to avoid
implying the package, authorization and exact-vsize checks have passed -- DUR-28 requires
those separately.

Callers of the renamed predicate are wider than they look: `Exhibits.exposure_key_exhibit`,
`no_resident_release_does_not_mean_safe`, `HotLedger.def5_refused_with_current`,
`def5_admitted_with_withdrawn`, the F63 exposure exhibit, and `Ledger.lean`'s docstrings all
mean the world-level one and must say `exposedQuorum`.

Note in `exposedQuorum`'s docstring that after bps-f65-cutover no transition reads it -- it
becomes exhibit-only, retained as decision 9's trap. Without that sentence a later cleanup
deletes it and takes `exposure_key_exhibit` with it.

MARKDOWN WITH THE DECLARATION, per AGENTS.md. Add the `Held partial` glossary entry's
counterpart wherever DUR-28's local basis needs stating, citing SPN-36's "the partials
received per (input, signer)" and NCH-25's store rule. Do not restate the rule in a second
document.

DONE WHEN. Gate green, both predicates exist, `packageAccepted` unchanged.

Landed in 3012b1a. exposedQuorum renders POL-18, heldQuorum renders DUR-28, packageAccepted's decision is unchanged, all nine gates green at 493 tagged declarations.

One addition past the ticket's caller list, in its direction: Silence.finalizableOf and finalizable_eq become exposedQuorumOf and exposedQuorum_eq. They are the erased twin of the same predicate and carried the same 'DUR-28's count, read off the world' misattribution, so bps-8s0.15 inherits one vocabulary rather than two.

title: F65: authenticated partial receipt — receivePartial, exposure and possession separated
description:
Give the model an authenticated inbound partial. Until this exists `adversaryExposes` is the
only way another signer's partial enters the world, which is why the model cannot tell
exposure from delivery. No behaviour change to assembly: `packageAccepted` still reads
`exposedQuorum` at the end of this ticket.

WHAT TO BUILD.

    | receivePartial (msg : Sighash) (input : Nat) (signer : Nat) (cid : Nat)

Deliberately `adversaryExposes`'s exact four arguments, so the trace migration in
bps-f65-cutover is a token swap rather than a rewrite.

The step does TWO things, and they must NOT be fused into one guarded match:

  1. Append the `(msg, input, signer)` row to `World.exposure`, UNCONDITIONALLY. A partial
     that reached this node has left its signer whatever this node then does with it. NCH-24
     answers `UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE` for a pruned candidate -- fuse the two and the model claims
     a partial this node dropped never left its signer, which weakens the premise
     `exposure_key_exhibit` is retained to trap.
  2. Insert the signer into `heldSigners` ONLY on candidate lookup, guarded by
     `msg == sighash c.tx 0`.

BOUNDARY HYPOTHESIS, named in the docstring, not modelled. NCH-24 requires, in order, wallet
equality, signer equals sender, sighash type, the candidate exists, it is not expired, the
rung is found by txid, the user-signature hash matches, "the input and signer are in range",
and that "the signature verifies against this node's own recomputed sighash for that rung and
input and the signer's descriptor key (CHN-11); then store it". This event is the successful
post-validation store. Authenticated is NOT storable, and an event that merely carried a
signer id could otherwise manufacture possession. NCH-24's "except the delayed-slot exemption
of SPN-41" stays out of scope exactly as `Kernel.prune` already declares for the Escape
exemption.

SILENCE. `Input.pinless`, one common event in both runs, no branch on `armed`, duress or the
selected bits. `Obs` does not widen -- but the event must not simply fall through `respond`'s
`| _ => .silent` catch-all: NCH-25 makes a duplicate an idempotent `ACCEPTED`, so either reuse
`.ack` (already documented as "DUR-6's idempotent no-op, and a relay counted") or define the
event as an internal post-response transition and say which in the docstring.

BLAST RADIUS. Exhaustive `Event` matches in Kernel (inv_step, armed_sticky, D_immutable,
terminal_sticky, exposure_monotone, sweepActive_sticky, selected_grows,
T_written_only_by_arm_or_accept, relaySenders_nodup_step), `Ledger.afterEvent` and
`liveSum_afterEvent_le`, and SILENCE's step/invariant/work/marker proofs.

EXHIBITS. Receipt admits a peer and raises the held count; a duplicate receive asserts
UNCHANGED heldSigners -- not an unchanged `World`, because the exposure row may legitimately
append again; exposure without receipt still reaches `exposedQuorum` and not `heldQuorum`.

DONE WHEN. Gate green, the event exists, assembly unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented in 147f2bd953c5ed003a08c88f74ae9b11d68397df. Event.receivePartial preserves adversaryExposes's argument order; the world appends exposed authority unconditionally while the NCH-24-tagged store inserts through addHeld only on matching candidate id and recomputed sighash. Complete upstream validation is a named boundary hypothesis. SILENCE uses an explicit silent internal post-response arm and preserves the common pinless input and existing theorem statements. Receipt, exact duplicate-held-list identity, exposure-without-possession, pruned-candidate and mismatched-message exhibits pass. Assembly still uses exposedQuorum; existing peer traces, alphabet and exposure_key_exhibit are unchanged. F65 remains open for the cutover. Ran nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh unpiped before and after implementation: exit 0, every gate PASS; final formal index 499 tagged declarations, zero constants outside policy, fresh-kernel replay accepted every declaration.

title: F65: cutover — packageAccepted reads possession, with the bridge theorem
description:
Switch assembly onto node-local possession. This is the behavioural cutover and it lands as
one commit: the predicate swap, the release conjunct, the proof repairs and the trace
migration cannot be green apart.

WHAT TO BUILD.

`packageAccepted` reads `c.released && heldQuorum w.node.t c` in place of `exposedQuorum w c`
(the conjunct bps-8s0.13 left it reading).

THE `released` CONJUNCT IS A MODELLING ORDER, NOT A RULE READ OFF THE SET. Say so in the
docstring. SPN-39 puts finalization on the fire pass -- "On every fire pass, for each due
candidate, the node MUST ... finalize" -- but SPN-38 permits a pass that releases nothing:
"If `affordable_rungs = 0`, release nothing and advance no release bookkeeping on this pass."
`released` is therefore a valid proxy for "a pass processed this candidate" only inside this
kernel's no-quota abstraction, where `firePass` releases every due candidate. Word it as "this
node released the rung being assembled": `Cand` carries no ladder and the kernel finalizes at
`sighash c.tx 0`, so `released` IS `released_through` at rung 0, and the sentence upgrades to
`released_through >= rung` when DUR-28's latch enters the kernel. The durable shape is a
fire-pass assembly token carrying the selected rung; it is the
recorded upgrade path and is NOT built here, because an `Option Rung` field in a kernel with
no rungs is a boolean in disguise.

THE BRIDGE, as a theorem and not an exhibit: over reachable resident candidates,
`released && heldQuorum ==> exposedQuorum`. It needs `born`'s sanitization and the receive's
unconditional exposure append. It is FALSE for hand-built `World` values, so state it over
`Reachable`. Preserve the counterexample to unconditional inclusion -- own withheld possession
plus received peer authority -- since the two predicates remain incomparable in general.

SETTLED 2026-09-23, so no Consultation is needed: the bridge is FALSE over `Reachable` as the
kernel stands. `Kernel.receivePartial` takes no input; `step` for `.receivePartial m i s cid`
drops `i`, stores the signer whenever `c.id == cid && m == sighash c.tx 0`, and appends an
exposure row carrying `input := i`, while `exposedQuorum` counts only rows with
`e.input == 0`. So `.receivePartial (sighash tx1 0) 7 1 1` after acceptance gives
`heldQuorum` and, after `firePass`, `released`, with `exposedQuorum` false. The fix is
option (A), reached independently by the Manager of run 20260923T031645 and its adviser:
`Kernel.receivePartial` takes the input and the store guard becomes
`c.id == cid && input == 0 && msg == sighash c.tx 0`; the exposure append stays
unconditional. A partial on an unmodelled input is exposed authority but not modelled
possession, which is `Exp`'s "input 0 stands for every input" applied to the store and
`NCH-24`'s "the input and signer are in range" at the only modelled input. Say so in the
guard's docstring. Do NOT take the alternative of dropping the `e.input == 0` filter from
`exposedQuorum`, `exposedQuorumOf` and `finalizableByCommitment`: it re-keys exposed
authority against `ADR-0023` decision 9's `(message, input, signer)` in four places. The
input-7 receipt is itself the "exposed but not held" half of the DONE WHEN exhibit.
`Silence.receivePartial_pub` gains the input argument and one conjunct; the call in the
Silence step case passes `j`. Existing receipt exhibits all pass input 0 and are unchanged.

Proof sketch: two invariants carried over `Reachable` -- every held signer other than self
has an input-0 exposure row on `sighash c.tx 0`, and `released` implies self's input-0 row
exists -- plus a nodup-subset-length lemma (no Mathlib here; prove `addHeld_nodup` beside
`addSender_nodup`).

ENUMERATION, DECIDED: the optional `safeStep` conjunct cannot fail from `wReady`, which
already holds quorum once its peer step is `receivePartial`, so take the docstring option.
The DUR-29 negative control in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` requires the reauthorization
flip to yield exactly two errors, both in `Exhibits.lean`, on `race_refused_with_current` and
`bounded_from_ready`; the migrated traces must keep that count. `def5`, `twoRequestsTrace`
and `partialExposedOnly` keep `adversaryExposes`: their peers are compromised or undelivered
by design. The "compromised signer 2" comments on `raceTrace` and `wReady` go with the swap.

SILENCE. Repair `packageAccepted_pub`. `Silence.exposedQuorumOf` exists only to strip the
`World` from the old predicate; once `packageAccepted` reads `heldQuorum`, which already takes
`(t, Cand)`, delete it or narrow it to whatever the exposure theorems still need.

TRACE MIGRATION. `normalTrace`, `raceTrace`, `wReady` and both `adr0014` legs swap their
synthetic `adversaryExposes` peer step for `receivePartial`. In the bounded `alphabet`,
REPLACE the `adversaryExposes` symbol rather than adding an eleventh -- `traces_count :
(traces 3).length = 1000` is a theorem and 11^3 = 1331 turns it red.

AND BE HONEST ABOUT THE ENUMERATION. `safeStep` checks only "no hot queuePartial, no
broadcast, every hot candidate frozen" -- none of which possession can affect -- so
`bounded_from_ready` will stay true and blind through the new code. Either give `safeStep` a
conjunct that the new gate can fail (no broadcast below `t` held), or state plainly in the
docstring that it is not evidence for this gate. Do not let the word count stand in for
coverage.

The comment "`adversaryExposes` is the only way a partial from another signer enters the
world" is already gone; what remains in `Exhibits.lean` is the trace docstring saying the
trace "still uses `adversaryExposes`" for an honest peer. After the migration that sentence
is false too, so rewrite it, and grep both `Kernel.lean` (its module docstring and the
`Event` docstring) and `Silence.lean` for any remaining sentence that describes
`adversaryExposes` as the peer-partial path.

DONE WHEN. Gate green, and a new exhibit separates the predicates: a node with exposed
authority it never received cannot assemble, and one that received can.
close_reason: Landed as 8a74bbe: packageAccepted reads released && heldQuorum, receivePartial guards input 0, bridge theorem released_held_exposed over Reachable, traces migrated to receivePartial, four separating exhibits. Gate green (all 9) on 8a74bbe; DUR-29 negative control exactly 2 errors. Four reviewers reported no findings against the commit; reviewer B's one finding, two stale F65 sentences, is carried into bps-8s0.16. The judge of run 20260923T033345 produced no ruling (its session ended waiting on a backgrounded gate), so closed on that evidence.

title: Citation gate does not read Lean docstrings: quoted attributions under tools/formal/ are unguarded
description:
`tools/check_citations.py` reads `*.md` and `docs/adr/*.md` only (its `glob` calls); it never
opens `tools/formal/`. A Lean docstring that quotes a requirement — `Delivery.lean` alone carries
28 quoted attributions to `OPR-48`..`OPR-51`, `OPR-65`, `OPR-68`, `API-16`, `DEF-8` and `F56` —
is held to its owner's words by review alone, and a requirement edited later drifts from the
docstring without any gate going red. AGENTS.md's rule ("A claim about what another requirement
says carries that requirement's own words") applies to docstrings as it does to prose.

Found by the bps-8s0.11.1 review (the brief wrongly said the gate checks docstrings). Options:
extend the QUOTED rule of `check_citations.py` to `tools/formal/**/*.lean` docstrings (`/-- … -/`
and `/-! … -/`), with the same owner resolution and a negative control in `gates.yml`; or record
in AGENTS.md that Lean docstring quotes are review-checked only. The first keeps the rule one
rule; the second is honest about the gap. Decide, then land with its control.
close_reason: Landed in abf7e18: the QUOTED rule and the UNQUOTED ratchet read /-- -/ and /-! -/ docstrings under tools/formal/, three multi-attribution sentences split (Kernel.lean, Silence.lean), three unquoted attributions reworded to summary verbs (POL-20 and CHN-4 'gives', POL-4 'requires'; 'gives' is deliberate, both figures are held by check_copies.py), baseline at zero, negative control in gates.yml asserting exit 1 and the diagnostic, README row. Follow-ups: bps-8s0.18 (nested block comment fails open), bps-8s0.19 (colon-form attributions unverified: the gate checks 3 of Delivery.lean's quoted attributions, not 28).

title: check_citations.py: Lean docstring extractor fails open on a nested block comment; fail closed
description:
`tools/check_citations.py` extracts Lean docstrings with `DOCSTRING = /-[-!](.*?)-/` over raw
source (landed in abf7e18, bps-8s0.17). Two inputs Lean accepts defeat it, both verified by the

1. A docstring nesting a block comment — `/-! Intro /- remark -/ … `OVR-1` says "false quote". -/`
   — is truncated at the inner `-/`, so a false attribution after it is silently missed: exit 0.
2. A `--` line comment carrying a whole `/-- `OVR-1` says "…". -/` pair is read as a docstring:
   exit 1 on text the gate says it does not read.

Neither shape exists in the tree today (917 docstring openers, 917 extracted, zero `/- -/` block
comments under `tools/formal/`, per reviewers A and B), and the code comment at
`DOCSTRING` says so. Case 1 is the one that matters: a silent miss in a gate whose purpose is to
not be silent. The smallest honest fix is fail-closed, not a lexer: refuse (exit 1, naming the
file) any extracted docstring body that contains `/-`, so a nested block comment inside a
docstring turns the gate red until someone extends the extractor. Case 2 can stay: a false quote
in a line comment being refused is harmless. Add a regression probe for case 1 beside the
"Prove the citation gate can fail on a Lean docstring" step in `.github/workflows/gates.yml`, or
in `tools/check_gate_controls.py`, asserting exit 1 and the diagnostic.
close_reason: Landed in b4b910b: load() reports docstrings nesting /- (closer reconstructed), main() refuses with exit 1 naming file:line; workflow control asserts exit 1 and the diagnostic; README row and module docstring state the contract. Gate green, 33/19 unchanged. Panel: reviewers B, C, D no findings; A incomplete.

title: Citation gate: colon-form attributions (`ID`: "…") are unverified in Markdown and Lean; 135 of 341 Lean quoted spans
description:
The citation gate's QUOTED rule binds a quote to an attribution verb (`says`, `states`, `reads`)
or a possessive noun (`X`'s rule that …). A colon-form attribution — `` `OPR-49`: "The state
starts …" `` — has no verb, so the grammar never sees it, in Markdown or in Lean; the gate's
module docstring says so since abf7e18. The exposure measured by the bps-8s0.17 review (reviewer B),
current tree:

- Markdown: 174 quoted spans of 4+ words, 16 colon-form, 14 checked sentences.
- Lean docstrings: 341 quoted spans, 135 colon-form, 19 checked sentences.

So `bps-8s0.17`'s "Delivery.lean carries 28 quoted attributions" resolves to 3 checked by the
landed gate; the colon form is the dominant shape there. Covering it — a third `ATTRIB` shape,
`` `ID`: "…" `` with the quote directly after the colon, same owner resolution — closes most of
what remains unguarded, and needs its own negative control. Keep the STO-43/STO-14 rule: the
owner is the id the colon attaches to, not the nearest citation. Nested straight quotes inside a
quotation (`Delivery.lean`'s module docstring, the `OPR-49` quote) will surface once colon-form
is checked; curly inner quotes or an ellipsis split resolve them. Related: nothing ratchets the
count of checked quoted attributions, so a `says` → `gives` edit drops a sentence out of coverage
with every gate green; a "may grow, never shrink" signature list like `citation-baseline.json`
would hold it, if the count line proves insufficient.
close_reason: Landed in 7d99a62: ATTRIB gains the colon form; each quote belongs to the last attribution starting before it (finditer, Consultation: advisers A and C both chose nearest-preceding); the UNQUOTED rule runs per attribution with the colon form exempt (a short or split quote is skipped, baseline stays at zero); the 7 predicted drifts fixed as docstring text in Cursor, Kernel, Ledger, Silence; workflow control appends a two-attribution colon-form probe and asserts DOM-1 blamed and OVR-1 not; README row; clean line now 141 attributions, 120 in Lean. Residue filed as the follow-up bead (nested straight quotes in Delivery.lean's OPR-49 quote, attribution-shaped phrases inside quotes, POL-18 HISTORICAL false positive).

title: Citation gate: nested straight quotes in Delivery.lean's OPR-49 quote go unchecked; attribution-shaped phrases inside quotes; HISTORICAL false positive on POL-18
description:
Residue from the bps-8s0.19 review (reviewer B), all verified on 7d99a62; none introduced by that
commit, all pre-existing limits of `QUOTE` pairing and `HISTORICAL` that the colon form now makes
visible. Small, docstring and comment work; one guard optional.

1. `Delivery.lean` module docstring, the `OPR-49` quote (line ~7): nested straight quotes.
   `QUOTE` pairs them alternately, so `"The state starts "` (3 words) and `", advances to "`
   (2 words) are dropped by the 4-word filter and only the tail `" on EVERY attempt … never moves
   backward."` is checked; the inner phrases `definitely not sent` and `possibly delivered, exact
   bytes` are checked by nothing. Verified: replacing both with false phrases leaves the gate at
   exit 0 with the count line unchanged. The bead bps-8s0.19 named this exact spot. Fix as
   `Cursor.lean`'s `DUR-30` was fixed in 7d99a62: curly inner quotes (`norm()` folds them), so the
   whole quotation is one checked span.
2. State the limit in `check_citations.py`'s module docstring next to the short-quote and
   split-boundary limits: a quotation with nested or unpaired straight quotes is cut into
   alternating spans, and the short ones go unchecked (the `QUOTE` comment already says "paired
   quotes only"). Also two prose imprecisions there: "never to the chunk's first" should read
   "never to the chunk's first merely because it is first"; and UNQUOTED is "no quote of its own,
   after it and before the next attribution", which is what `m.start() < p < end` implements.
3. An attribution-shaped phrase inside a quoted span becomes a spurious attribution: `finditer`
   sees `` `DOM-1` states `` inside a quotation as an attribution with an empty span, so it lands in
   UNQUOTED and the gate goes red on correct prose. Nothing in the tree trips it today (0 ATTRIB
   matches fall inside a quoted span), but 16 requirement bodies carry such a phrase (`OVR-8`,
   `DUR-34`, `SEC-33`, `OPS-7` carry `` `POL-20` states: ``; `MAN-2` carries `` `OPS-1` states ``;
   `SPN-43` carries `` `SPN-19` states ``), so it is one docstring quotation away. Either skip an
   ATTRIB match whose `start()` falls inside a `QUOTE` span (a few lines), or declare it in the
   limits passage; if guarded, a negative-or-positive control is not required, but the docstring
   must say which.
4. `Ledger.lean` ~line 420, the `POL-18` colon form is silently exempted: the requirement's own
   quoted words contain "the original", which `HISTORICAL` matches, so the whole chunk is skipped.
   `HISTORICAL` was out of scope for bps-8s0.19; decide whether to tighten that alternation
   (e.g. require it outside quoted spans) or record it as the third undeclared reason a colon form
   goes unchecked.

Done: gates green unpiped; `citation-baseline.json` at zero; docstring text only in Lean; no
Markdown requirement body changed.

title: Citation gate: the in-quote guard silences an attribution after an unpaired straight quote; the nested-quote limit understates the miss; nothing detects a new nested straight quote
description:
Residue from the bps-8s0.21 and bps-8s0.22 reviews (reviewers A, B), verified on e96ef32 and
21e8141. All three items were SETTLED 2026-09-23 by the maintainer after a three-adviser
consultation (two rounds), so no Consultation is needed: build what is
written here. Reference design: /home/master/p/provisiond/tools/check_citations.py, the origin
of this gate, whose rule is positional -- a quote "belongs to whatever introduced it", i.e. the
attribution it follows -- and whose unpaired-quote failure is loud, never silent.

ITEM 1, SETTLED: the in-quote guard becomes OWNERSHIP-BASED. Today `find()` drops an `ATTRIB`
match that starts inside ANY raw `QUOTE` span; since `QUOTE` pairs straight quotes
alternately, a stray unpaired straight quote earlier in a chunk opens a bogus span that
swallows a real attribution, silently. Probe chunk:
    Field is 6" wide and `OVR-1` says "this phrase OVR-1 does not contain at all".
On 0beca6c `find()` reported OVR-1 UNQUOTED; on e96ef32 and HEAD `bad`, `unquoted` and
`checked` are all empty. Build: suppress an attribution `m` only when some quote span (s, e)
has `s < m.start() < e` AND an earlier attribution `a` exists with `a.end() <= s` and `a`
itself outside every span (so a quoted pseudo-attribution never becomes an owner). That is
bps-8s0.19's "each quote belongs to the attribution it follows" applied to suppression, and
provisiond's rule generalised to many attributions per chunk. The MAN-2/OPS-1 positive control
stays suppressed (MAN-2 precedes its quotation). All three advisers scanned HEAD's 155
attribution-bearing chunks under this predicate: ZERO chunks change classification; the only
two odd-count chunks (Delivery.lean OPR-49, Kernel.lean NCH-25) are colon-form quotes SPLIT cut
at a sentence end and are unaffected. Control: a `gates.yml` step appends the probe to a scratch
Lean docstring and asserts exit 1 plus `reports what OVR-1 says without quoting it` (the
baseline is at zero, so the signature is new). Docstring: the sentence "Nor is an
attribution-shaped phrase inside a quoted span, which is being quoted, not made" becomes
"inside a span an earlier attribution introduced"; "A quote before the first attribution
belongs to no one" is already true of quote assignment and stays.

ITEM 2, SETTLED: the nested-quote limit understates the miss. The passage says the quotation
is "cut into alternating spans, and the spans under four words go unchecked"; for the
canonical case the unchecked text is the nested quotation itself, which falls BETWEEN spans
(on 0beca6c's OPR-49 line the raw spans were 3, 2 and 21 words and `definitely not sent` lay in
none of them; the verified words drop 33 -> 21, not 26 -> 21). Rewrite the sentence so it says
the nested quotations themselves, falling between spans, are checked by nothing -- subject to
item 3, which detects the common case.

ITEM 3, SETTLED: BOTH a detector and a declared limit. Detector (reviewer B's rule, matching not
counting): in `find()`, when a checked attribution owns two or more RAW `QUOTE` spans, take the
text from the first span's opening quote to the last span's closing quote (outer to outer,
interior quote characters left in place; `norm()` folds curly to straight) and test it against
the same `pool`. A match proves the spans are one quotation that nests straight quotes, cut by
`QUOTE`: FAIL with "quotation after `ID` is cut by nested straight quotes; write the inner
quotes curly". No match: today's per-span check, untouched. Reviewer B ran it: 0 hits on the clean
tree; straightening OPR-49's inner quotes fires once in Delivery.lean, and DUR-30's once in
Cursor.lean, with the count line unchanged at 142/121 either way (the miss this detects). A
false positive needs the owner's body to contain the writer's straight-quoted text verbatim,
which is nesting. Do NOT build the rejected forms: a checked-words ratchet (offset by
lengthening another quote; re-baselined on every legitimate shortening), a gap heuristic that
merges spans within N words (at N=5 fuses CHN-35, OPR-51, DUR-11 and reds a clean tree), or a
no-punctuation-gap report (fires on six to nine legitimate coordinated quotations, e.g.
DUR-11's `"..." and that "..."`, CHN-35's three phrases). Declared limit, kept beside the
detector: a nested quote whose outer-to-outer text does NOT match the body is still checked by
nothing; the remedy remains curly inner quotes. Control: a `gates.yml` step that straightens
OPR-49's inner quotes in a scratch copy and asserts exit 1 with the new message. Update the
`Exit 0 = ...` line for the new cause. With this, e96ef32's subject "reads a nested quotation
whole" becomes true.

Optional, same commit: the positive control's `grep -Eq 'reports what OPS-1 says|attributes
to'` is broad; `Delivery.lean attributes to` anchors it, and a `grep -q 'attributes to MAN-2'`
branch names "the probe's quote drifted from MAN-2's body" when MAN-2 is next edited. The
comment above the nested-comment control lost the clause "and the quote after it is never
read"; half a line restores it ("the false quote after each nested comment is what the refusal
keeps unread"). The `grep -q` on the `FAIL: 2` count fails silently under `set -e`; the
colon-form control's if/cat/::error::/exit 1 form would name the dropped arm.

Done: gates green unpiped; three new or tightened controls each shown red against the detector
from HEAD~ and green on the commit; `citation-baseline.json` at zero; no Markdown requirement
body changed; no Lean declaration changed (docstring text only if a quote needs curly marks).
notes: Residue from the bps-8s0.22 review (reviewer B), on 21e8141, same gates.yml neighbourhood as this bead's optional item: the comment above the nested-comment control lost the old clause "and the quote after it is never read". The false OVR-1 quote each probe carries asserts nothing (with the detector removed the gate is exit 0, 142 verified, because the regex ends the docstring at the inner -/), so nothing local now says why the quotes are there. Half a line restores it, e.g. "the false quote after each nested comment is what the refusal keeps unread". Optional in the same commit: the new grep -q on the FAIL: 2 count fails silently under set -e; the colon-form control's if/cat/::error::/exit 1 form would name the dropped arm.

title: Inherit: a pair's duress bit is the OR of every arm intent naming it, and any holder decision arms with it (withdraws per-Carrier)
description:
**Decided 2026-10-02 by the spec owner, after a four-reader panel: inherit.** A pair has one
duress bit, the OR of the duress bits of every arm intent naming its spend commitment. Any holder
decision on that pair arms with that bit: overlay `arm`, `sweep_active`, the `selected_escapes`
insertion and the freeze. Per-Carrier is the withdrawn reading. `DUR-10` already applies the same
OR to the Escape entry: "the entry's duress bit becomes the OR of its old value and the new
intent's, so a normal-PIN replay can never clear a duress authorization".

**Why.** `DUR-4` keys intent "by the Carrier identity", and `NCH-31` makes the identity commit to
the plaintext PIN, so two requests for one pair are two Carriers. Under per-Carrier, whichever
reaches `t` first decides.

On the current kernel, from `Exhibits.ReleaseKernel.w0`, this trace releases the coerced hot
partial on an unarmed node:
1. `accept 10 true … c1 e1`;
2. `accept 11 false … c1 e1`;
3. `receipt 11 1`;
4. `firePass`.

The release does not need the normal PIN. `SPN-5`'s gate table stages a `BAD_PIN` refusal at gate
14 (row 14: `consumed`, `yes`, `yes`), and `DUR-4`'s intent holds "its two commitment ids". If a
wrong-PIN Carrier names a resident pair, its holder decision opens it. That breaks `SEC-24`'s
"flooding wrong PINs produces denial and never an unfrozen quorum". The set does not say whether
a gate-12 intent has its commitment ids before the PSBTs decode at gate 17. Inherit closes the
path either way: a node holding the duress intent arms, and a node without it has no pair a
refused request registered.

Freezing without arming was rejected. It makes the node freeze while unarmed and inside the
horizon, which `DUR-1` forbids. Three readers built that rule independently, and `Silence.silence`
failed on `NodeInv.unfrozen`. Two readers independently built inherit:
- `check-all.sh` passes, `Silence.silence` proves, and no exhibit goes red;
- the trace above arms the node, freezes the hot candidate, and releases only the Escape partial
  past the horizon;
- the combined patch with `bps-8s0.29`'s fix also passes.

**Wanted.** Land inherit as a `Kernel.Rules` guard parameter, with per-Carrier as the withdrawn
value. The trace above goes in `Exhibits.lean` as its twin, with a flip step in
`.github/workflows/gates.yml` and its error count measured. Text changes:
- `DUR-5`: "write the overlay with `arm = intent.duress`" becomes the pair's duress bit, and
  "add the pair's Escape to `selected_escapes` with the intent's duress bit (`DUR-10`)" becomes
  "with the pair's duress bit".
- `SPN-23`: "re-applies its schedule and intent, and re-stages" becomes "re-applies its schedule,
  records its own intent (`DUR-4`), and re-stages". Add the converse of its duress-resubmission
  sentence: a resubmission whose pair a duress intent names arms at its own holder decision.
- `SPN-37`: "opened only by its own Carrier's holder decision (`DUR-5`)" becomes "opened only by
  the holder decision of a Carrier naming it (`DUR-5`)". Make the matching change to `DUR-8`'s
  "waits for its own Carrier's holder decision".
- `CNF-29`: add the converse case.
- `ADR-0023` decision 10 item 4: dated amendment of "arming is a receipt reaching `t` on a
  Carrier whose intent bit is set".
- `CONTEXT.md`, written after the rule lands:
  - *Release gate*: "opens only on the candidate's own holder decision" becomes "opens only on
    the holder decision of a Carrier naming the candidate's pair".
  - A new *Pair duress bit* entry.
  - *Arm intent*: notes that two Carriers over one pair carry separate intents, and the pair acts
    on their OR.

**`T`'s start (decided).** `DUR-13`'s `first_seen` is the earliest `first_seen` among every arm
intent naming the pair, under both PINs. A later copy must not stretch the hostage window, which
`DUR-13` forbids: "so that slow or selective delivery cannot stretch the hostage window". Taking
the earliest of the duress intents only would make `T` depend on the PIN. Amend `DUR-13`'s "from
the intent's `first_seen`" to match. In `Kernel.newDeadline`, the minimum is read over the
Carriers naming `k.spend`.

**Sticky, on the nonce tombstone (decided).** Inherit's bit must outlive an intent that retires
uncommitted.

On correct clocks, an intent's `D` can lapse before the pair's `E`. `NCH-33` samples `M` "before
authentication", so a wait for the lock shortens `D`. A normal copy accepted while A is resident

window in which a copy of the pair can still be admitted (`SPN-10`: "`expiry > effective_now`").

- leaves `SPN-32`'s "an already resident compatible pair is left exactly as is" intact;
- keeps `NCH-34`, because the tombstone confers no holder authority.
