title: POL-4's beyond-max theorem has premises the documented derive cannot meet, and POL-4's skip rule has no model
description:
`BtcPolicy.Membership.not_matches_beyond_max` is the formal home of the upper end of `POL-4`'s
"derive indices `0..=max` if it has a wildcard", which `CNF-15` tests as "not at `max + 1`". Both
of its premises range over every `SinglePath`, not over `d.paths`:

- `hdistinct : ∀ p q, p ≠ q → ∀ i j, derive p i ≠ derive q j` fails for every `derive` that reads
  only `id`. `SinglePath`'s docstring calls `id` "its identity (keys, origin, script context —
  everything `derive` reads)", so two paths that differ only in `wildcard` derive the same scripts.
- `hinj : ∀ p i j, derive p i = derive p j → i = j` fails for every `derive` that is constant in
  the index on a definite path. `POL-4` says "A definite descriptor ignores `max`".

The two premises can both hold, but only for a `derive` that also reads `wildcard` and puts
distinct scripts at definite-path indices no scan reads. So the theorem is not vacuous in the
abstract; it is vacuous under the module's own description of `derive`. Its premise `_hp` is
unused, and no exhibit instantiates it.

Second, `POL-4` says "An index the library cannot derive is skipped", but
`derive : SinglePath → Nat → Script` is total, so a failed derivation has to be some script. An
empty-script sentinel matches an empty output script. The module docstring's "The structure
covered is the whole of what `POL-4` requires beyond that boundary" is therefore not yet true.

Wanted:
- `derive : SinglePath → Nat → Option Script`, where a failed derivation contributes no match.
- `matchesScript derive max d s = true ↔ ∃ p ∈ d.paths, ∃ i ∈ indices max p, derive p i = some s`.
- The bound stated as locality, with no premise and over the bound itself: two `derive`s that agree
  on every `p ∈ d.paths` and every `i ≤ max` give the same `matchesScript`.
  - Do not state it over `i ∈ indices max p`. That form still proves when the wildcard range is
    `List.range (max + 2)`, so it does not pin the bound.
- `not_matches_beyond_max` kept as `CNF-15`'s formal home, restated for a wildcard path only:
  `p ∈ d.paths` with `p.wildcard = true`. Its premises are that `derive p (max + 1)` differs from
  every `derive q i` with `q ∈ d.paths` and `i ∈ indices max q`. That is local to `d`, and a
  `derive` constant in the index on definite paths meets it. Add an exhibit that instantiates it.
  - The wildcard condition is required, not optional. On a definite path, a `derive` that ignores
    the index has `derive p (max + 1) = derive p 0`, which the scan reads, so the old conclusion is
    false there. `CNF-15`'s "not at `max + 1`" is about wildcard scans in any case.
- An exhibit that a `derive` returning `none` everywhere matches nothing.
- `kindOf` and `member_discharged` carried over, unchanged in meaning.

Evidence: reviewers A, B, C and D of the 2026-10-02 reading, each with scratch builds. The
off-by-one mutation and both locality forms were compiled. The exhibits above land those probes in
the repository.

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- in a scratch copy, changing the wildcard range in `indices` to `List.range (max + 2)` turns a
  `POL-4`-tagged theorem red;
- every `POL-4`-tagged theorem that has a premise has an exhibit instantiating it.

title: CHN-11's sighash has no BIP143 instance, but the Kernel docstring and ADR-0023 item 4 say milestone 5 supplied one
description:
`CHN-11`'s sighash has no instance, and two records say it does. The `Kernel` module docstring
and `ADR-0023` decision 10 item 4 both say "milestone 5 supplies the BIP143 encoder as its
instance". Milestone 5 (`bps-8s0.5`) never listed a BIP143 encoder and closed without one: its
six tickets are `Encode`, the `CHN-24` edit, `CoordRequest`, `Manifest`, `Witness` and the
packaging test. The sentence entered with milestone 4.

Item 4 also calls the sighash "a structure whose field is a function of the transaction and the
input index". In the code, `BtcPolicy.Kernel.sighash` is a plain `def` over
`abbrev Sighash := Nat × Nat`, so there is nowhere for an instance to plug in.

Because the declaration carries `@[req "CHN-11"]`, the requirement index lists `CHN-11` against
`sighash` alone. What `sighash` actually formalizes is one property of `CHN-11`: the message is a
function of the transaction and the input, "and of no request field". It does not formalize
`CHN-11`'s "BIP143 P2WSH sighash computed with `SIGHASH_ALL` … with the input's `witness_utxo`
value".

The defect is in the accepted ADR's record of what milestone 5 delivered and what the boundary is.
Correcting the code comment alone would be cosmetic.

Wanted:
- `ADR-0023` decision 10 item 4 and the `Kernel` docstring name the BIP143 instance as an open
  boundary, not a milestone-5 deliverable.
- Item 4 describes the sighash as it is: a fixed symbolic definition, not a pluggable structure.
- `sighash`'s docstring says which part of `CHN-11` it formalizes and which part is the boundary.

Building a BIP143 framing encoder is a separate `ADR-0023` decision and out of scope here.
`Encode`'s docstring already records why framing stops at the digest: "(decision 3, and the bead:
no SHA-256 in Lean)". Framing alone would prove a field layout and nothing about binding.

Done when `tools/check-all.sh` is green and neither record claims an instance or a structure the
formal layer lacks.

title: Kernel accept re-registers a resident pair: a fresh-nonce resubmission revives a claw-back-defeated hot spend
description:
**Decided 2026-10-03 by the spec owner, after a four-reader panel, which agreed unanimously.**
Registration is indivisible. A resident candidate under either requested id is compatible only if
it is resident **as this pair**: in the role the request gives it, with the request's other id
recorded as its sibling (`SPN-36`), over the same `tx`, `hot` and `expiry`. Anything else is a
conflicting resident commitment, `PSBT_INCONSISTENT` / `candidate_identity`, and the refusal leaves
every resident candidate untouched: exactly one id resident; both resident but in two different
pairs (`(S1,E2)` with `(S1,E1)` and `(S2,E2)` resident); the swapped request `(E1,S1)`; a
resident claw-back (`SPN-51`, no sibling) under either id; and `sp.id = es.id`.
- The prototypes' `pairAdmits` (both-or-neither plus per-id fields) MUST NOT land as written: it
  admits the cross and swapped requests and opens `c1` under them.
- Kernel: the role and sibling live on `Cand`, stamped by `register`. An equal-expiry premise on
  `accept` alone refuses neither the cross nor the swapped case; it is the extra premise for an
  invariant that every resident member's sibling is resident with the same expiry.
- A gate-29 refusal still stages (`SPN-5` row 29); its holder decision follows `bps-8s0.34`.
- **The ladder (decided the same day, after a second four-reader panel, unanimous).** Compatibility
  also requires the resident Escape to hold the request's rung txids in the same order, the empty
  list included. A different ladder over the same spend and base Escape is a conflicting resident
  commitment. Compare txids, never PSBT bytes (`SPN-23` sends changed bytes of the same
  transaction to fresh evaluation, and those stay compatible), and never held partials, the rung
  latch, the release floor or `released_through`, which can differ by PIN (`DUR-1`). This is
  `SPN-32` and `CNF-34` text only: `Cand` models no ladder, and no Lean change is wanted for it.
  An honest repeat carries the same ladder (`CHN-17` is a function of the base) and is a gate-19
  replay; a different ladder needs only a coordinator stripping rungs (`SEC-21`).
- **`SPN-29`.** A registration refusal unwinds only the velocity reservation this request placed;
  a reservation an earlier acceptance of the same commitment placed stays (`POL-18`).
- The cross-node ladder split is a different requirement, filed separately; not part of this bead.

Evidence: `.context/vault-review-1002/round5-pair/` and `round6-ladder/` (briefs, answers, patches, exhibits).

`BtcPolicy.Kernel.accept` re-registers a resident pair, so a fresh-nonce resubmission revives a hot
spend that a claw-back has defeated.

`SPN-32` owns the rule: "an already resident compatible pair is left exactly as is" and "a
conflicting resident commitment is `PSBT_INCONSISTENT` / `candidate_identity`". `SPN-23`'s replay
"re-stages", and staging belongs to the Carrier: per `SPN-32`, the node "stages the Carrier — pushes
the request to the outbox and counts itself as a holder".

Beside its lockdown guard, `accept` checks resident Carrier ids but not resident candidate ids. On a resubmission it prepends fresh `born` copies with `terminal := false` and
`released := false`.

Trace on the current kernel, from `Exhibits.ReleaseKernel.w0`:
1. `accept 10 false … c1 e1`;
2. `settle claw`, which marks candidate 1 terminal;
3. `accept 11 false … c1 e1`, the same pair under a fresh nonce;
4. `receipt 11 1`;
5. a fire pass after the claw-back is evicted.

The pass emits `queuePartial (sighash tx1 0) 0 true 1`, and a terminal copy of candidate 1 is still
resident. Without step 3 the pass emits nothing.

That is `F57`'s defect class in the model. `SPN-33` says "a hot spend a claw-back has defeated is
not finalized at its Hold expiry even if the claw-back is later evicted", and `terminal_sticky`'s
own disjunct, "or was born by this step", admits the revival. The guard does not read the PIN.

`accept` also takes `sp.id = es.id` and registers two candidates under one id.

Wanted:
- An accept whose pair is resident, with equal `tx`, `hot` and `expiry`, adds its Carrier and
  leaves the candidates exactly as is.
- A resident id with any other field, or `sp.id = es.id`, is refused.
- Say whether a replay still runs `DUR-14`'s shrink and `DUR-20`'s traversal, since `SPN-23` says
  it "re-applies its schedule".
- A theorem: on every `Reachable` world, one id names at most one resident candidate.
- `terminal_sticky` restated so that a resident terminal id is never matched by a non-terminal
  candidate.
- The trace above as an exhibit that releases nothing under `current`, plus a same-PIN and a
  cross-PIN replay that leave the resident candidates' `terminal`, `released` and `heldSigners`
  untouched.

Evidence: reviewer B (scratch builds, with the control run), reviewers C and D (same-PIN
duplication).

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- every guard-parameter flip in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still goes red in `Exhibits.lean`
  only, with its asserted count.

title: silence's relation stops at a resubmission after its pair's holder decision: wfEvent refuses SPN-23's repeat
description:
`BtcPolicy.Silence.silence`'s relation stops at a resubmission.

`obsPair` walks a trace only while `wfEvent` holds. `wfEvent` refuses an accept whose candidate ids
are already in `selected`, and `selected` holds Escape ids, which a holder decision inserts. So a
resubmission after its pair's holder decision ends the walk; an earlier one is walked.
`wfEvent`'s docstring justifies the refusal as requiring "what the identifiers intend". But `SPN-23`
specifies that repeat: a request whose acceptance key matches an earlier `Accepted` "re-applies its
schedule and intent, and re-stages".

`DUR-15` says a post-wrench coordinator "can mint validly signed requests indefinitely". So it can
end the relation's coverage at a step of its choosing, inside the concealment horizon.

Reviewer B ran `armTrace` plus one resubmission. Both entering states are `preHorizon`, `wfEvent`
is false, and the walk yields 2 observation pairs instead of 4. A walk without the guard gives equal
observations at all four steps, so this is a coverage gap, not a leak.

Wanted: once `bps-8s0.29` makes `accept` leave a resident pair as is, replace `wfEvent`'s repeat
conjuncts with the uniqueness invariant that bead proves. Then state `silence` over traces that
include resubmissions.

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- an exhibit replaying `armTrace` plus a resubmission yields an observation pair for every
  pre-horizon step, the resubmission included, and proves them equal (equality over a truncated
  walk does not count);
- the existing `DUR-1` exhibits still prove;
- every guard-parameter flip in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still goes red in `Exhibits.lean`
  only, with its asserted count.

title: silence's starting premises cannot be derived from Reachable: Reachable.init leaves sweepActive free
description:
`silence`'s starting premises cannot be derived from `Reachable`, because
`BtcPolicy.Kernel.Reachable.init` pins only `armed = false`, `cands = []` and `carriers = []`. It
leaves `sweepActive` free, so a node with `armed = false`, `sweepActive = true` and
`selected = [(7, true)]` is `Reachable`, and it fails `Silence.NodeInv`'s sweep clause (reviewers A
and C, compiled).

`silence` takes `NodeInv` at the trace's first sample, "assumed here and not derived from
reachability", and `Exhibits.TwoRun.nodeInv_A` discharges it for one concrete start only.

No theorem is false. `holderDecision` sets `armed` and `sweepActive` with the same `|| k.duress`,
so `sweepActive = armed` is preserved by every event (compiled), but nothing states it. This is a
missing invariant, not a bug.

Wanted:
- `Reachable.init` pins `sweepActive = false`. Pinning `selected = []` as well is optional: the
  corollary below does not need it.
- A theorem `sweepActive = armed` over `Reachable`.
- `no_entry_released_before_arming` restated over `armed = false`.
- A corollary, after `Init.silence_from_init` in `.context/vault-review-1002/probes/Init.lean`:
  `silence` for two runs from the same node, the same ledger and empty exposure, with
  `armed = false`, `sweepActive = false` and empty candidates. The rule and monotone-sample
  hypotheses stay explicit.

This establishes initialization only, not `NodeInv` for every `Reachable` state. Pinning `init`
removes worlds from every `Reachable` theorem, which is intended: the removed worlds have
`selected` entries that no accepted Carrier put there.

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- the guard-parameter flips in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still fail at their asserted
  `Exhibits.lean` sites;
- the corollary is tagged `DUR-1`.
close_reason: Below the filing bar: no theorem is false and the invariant already holds per step. Silence.NodeInv.sweep is sweepActive = armed and inv_sysStep preserves it on every event. Mutating holderDecision so a duress commit no longer sets sweepActive goes red in Silence.lean today, so pinning Reachable.init adds no catching power.

title: DUR-8's coupling has no theorem: prove hot-release provenance at input 0 and the counting corollary
description:
`DUR-8` says "So no honest node ever releases a coerced partial, only `≤ t − 1` compromised nodes
can, and that is never a signing quorum. This coupling, not the holder count, is the safety proof".
No declaration states it. The `Kernel` docstring says "`DUR-8`'s federation consequence is a
counting statement under `compromised < t`, not a theorem here", and `no_hot_partial_while_armed`
covers armed nodes only.

Wanted, node-local and at input 0, with no federation and no scheduler:
- **Provenance.** On every reachable world, a hot `queuePartial` for candidate `cid` is emitted
  only by an unarmed node, and only after a normal-PIN holder decision that opened `cid`, tied to
  the emitted message and commitment. Prove it over the event trace or recorded commit history:
  `holderDecision` retires the Carrier, so the Carrier need not stay resident. A ghost field on
  `Node` changes every `Node` literal in `Exhibits.lean`.
- **Counting corollary over the world's exposure.** The premise that every honest exposure row for
  a message carries that provenance is a named hypothesis, since `adversaryExposes` and
  `receivePartial` admit any signer. Under that premise, with no honest normal holder decision for
  the message and fewer than `t` distinct compromised signers, `exposedQuorum` is false for it.

Input 0 is enough for prevention. Under `SIGHASH_ALL`, `DUR-28`'s "`≥ t` distinct valid partials
on every input" makes a quorum at input 0 necessary for finalization, so counting there
over-approximates availability (reviewers A and B).

On an unarmed node every committed Carrier is normal-PIN: `holderDecision` sets
`armed := n.armed || k.duress`. So the statement holds on the current kernel and needs neither
`bps-8s0.26` nor `bps-8s0.31`.

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- both theorems are tagged `DUR-8`;
- an exhibit instantiates the corollary at a concrete world, and another shows a successful normal
  release;
- a twin in which quorum opens without a holder decision refutes the provenance statement;
- every guard-parameter flip in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still goes red in `Exhibits.lean`
  only, with its asserted count.

title: A refused-but-staged Carrier's holder decision opens a resident pair: DUR-4 names commitment ids before SPN-23 computes them
description:
**Decided 2026-10-02 by the spec owner, after a four-reader panel, which agreed unanimously.**
1. An arm intent names a pair only once `SPN-23` has computed the pair's commitments.
2. The holder decision of a refused Carrier opens nothing. A refused Carrier carrying a duress
   intent still arms.

**The defect.** `DUR-4` says the intent recorded at ingress (`SPN-5` gate 12) holds "its two
commitment ids". But the PSBTs decode at gate 17, and `SPN-23` computes the commitments "After all
preceding admission, PIN and post-preflight clock gates pass". The set never says when a gate-12
intent learns its ids.

`SPN-5`'s gate table stages some refusals: they consume the nonce, propagate and stage.
- **Before `SPN-23`:** gate 13 and 16 (clock predicates) and gate 14 (`BAD_PIN`). Read literally,
  `DUR-4` lets such an intent name a pair.
- **After `SPN-23`:** gate 21 (prevout fetch), gate 22 (only `HOT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`), gate 24
  (`HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED`) and gate 27 (`EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT` / `commitment_expiry`). These do name
  a pair.

`DUR-5`'s holder decision sets "`holder_quorum_reached` on both members of the pair, which opens
their release gate". So a refused Carrier that reaches `t` holders opens a resident pair that
this node refused to authorize, though `SPN-9` says "Neither path signs a partial". A gate-14
refusal needs no valid PIN at all. That contradicts `SEC-24`: "flooding wrong PINs produces denial
and never an unfrozen quorum".

**Wanted.**
- `DUR-4`: "its two commitment ids" becomes "its two commitment ids once `SPN-23` has computed
  them; an intent refused before then names no pair".
- `DUR-5`: a holder decision opens the pair only for a Carrier this node accepted, or replayed as
  accepted (`SPN-23`). For a refused Carrier it performs the same arm write, scan and set work
  under both PINs, and opens no candidate. It still arms with the duress bit, as `SEC-24` requires
  ("MUST arm regardless of lockout") and as `DUR-4` requires ("the duress bit MUST be set for a
  refused-but-staged duress request just as for an accepted one").
- `DUR-10`: "**Every** holder decision adds its intent's Escape id" applies only when the intent
  names a pair.
- The kernel gains a refused-but-staged acceptance event. A theorem states that its holder
  decision opens no candidate, with an exhibit replaying a staged refusal that reaches `t`.
- The `DUR-1` relation covers the new event.

**Interaction.** Independent of `bps-8s0.26`'s inherit rule, and needed under every reading. One
reader judged inherit's sticky extension unnecessary once this lands, so decide this before the
sticky question.

Evidence: `.context/vault-review-1002/round4-sticky/` (briefs, four answers, four prototype
patches).

Done when:
- `tools/check-all.sh` is green;
- every guard-parameter flip in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` still goes red in `Exhibits.lean`
  only, with its asserted count;
- the staged-refusal exhibit opens nothing under `current`.

WIR-18's five little-endian moves (fixed, u8, u16/u32/u64, var, list) over `List UInt8` (or `ByteArray`
if core Lean decides well on it), and CHN-25's big-endian commitment encoding as a structure
`Commitment` (wallet_id 32, version i32, lock_time u32, inputs [(txid 32, vout u32, sequence u32)],
outputs [(script var-u32, amount u64)], fee u64, expiry u64, policy_version u32) with `encode` and
`decode`. Theorems, all core Lean: decode (encode x) = some x (WIR-18 moves and Commitment);
exact byte lengths (`(encode x).length = 108 + 40·inputs + Σ(12 + script) …` stated from CHN-25's
widths); injectivity over the bound fields (encode a = encode b → a = b); and F32/CHN-24's
negative: signature metadata (partials, coord_sig, request nonce) is NOT bound — a Commitment has
no such field, stated as a theorem that two requests differing only there encode equal.
Exhibit: protocol-vectors.json `commitment.fields` encodes to `commitment.preimage` byte for byte
(hex parsed in Lean as data; the SHA-256 id stays check_vectors.py's — no SHA-256 in Lean).
Endianness is one property: CHN-25 is "the ONE big-endian encoding"; a theorem that u32 BE ≠ u32
LE on a witness value keeps the two encoders apart. Tags: WIR-18, CHN-25, CHN-24 at clause
granularity; no CNF id. Done when `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green and
the vector exhibit closes by `decide`. One commit on main + beads close.
close_reason: Encode.lean landed: WIR-18 moves + CHN-25 commitment, decode∘encode, injectivity, lengths, unbound metadata, vector exhibit; check-all green

title: Milestone 7: selected Escapes, accounting bridge, SILENCE as a two-run relation
description: ADR-0023 decision 10 item 7. Selected set: List (EscapeId × Bool) keyed by Escape commitment id with DUR-10's OR-merge; a normal-PIN entry never released whatever sweepActive does (F54 fix row 4); every holder decision and hot acceptance writes every window (DUR-20) as a writes count equal under both PINs. DUR-22 denominator computed from ChainView + the selected set with restoreAll; theorem it is the same value on every pass while the set only grows; distinguish equality across candidates in one environment, preservation across the sequence, agreement across nodes — if the across-pass claim needs more than DUR-22's construction supplies, return the precise gap to DUR-22 as a finding (first reader §4). Accounting bridge: POL-18/POL-19 reserve/refund/age-out transitions establish milestone 3's counting premises for POL-20's cohort; ADR-0014's trace becomes a reachable exhibit and the withdrawn completion bound a refuted theorem (¬ ∀ window, completed <= n/t × cap) while the admission theorem holds; SPN-33 mempool settlement refunds nothing. SILENCE: Obs structure (response shape, /pending, /healthz bucket, /events queue, peer message shapes and sizes, abstract work counts) with observe ∘ step = stepObs ∘ observe on every prefix where now < current T (DUR-14 dynamic, may be zero, sticky once ended); two worlds = one request body with two enrolments (SEC-10); leaky twins: DEF-12's arm-conditioned marker and F54's conditional window traversal; docstring says counts are not durations (F22, SEC-47). F3, F4, F13 kept as traces with no repair chosen. Glossary gains observer projection and concealment horizon when this lands.
notes:
Q1 DECIDED 2026-09-19 (four-reader panel, .context/m7-q1b-*.md; landed as F59 + amendments to DUR-22/24/28/31, CNF-140, MAN-9, ADR-0020, commit e74d9ff): Coverage denominator = filter on the chain read + every distinct selected input outpoint added once (counted regardless of the read; precedence over exclusions) — NOT confirmed+restored-excluded; rebuild Coverage.denominator from a ChainView + selected set. Theorems: (i) one value per pass; (ii) floor: P >= union of selected inputs on every pass; (iii) per-node single sweep under "both selected at this node's first release"; (iv) aggregate burn <= (100-pct)% of swept. Exhibits kept: restoreOne (F54), unconfirmed-external-deposit two-pass trace, subtracting-shape breaks the floor, cross-node 2-of-3 trace, late-selection trace, phantom-prevout denial. No snapshot, no ingress rule.

Q2 DECIDED 2026-09-20 (three-reader panel, .context/m7-q2-*.md; the clock gap landed as F60). SILENCE relation: one request body, two enrolments (NOT two PIN bodies; CNF-40 is the conformance approximation). Horizon = the duress run's CURRENT T (DUR-13 then DUR-14 shrinks), guard on the state ENTERING each step so the arming receipt is always inside the prefix (its effects are the last shared observable, and DEF-12's twin sits there); sticky by prefix quantification, since Effective is not monotone. Freeze-invisible is a LIVE INVARIANT over the holder-decision scan, not an unconditional inequality, and carries a non-decreasing-sample hypothesis (F60). Obs carries response BYTES/refusal codes, Effect.broadcast, /healthz locked_down + last_deadline_tick, ordered peer effects with destinations and sizes — not shapes and aggregate counts; omits timing class, allocations, lock-hold time (F22/SEC-47). Theorem shape = coupling invariant between the two runs with equal observable effects per step, NOT observe-commutes-with-step. Twins: (a) DEF-12 arm-keyed marker, (b) F54 conditional window traversal, (c) static T — FAITHFUL, ADR-0012's 2026-07-15 log says "One true silence break -> FIXED: dynamic T", so a real guard parameter; plus a fourth NEGATIVE EXHIBIT (not a flip): duress-only selected-entry insertion, which also opens SPN-41's capacity probe. One node; the federation horizon is the first node's crossing, a corollary, and no federation claim is made.

Q3 DECIDED 2026-09-20 (three-reader panel, .context/m7-q3-*.md; landed as F61 CLOSED + F62 OPEN + POL-20 and DOM-24 amended). Accounting bridge = a ledger transition model (reserve at acceptance POL-18/SPN-29, refund only at terminal-without-exposure POL-18/SPN-33, one-way age-out POL-19) COMPOSED WITH milestone 4's kernel — a ledger-only model cannot make ADR-0014's trace reachable (needs holder decisions, releases, settlement, completion). Bookkeeping: Ledgers.counting has TWO hypotheses (hcap, hq), not three; hq already fuses "at least t-c acceptances" with "still charged at the cut", so H2/H3 are bridge lemmas, not arguments. No-age-out lemma: TRUE, needs only that the reservation is in the trailing interval; POL-17 not needed; saturating Nat subtraction truncates toward live; requires non-decreasing HotClock samples in the trace (Kernel.Reachable admits arbitrary Env samples today — add the premise). Cohort exclusion is PER RESERVATION; per spend the conclusion is false. H1 needs the one-way-release model (F62). A1 also needs a reservation map keyed by commitment id with the authoritative amount, and a well-formed cohort (distinct ids, amounts matching) or Ledgers.charge's hcap cannot be derived. ADR-0014 refutation is EXISTENTIAL over a reachable trace (exists start, completed in [start, start+W) > (n/t) x cap), not a bare forall-negation; the trace hits exactly 2V so it refutes the n/t reading and NOT the loss-div-t sizing rule. New twin required by decision 6: DEF-5 / F57's settlement-refund row (current retains on mempool-only settlement per SPN-33, withdrawn refunds on any settlement), distinct from milestone 4's pending-log flag. The ledger is NOT in Obs but IS part of Q2's two-run relational invariant (later HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED and work counts are observable); DUR-11 keeps the freeze off it, POL-21 puts the frozen candidate's refund strictly after Lockdown, past the horizon.
close_reason: Milestone 7 complete: the Armed overlay, the coverage denominator, the Hot ledger and accounting bridge, and SILENCE as a two-run relation, with F59-F64 recorded along the way

title: M7.1 Armed overlay on the kernel: T, sweep_active, selected set, DUR-14 shrink + DUR-20 traversal, monotone-sample premise
description:
Milestone 7, ticket 1 — the Armed overlay on milestone 4's kernel. BLOCKS 7.2, 7.3, 7.4: neither
the bridge nor the SILENCE relation can be stated against the kernel as it stands.

Extend `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Kernel.lean` (its docstring's scope cut names exactly this work):

- Overlay on `Node`: `T` (wall domain — DUR-13 computes it from `first_seen`, an effective time,
  and `earliest_hot`, a `fireAt : Wall`; it is compared against the effective sample, so add the
  named comparison to `Clocks.lean`, never a raw field read), `sweepActive : Bool`, and
  `selected : List (EscapeId × Bool)` with DUR-10's OR-merge. DUR-10: `active` "has exactly one
  writer — the holder decision with `arm = true` — and once set it is never cleared".
- Holder decision (already one step, DUR-5): additionally insert the intent's Escape id with its
  duress bit OR-merged, compute `T` per DUR-13 (`Deadline.initialT` is the arithmetic), install
  every selected Escape's fire window `[T, T + combine_slack_secs]` (DUR-20; SPN-37 registers the
  Escape with none), and set `sweepActive` on a duress commit. Pin-uniform: DUR-5's "identical
  scan, overlay write, set insertion and window refresh", differing only in one internal bit.
- Hot acceptance while armed: DUR-14's shrink (`Deadline.shrink`), and re-install EVERY selected
  window unconditionally — DUR-20: "an actual shrink MUST NOT trigger a traversal a non-shrink
  does not". The traversal count must not depend on whether `T` moved.
- Release gating per entry: `sweepActive` AND the entry's own duress bit (DUR-10), so a normal-PIN
  entry is never released (F54's row).
- `Reachable` gains a non-decreasing-sample premise on the trace — it admits arbitrary `Env`
  samples today, and both F60 (effective) and the ledger's no-age-out lemma (mono) need it.
  State it as a hypothesis on the trace, not as a clock-type property: `Effective` is not
  monotone, since the high-water advances on an accept only (SPN-13).

Every milestone-4 theorem stays green, and the four CI flips stay red at their measured counts.
Done when `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green and each existing flip is
re-measured locally. One commit + beads close.
close_reason: overlay landed: T, sweep_active, selected set, DUR-13/14/20 writes, release gating, six new theorems, MonotoneSamples; check-all green and all four flips re-measured

title: M7.2 Coverage rebuilt: set-shaped denominator, the floor, per-node single sweep, burn bound, F59's exhibits
description:
Milestone 7, ticket 2 — the selected set and the coverage denominator (Q1, panel
.context/m7-q1b-*.md; F59; DUR-22 as amended). Depends on 7.1.

Rebuild `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Coverage.lean`: `denominator` today takes `vaultAsArmed` as a
number and has the shape confirmed + restored − excluded. That shape falls below the floor when
one selected Escape spends another's change output (CHN-30 permits vault change). Build it
instead from a `ChainView` and the selected set as a SET construction: filter the live read by
the exclusions (selected-Escape and resident-rung outputs), then union in each distinct selected
input outpoint ONCE at its `witness_utxo` value, counted whatever the read says of it; counted
inputs take precedence over every exclusion. Never subtract after unioning.

Theorems:
- Within one pass every selected Escape is measured against the same value.
- The floor: on every pass the denominator is at least the union of the selected Escapes' inputs.
- Per-node single sweep: two input-disjoint Escapes both selected at this node's first release
  cannot both cover, whatever moved the denominator between their passes.
- Aggregate burn: this node's total sweep burn is at most `100 − escape_coverage_pct` percent of
  what it sweeps, which is also what makes DUR-24's own fee-cap sentence true.

Exhibits (keep the existing `restoreOne` twin, F54): the unconfirmed-external-deposit two-pass
trace; the subtracting shape breaking the floor; the cross-node 2-of-3 trace where two honest
nodes selected different Escapes and both confirm; the late-selection trace; the phantom-prevout
denial. The last three are residuals F59 records, not defects to repair here.

Selected-set semantics from 7.1: release requires `sweepActive` AND the entry's own bit, so a
normal-PIN entry is never released. Tags DUR-22, DUR-24, DUR-10, MAN-9 at clause granularity.
Done when check-all is green. One commit + beads close.
close_reason: Coverage rebuilt as a set construction with the floor; per-node single sweep over the model; both twins measured red; residual exhibits landed; two-axis review findings fixed; check-all green

title: M7.3 Ledger.lean + the accounting bridge: one-way age-out, hcap/hq for POL-20's node-indexed cohort, ADR-0014 reachable, DEF-5 twin
description:
Milestone 7, ticket 3 — the Hot ledger and the accounting bridge (Q3, panel
.context/m7-q3-*.md; F61, F62; POL-20 as amended). Depends on 7.1.

New `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Ledger.lean`: a reservation map keyed by commitment id holding the
authoritative amount, the reservation time, the expiry and the exposure bit (SPN-33 keeps all
four independently of candidate residency). Transitions: reserve at acceptance with POL-16's
admission check and POL-18's idempotent retry ("a retry keeps the original reservation time");
refund ONLY at a terminal state reached without exposure, and never on mempool-only settlement
(SPN-33); age-out as a ONE-WAY release, POL-19's predicate being the condition for releasing
rather than a membership test re-run (F62 — re-running it lets a backward wall step resurrect a
reclaimed charge and put the live sum over the cap).

Bridge to `Ledgers.counting`, which has TWO hypotheses, `hcap` and `hq`, not three: `hq` already
fuses "at least `t − c` acceptances" with "still charged at the cut".
- `hcap` from the live-sum invariant, by induction over the transitions (needs the one-way
  release above). SPN-29's registration-refused reservation is unwound in the same step, so the
  intermediate state is not reachable; the 4 096-entry refusal inserts nothing.
- `hq` from POL-20's node-indexed cohort plus the no-age-out lemma: a reservation whose time lies
  in that node's trailing `hot_window_secs` at the cut is still live there. The lemma needs only
  membership in the trailing interval — POL-17 is NOT needed, saturating `Nat` subtraction
  truncates toward live, and the boundaries are inclusive — plus 7.1's non-decreasing Mono
  samples, without which a charge can be released at one sample and be live again at a later one.
- Well-formedness the bridge needs and `Ledgers.charge` does not assume: distinct commitment ids,
  each cohort amount equal to the stored amount, distinct honest ledgers.
- The cohort counts only reservations not refunded while unexposed, PER RESERVATION: per spend the
  counting theorem's conclusion is false, not merely unproved (F61).

ADR-0014 reachable: compose the ledger with 7.1's kernel — a ledger-only model cannot reach it,
since the trace needs holder decisions, releases, settlement and completion. State the refutation
existentially over that trace: some window of length `hot_window_secs` completes more than
`(n / t) × cap`. It hits exactly `2V`, so it refutes the `n / t` reading and NOT the
`loss ÷ t` sizing rule; say so, and keep the admission theorem standing beside it.

New guard parameter (ADR-0023 decision 6 requires it — F57's DEF-5 row is a dated repair):
settlement refunds, `retainOnMempool` current versus `refundOnAnySettlement` withdrawn, red in
`Exhibits.lean` only, the exhibit showing the premature refund admitting another spend while the
first's exposed authority is still usable. Distinct from milestone 4's pending-log flag.

POL-21: the freeze does not touch the ledger, and a frozen candidate's refund waits for the
expiry sweep strictly after Lockdown. Tags POL-16, POL-18, POL-19, POL-20, POL-21, SPN-33.
Done when check-all is green and the new flip is measured red locally. One commit + beads close.
close_reason: done

title: M7.4 Silence.lean: Obs, two-run coupling invariant, entering-state horizon, three twins + one exhibit, glossary terms
description:
Milestone 7, ticket 4 — SILENCE as a two-run relation (Q2, panel .context/m7-q2-*.md; F60).
Depends on 7.1. Best done after 7.3, since the ledger is part of the relational invariant.

New `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Silence.lean`.

`Obs`: response BYTES and refusal codes (DUR-1 says "response bytes", and a refusal code is every
capacity and budget twin's channel), the pending projection, /healthz's bucket plus `locked_down`
and `last_deadline_tick` (API-19), the /events queue, `Effect.broadcast`, and ordered peer effects
with destinations, shapes and sizes — an ordered trace, not aggregate counts. Omit, and say so in
the docstring: timing class, allocation counts, store-lock hold time. Counts are not durations
(F22, SEC-47: "End-to-end timing has no hard gate"), and a unit-cost model must not be advertised
as constant-time.

Two worlds: ONE request body with two enrolments, the enrolment table being the secret. Not two
PIN bodies — the coordinator knows what it sent, so two bodies differ in a public input. CNF-40's
"identical under both PINs" is the conformance experiment that approximates this, not its
statement.

The relation is a COUPLING INVARIANT between the two runs with equal observable effects at each
step, not `observe ∘ step = stepObs ∘ observe`: identical observations do not determine the next
output, and exposing hidden fields to make a projection commute would defeat the purpose.

The horizon is a guard on the state ENTERING each step: unarmed, or the effective sample below
that state's current `T`. So the arming receipt is always inside the prefix and its own effects
are the last shared observable, which is where DEF-12's twin lives. Sticky by prefix
quantification, because `Effective` is not monotone. The horizon may be zero (DUR-14: "a hot
spend whose Hold already matured at arm time collapses the window to now").

Freeze-invisible is a LIVE INVARIANT over DUR-13's holder-decision scan, carrying 7.1's
non-decreasing-sample premise: without it a matured hot spend is due under normal and frozen
under duress at a sample still below `T` (F60, the retained trace).

Twins, guard parameters red in `Exhibits.lean` only: DEF-12's marker keyed on the arm bit instead
of the pin-uniform `committed`; F54's conditional window traversal; and static `T` — faithful,
ADR-0012's 2026-07-15 log records "One true silence break → FIXED: dynamic T". Plus ONE negative
exhibit that is not a flip: a duress-only selected-entry insertion, which also opens SPN-41's
capacity probe.

The ledger (7.3) is not in `Obs` but is part of the relational invariant: a duress-only refund
surfaces later as a HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED and in the work counts.

Scope: one node. DUR-1 is per node ("Every observable a node emits"); peers' relays are inputs
held equal, and the federation horizon is the first node's crossing, stated as a corollary by
events with no federation claim made. Docstring names what is not claimed: machine timing, a
compromised node or pre-wrench coordinator (SEC-10), any Lockdown latency (DUR-15, F13, SEC-48),
the cover story's plausibility, and anything past `T`. F3, F4, F13 and F60 stay traces with no
repair chosen.

CONTEXT.md gains **observer projection** and **concealment horizon** when this lands (ADR-0023
decision 7: the terms enter the glossary when the first model uses them). Done when check-all is
green and all three flips are measured red locally. One commit + beads close.
close_reason: SILENCE as a two-run relation landed: Silence.lean with the coupling invariant, the entering-state horizon, the three twins and the non-flip exhibit; F64 recorded

title: btc-policy-lean: create the implementation repo with the offline ceremony verifier
description: ADR-0023 decision 8. Created when milestone 5 (bps-8s0.5) lands. First commit: lake git dependency on btc-policy-spec/tools/formal at a pinned commit (packaging tested in milestone 5), plus the OPR-10..OPR-15 public-artifact verifier of lean-02.md §4 (schema revision refused first, descriptor normalize/parse, script reconstructed, threshold and key order verified, wallet_id and manifest_hash recomputed, endorsements verified, recovery lock read back from the descriptor not hardcoded, network/destination parameters from the authenticated manifest). Second app: the key-less validator of the three-arm user-signer group (OPR-20..OPR-29). No secrets in scope; node-*.toml, PIN digests, backend credentials never inputs. Records its own conformance status per OVR-17. STO-9's lock order and STO-13's dedicated deadline thread bind this signer too: an actor/event-loop design is a proposed amendment to their owners, not conformance by a cleaner model (first reader §3). Nothing that implements the system goes into the spec repo.

title: Milestone 3: lifecycle arithmetic (F52 alternation, POL-20 counting theorem, SPN-38 cross-node prefix)
description: ADR-0023 decision 10 item 3; pulled ahead of the encoders by both panel readers. (a) SPN-46 age over a ChainView structure (tip, confirming : TxId → Option Block, mtp : Block → Nat) with the source as a guard parameter .chainMtp | .perNodeLog; F52's alternation table (one compromised signer rotating which honest node co-signs, seven links in fifteen days against a thirty-day interval) admitted under .perNodeLog and refused at its second link under .chainMtp on every honest node; the WTC-25 replacement exhibit (unconfirmed refresh's higher-fee replacement admissible under .chainMtp). (b) POL-20's counting theorem over a list of honest ledgers: each ledger's charges <= cap, each counted spend in >= t − c ledgers ⇒ (t − c) A <= (n − c) cap; corollaries per shape. Not the accounting bridge (milestone 7). title: Review fixes for bps-sio, bps-mmt, bps-pxp.1 and bps-pxp.2: false sentences, weak checks, second homes
description:
Review fixes for `bps-sio`, `bps-mmt`, `bps-pxp.1` and `bps-pxp.2` (two-axis review of
`e50abc5..2609756`, 2026-10-12). No decision changes: each item is a false sentence, a weaker check
than the ticket asked for, or a second home of a rule. Verify each item against the tree before
changing it — the line references are from the review, not guarantees.

## False statements

1. `tools/check_formal.sh`: the comment says a declaration list "left by an earlier run is never
   read stale", but the `rm -f` sits after the script's early exits, so a failing local run leaves
   the old list for `check_citations.py`. Move the removal to the top.
2. `tools/check_citations.py` `read_index()`: "Shared with check_regions.py and check_ids.py -- one
   reader, not three" and its missing-file message no longer describe who reads the index
   (`check_citations.py` no longer does; `check_copies.py` imports it). Make both true.
3. `tools/check_citations.py` `HISTORICAL` comment (and `bps-mmt`'s closing comment): "each stem's
   forms spelled out" is false — only `withdraw` has its forms, and "withdrawing" no longer
   matches. Fix the regex or the comment.
4. `ADR-0028`: "The owner accepted that residual with the first ticket" — `bps-pxp.1` stated the
   backward-step residual under its *Formal* section and left it unfixed; the owner did not rule on
   it. Say that, and name `bps-pxp.1` / `bps-pxp.2` instead of "first ticket" / "two tickets".
5. `MAN-29`: the ceremony's floor sentence drops `SEC-37`'s "except through such a spend". Quote or
   cite it whole.
6. `CNF-47`: check "the earliest such record lowers `T`" against a trace where `T` was already
   lowered since the arm (reviewer B: 640, not 650); `CNF-47` is test guidance, so an
   implementation's suite would assert the wrong value. `bps-pxp.2` reports fixing ticket 1's gaps
   (1) and (2) — confirm, and fix what remains.
7. Unquoted claims about `DUR-13`: `SPN-41`'s "starts at a seed `max(ratchet, now)` (`DUR-13`)",
   the `Clocks.Effective.deadlineReached` docstring. Quote `DUR-13` or cite it without claiming.

## Checks weaker than asked

8. `BtcPolicy.Exhibits…backward_step_keeps_duress_start`: its docstring says 1200 is "not reached by
   `DUR-7`'s driver at the ratchet"; the theorem asserts only `armed` and `T = 1200`. Assert
   `deadlineReached … = false` (its withdrawn twin asserts `= true`).
9. `Kernel.HotDomain` carries two choices in one guard (which candidates are in the domain; a repeat
   reads the resident). `AGENTS.md`: every semantic choice is a guard parameter — split it, each
   with its own flip control asserting errors in `Exhibits.lean` only, counts measured.
10. `.github/workflows/gates.yml`: the `$((before + 4))` expectation in the citation-gate step is
   hand-derived from the planted string; derive it from the plant or assert the names directly.

## One rule, one home

11. What the declaration list holds is restated in about nine places (`CONTEXT.md` *Declaration
    list*, `ADR-0023` decision 1 and its rejected option, `README.md`'s `check_formal.sh` row,
    `check_formal.sh`, `Exe.lean` twice, `check_citations.py`'s NAMES docstring, `LEAN` comment and
    `lean_names`). Keep `ADR-0023` decision 1 as the home; point at it elsewhere. `Req.lean`'s
    docstring and `ADR-0023`'s *Consequences* restate `check-all.sh`'s reader list (the ADR copy
    omits `check_ids.py`): cite the list.
12. How to quote genuinely withdrawn wording lives only in `check_citations.py`'s docstring.
    `README.md` *Requirement conventions* owns retention ("Withdrawn wording is retained only where a
    trap sits behind it"): add the how there, point the docstring and the gate's failure hint at
    it, and drop the docstring's copied numbers ("eight characters", "four or more words").
13. `CONTEXT.md`: *Arm intent* restates `DUR-13`'s rule, *Hot domain* carries mechanism ("On a
    repeat, `DUR-14` reads the resident"), *Declaration list* cites no owner. Terms only, owner
    cited. "seed" is listed under *Preimage*'s `_Avoid_`; give `DUR-13`'s seed a flagged-ambiguity
    line or another word.
14. `SEC-37`'s "caps `T` at the value it had while live … no route" argument appears in `SEC-37` and
    twice in `ADR-0028`; `ADR-0028` *Consequences* copies a `DUR-13` sentence unquoted; `CNF-47`
    restates the domain. One home each; quote elsewhere.

## Stop rule

Accept when items 1–14 are done and the gate is green unpiped. A Panel finding outside this list goes
into the closing comment, not a new Round, unless it shows a sentence of a requirement stating false
behaviour.

title: SPN-41's removal: pin the effective-time close with an exhibit and a control; ADR-0027's 'only'
description:
Two gaps the review of `bps-l5b` (`bfcbcb2..b4c2c0a`) found. No decision changes.

1. **Check strength.** `SPN-41` says "The close is read at effective time and never at the time
   ratchet". A planted removal that reads the time ratchet instead builds green once
   `Silence.prune_pub`'s proof is stubbed: no exhibit pins it. It is reachable: after a backward wall
   step on an armed node the ratchet runs ahead of effective time, and a ratchet-reading removal would
   delete a selected Escape whose window is still open on effective time. Add an exhibit (an armed
   node, the ratchet past `T + combine_slack_secs`, effective time back inside the window: the Escape
   and its pair stay resident) and a planted-mutation control in `gates.yml` that goes red in
   `Exhibits.lean` only, per `AGENTS.md`.
2. **A false "only" in `ADR-0027`.** "On every other node only `SPN-41`'s expiry pruning collects it":
   `SPN-33` and `POL-18` also name `NCH-24`'s lookup eviction ("or `NCH-24`'s lookup evicts it"). Say
   both routes, both expiry-based.

Out of scope (a modelling boundary, recorded so nobody files it): the removal written as an outer
branch on `active` is not observable in the model, because a prune pass's candidate visits do not
reach `Obs`; only a conformance item against an implementation can catch it.

Done when: the exhibit and control pass, `ADR-0027` is true, the gate is green unpiped.

title: check_formal.sh's req-attribute greps are lexical: multiline duplicate tags and multiline attribute [req] retags pass
description:
`tools/check_formal.sh:45-49` refuses a declaration tagged `@[req]` twice and an after-the-fact `attribute [req …]` with two greps. Both are lexical: the first requires the literal spacing `req "` (a newline between `req` and the string defeats `\breq "`), and the second is per-line (`grep -rnE`), so `attribute [\n  req "CHN-4"\n] name` is not seen. Lean accepts both multiline forms; the runtime gate then sees only the effective (last) tag and passes, so a declaration can be silently retagged. Reported by reviewer D; not yet reproduced — reproduce first.

Repair, smallest that works: make both greps whitespace-tolerant and file-spanning — `-z` on the attribute check as well, `\breq\s+"` in place of `\breq "` (the multiline implemented_by check at line 37 is the pattern to copy). Add two negative controls in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` beside the existing "implemented_by … written over several lines" control: a multiline duplicate `@[req\n "CHN-4", req\n "CHN-2"]` tag and a multiline `attribute [\n req "…"\n]` retag, each red at the named message. Do not move these checks into the Lean gate unless the grep cannot express them.

Acceptance criteria:
- Both multiline forms are red at `check_formal.sh` with the existing messages.
- Two new gates.yml steps prove it, runnable locally.
- KEEP working: the single-line forms still red (existing behaviour); a legitimate `@[req "X"] def …` and a docstring containing the word `req` still pass; `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green on the final tree.
- Files: `tools/check_formal.sh`, `.github/workflows/gates.yml`. No other files.

Source: reviewer D's review of commit 949d63f (confirmation pass, 2026-09-16). Reviewer A did not report it.

title: Formal: move bps-nfx's general proofs into Evaluate.lean, drop the hint seam and POL-10's dated tag
description:
This bead fixes three findings from the review of `bps-nfx` (`e5c0810`). None of them changes a
verdict or a theorem statement.

## Findings

1. **General proofs live in `Exhibits.lean`.** `ADR-0023` keeps each model's general proofs in
   its own module. `Exhibits.lean` holds the `current` instantiations and the executable verdicts
   (decision 6, decision 12 and Consequences: "`BtcPolicy/Exhibits.lean` holds the current
   exhibits"). Its other theorems with general binders are all `_with_current` instantiations of
   proofs owned elsewhere.

   `bps-nfx` instead put these general proofs under `BtcPolicy.Exhibits.Evaluate`:
   - `softenCode`, `FirstAt`;
   - `hints_never_admit`, `hints_acceptance_iff`;
   - `recognised_iff`;
   - `firstUnknown_none_iff`, `firstUnknown_some_iff`;
   - `allowlisted_iff`;
   - `dest_allowed_iff`, `dest_notAllowed_iff`, `dest_changeNotDerivable_iff`;
   - `acceptance_exact`, `first_failing_output`.

   `POL-6`'s formal-home sentence therefore points into `Exhibits`. The cause was `bps-nfx`'s own
   control clause, which named "theorem 2 and the hinted-stranger exhibit" in one build. That
   clause is withdrawn here.
2. **`recognised` takes a `_hint` argument it never reads.** Its docstring says the argument
   exists only for the negative control, so the definition is shaped by its test.
3. **`POL-10` ends "(amended 2026-10-05)".** README forbids inline dated tags ("The reference
   project kept every correction inline with a dated tag, and its documents became hard to
   read"). No earlier value exists, because `POL-10` was silent on the case before.

## Scope

- **Move the general proofs listed in finding 1** into `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Evaluate.lean`,
  namespace `BtcPolicy.Evaluate`, without changing their statements. The decided exhibits stay in
  `Exhibits.lean`, under `BtcPolicy.Exhibits.Evaluate`: `cfg`, `accepted`, `consistencyRows`,
  `fixture_membership`, the `POL-7` rows, `foreign_input`, the stranger exhibits,
  `hot_budget_refused` and the two fee exhibits.
- **Drop `_hint` from `recognised`.** `recognised_iff` loses its hint argument.
- **Move the mutation seam into `firstUnknown`.** Its `if recognised …` line carries a trailing
  `-- hint-trust` marker, and the `gates.yml` control's `sed` adds `|| hs.headD false` to that
  condition.
- **Rewrite the control so its errors fall in `Evaluate.lean`.** It must name
  `hints_never_admit`. Measure the exact count with
  `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py <name>` and pin the measured value.
  The decided exhibit is no longer part of the control, since `Exhibits.lean` cannot build once
  `Evaluate.lean` fails. Keep it in one shard.
- **Rewrite the docstrings written around the test.** These are `Evaluate.lean`'s module
  docstring ("The planted hint-trust mutation must leave this upstream module buildable…") and
  `hints_never_admit`'s "independently of all mutation-sensitive characterisation lemmas". A
  docstring states what the declaration says, not how CI breaks it.
- **Update `POL-6`'s formal-home sentence** to the `BtcPolicy.Evaluate.*` names.
- **Delete "(amended 2026-10-05)" from `POL-10`.** The rest of the sentence stays verbatim, since
  `CNF-17` quotes it.

## Out of scope

Any change to a theorem statement, an exhibit's verdict, `request`, `evaluate`, or the
`CNF-17`/`POL-10` rule. Leave the other dated tags in `ADR-0020` and `05-duress-and-lockdown.md`
alone.

## Done when

- The three findings are fixed.
- No general proof remains under `BtcPolicy.Exhibits.Evaluate`.
- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, run unpiped.
- The rewritten control passes locally with its measured count.
- Every other `gates.yml` control whose count or line moves is re-run with `run-steps.py` and
  updated to the measured value. This includes the `DEF-15`, `F57` and citation declaration-name
  controls.

title: check_regions.py requirement_at tests HEADING before DEF_RE, so a region under a heading-form DEF requirement resolves to nobody
description:
`tools/check_regions.py:103-113` `requirement_at` tests the generic `HEADING` boundary before `DEF_RE`. `DEF_RE`'s second alternative (`tools/check_ids.py:42`) accepts heading-form definitions such as `### DEF-1 — …`, and `14-known-defects.md` defines DEF-1 onward that way. title: Citation gate: a baseline-listed unquoted attribution hides the earlier pairing's false quote in its chunk, and nothing keeps the baseline empty

pairing's false quote in its chunk, and nothing keeps the baseline empty.

nothing for it. An unquoted attribution the landed reading reports counts as something. With the

title: API-25: a refusal carries a bounded fault list for the first per-item check that refuses
description:
The owner needs to debug production cases where a node and the client disagree: which inputs or
outputs a node refused, and why. Today a refusal says only `{code, check, detail}`, and the client
may parse only `code` (`API-16`). The design below came from four readers over two rounds on
2026-10-05, and the owner accepted it that day, with printing on a live terminal only.

## The member (new `API-25`)

```json
{"refusal": {"code": "CHANGE_NOT_DERIVABLE", "check": "verified_change", "detail": "…",
  "faults": {"tx": "spend",
             "entries": [{"output": 1, "code": "CHANGE_NOT_DERIVABLE"},
                         {"output": 3, "code": "DEST_NOT_ALLOWED"}],
             "truncated": false}}}
```

- **`tx`** names the transaction the indices point into: `spend`, `escape`, `refresh` or
  `clawback`. The client does not parse `check`, so `check`'s `escape:` prefix cannot tell it.
- **Fee-bump rungs carry no list.** `CHN-16` gives a rung "the same ordered input set, the same
  ordered output script set" as its base, so a rung fails a per-item check only if its base does,
  and the base is checked first. State this in `API-25`.
- **Each entry** has exactly one of `input` or `output`, a zero-based index into `tx`, and a
  `code` from `API-13`.
- **Order and length.** Entries are strictly ascending with no duplicates, and all name the same
  side. They are the first 32 failing items; `truncated` is true exactly when more exist. The
  operator program's 64 KiB `/sign` cap (`OPR-50`) needs this bound, and policy sets no output
  count limit (`POL-15`).
- **Only the first refusing check contributes**, and only one of these:
  - `POL-7`'s missing-`witness_utxo` row, reached after its four preceding rows pass: each entry
    `PSBT_INCONSISTENT`;
  - `POL-9`: `UNKNOWN_INPUT`;
  - `POL-10`: each output's hint-selected code;
  - `SPN-25`'s confirmed-prevout mismatch: `PSBT_INCONSISTENT`;
  - `SPN-43`/`SPN-50`'s replacement-test `UNKNOWN_INPUT`. This refusal has no `check` string
    today, and `POL-9` returns the same code, so give it its own check string in `API-14`;
  - `SPN-46`'s too-young or unconfirmed refresh inputs: `REFRESH_TOO_SOON`.

  Every other refusal omits `faults`.
- **The top-level `code` and `check` are the first entry's.** Under `POL-10` that is the existing
  first-failing-output rule.
- **Agreement and silence.**
  - Honest nodes give the same list for the pure checks on identical inputs.
  - Chain-check lists may differ between nodes at different tips, and that difference is the
    debugging signal. No byte-identity across nodes is required.
  - The member is response bytes under `DUR-1`, so it must be identical under the normal and the
    duress PIN. Every listed check runs after the PIN gate; say so in `API-25`.
- **Replay.** `SPN-23`/`SPN-24` return a cached refusal with its member verbatim. Which refusals
  are cached does not change.

## The client (`API-16`, `OPR-8`, `OPR-9`)

- **Validate first.** A coordinator discards the member whole unless all of these hold:
  - `tx` names a transaction it sent;
  - every index is below that transaction's input or output count;
  - every code is one the check can return;
  - the first entry's code equals `code`;
  - the order is strictly ascending, with at most 32 entries.

  Allocation is bounded before decoding.
- **Show it only on a live terminal.** The operator program MAY render a validated list on an
  interactive terminal, in locally authored words, attributed to the node, beside its own
  evaluation of the same items where it can compute one. It MUST suppress the list when its
  output is not a terminal. It MUST NOT write the list, or any comparison derived from it, to
  logs, artifacts or persisted state. Only the closed code is retained, as today.
- **Never act on it.** Nothing the program sends, retries, recomposes, selects, or reports as the
  outcome or exit status reads a fault list. A node may lie: `SEC-9` keeps `t − 1` compromised
  peers in the model.
- **`check` and `detail`** stay never-printed and never-retained.
- **`OPR-65`** keeps one coin per refresh transaction. Its stated reason ("could not name the
  input at fault") becomes false, so replace it with the never-act rule.

## Requirement ids

- New: `API-25` and one new `CNF` item covering:
  - order, the cap and `truncated`;
  - PIN-uniformity;
  - a malformed list being discarded;
  - the chain-dependent rows;
  - replay.
- Amended: `API-12`, `API-14`, `API-16`, `WIR-8` (one example with the member), `POL-7`, `POL-9`,
  `POL-10`, `POL-13`, `SPN-23`/`SPN-24`, `SPN-25`, `SPN-27`, `SPN-43`, `SPN-46`, `SPN-50`,
  `OPR-8`, `OPR-9`, `OPR-65`, and `CNF-17` (two unrecognised outputs, both listed, in order).

## Out of scope

The Lean model of the list, which is the next bead; `OVR-13`; batched refresh; any change to which
refusals exist or to `POL-6`'s order.

## Done when

- The text above has landed.
- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, run unpiped, including the fixtures
  gate on the new JSON example.
- Every `gates.yml` control whose count moves is re-measured and updated.
close_reason: Accepted by Panel and Manager after Round 2; specified bounded refusal fault lists in 3a12b160a54af48d4fcb390d5cdb85c8ab3941f4, with review resolution and verification recorded in the closing comment.

title: A selected Escape id acts only on the candidate registered in the Escape role (a refused request aliased a hot spend's id)
description:
A selected Escape id acts only on the candidate registered in the Escape role.

## The defect (found reviewing `bps-pxp.2`, 2026-10-12; reproduced by four reviewers)

`CHN-24`'s commitment binds no role, so a transaction's id is the same whether it is presented as a
spend or as an Escape. A request refused after its commitments are computed and before gate 25
checks the Escape — gate 21, gate 22's `HOT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, gate 24's `HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED`
(`SPN-5`'s table) — can name a registered hot spend's exact transaction as its Escape. `DUR-10`: "A
refused intent with computed ids MUST perform the same insertion", so the hot spend's id enters
`selected_escapes`, and `DUR-20`'s window write for a selected entry lands on the hot candidate.

- **The floor breaks.** The rewritten window `[T, T + combine_slack_secs]` is open, so the hot
  candidate is back in `DUR-13`'s hot domain with `fire_at = T`, and each later holder decision
  writes `T − epsilon_secs`: 700 → 695 → 690 … down to `now`, inside the concealment horizon.
  `SEC-37`'s floor and `DUR-13`'s "A hot candidate whose window shut unfired, or that this node has
  broadcast, caps no `T`" are false as the set stands.
- **A pending payment is cancelled.** Under the normal PIN the same write moves an owner's pending
  hot spend's window and `DUR-10`'s release gate refuses it (selected, bit clear): a cancel, against
  `DUR-16`'s "there MUST be no cancel operation for a pending spend".

Gate 29 is not a text route (gate 25 precedes it, `SPN-27` requires escape-class there); the kernel
shows it only because it does not model gate 25.

## Decision (the owner's, 2026-10-12, after a four-reader design review over two rounds, 3–1)

**W: insertion is unchanged; every use of a selected entry applies only to the candidate registered
in the Escape role** (`SPN-36` records "its role (spend or escape)"): `DUR-20`'s window write,
`DUR-10`'s release gate, the hot-domain read in `DUR-13` / `DUR-14`, and the projection. A spend's
`fire_at` is always `SPN-30`'s. Kernel: delete `Kernel.inHotDomain`'s selected-entry disjunct and
`unarmedDeadline`'s selected-fire branch; the role test reads the registered role (reviewer B used a
`Cand.isEscape`), never `!c.hot` (that admits an unpaired non-hot candidate).

Rejected (record in `ADR-0028`, edited in place — it is unpushed):
- **G, an insertion guard** (insert only an id a resident Escape-role candidate carries): it drops the
  mark of a refused duress Carrier naming an Escape not yet resident, later registered beside a
  different spend (`DUR-5` inherits per spend, so the later decision does not recover it), and
  reverses `refused_repeat_selects_before_residency`; and in the kernel, where ids are abstract, a
  pruned selected Escape's id re-registered as a hot spend breaks it (`T` 510 against a floor of
  700) unless a kernel-only guard stands in for `CHN-24`.
- **R, a role-tagged commitment**: works, but changes every published commitment vector and the wire
  for a property the stored role already gives.
- **E, excluding selected entries from the hot domain alone**: the window write still lands, so the
  candidate re-enters the domain anyway, and the cancel remains.

## Formal

Reviewer B built W at `2609756`: `silence` and `silence_initial` re-prove with their statements
unchanged and no new premise, `lake build` and `lake exe gate` green, no `sorry`, every existing
exhibit passes unedited (about 21 Kernel lines, about 160 Silence lines). Make W a guard parameter
per `ADR-0023` (B expects this may add a Silence premise — build it; if `silence` needs a premise,

title: SPN-41: the armed-window removal runs only on a node whose active bit is set; the pending log as its own record
description:
`SPN-41` says the registry "MUST remove every selected Escape and its pair when the armed window
closes regardless of their own expiries", and does not say whether that runs on a node that is not
armed. `DUR-20` writes the selected set and its windows under both PINs, so an unarmed node holds
selected entries with installed windows too (`DUR-10`: an entry whose duress bit stays clear "sits in
the set present and never released"). `Kernel.prune` models `SPN-41`'s exemption but not this
removal.

## Decision (the owner's, 2026-10-11, after a four-reader design review, 4–0)

1. **The removal runs only on a node whose `DUR-10` `active` bit is set.** `active` equals `armed`
   and `sweep_active` at every reachable state (`NodeInv.sweep`); name `active`, the bit `DUR-7`'s
   driver reads. The entry's own duress bit is not the key: it would leave inert pairs on an armed
   node to linger for nothing.
2. **"Closed" is effective time strictly past `T + combine_slack_secs`**; equality is inside the
   window, as `SPN-41`'s exemption reads it.
3. **It is a constant-time conjunct of the prune pass's per-candidate keep test, never an outer
   branch on `active`**: an outer branch would visit candidates on one run only before `T`, which
   `DUR-1` forbids ("candidate visits"); as a conjunct it is false in both runs until the window has
   closed, which is at or after `T`, outside the concealment horizon.
4. **Registry only.** `SPN-42` says "Before expiry, an id is removed only on a public network
   settlement event (`SPN-33`), never by a PIN-dependent path", with no `T` scope, so the pending log
   keeps the entry until its own expiry. The Kernel derives `/pending` from resident candidates
   today; model the pending log as its own record (`SPN-30`: "recorded in the **pending log** as
   `commitment_id → expiry`"), so the removal empties the registry and leaves the pending log.

Rejected: removal on every node. It is not a SILENCE question; its harm is liveness: an ordinary
spend dies once a prune pass lands between its pair's window close and its own fire time, which
happens whenever `duress_delay_secs + combine_slack_secs < hold_secs` (with the defaults, any Hold
over a minute). Three reviewers built that kill trace.

## Formal

- `Kernel.prune` gains the conjunct; `silence` and `silence_initial` keep their exact hypothesis lists
  (four reviewers built it green; the proof needs one lemma that the condition is false inside the
  horizon).
- `ratchet_moves_only_at_its_events`' prune sample 320 lies past its window's close; move it to 290 or
  earlier.
- An exhibit that an ordinary spend survives a prune past its pair's window close on an unarmed node
  and fires at its own fire time; a planted-mutation control (removal on every node) that goes red in
  `Exhibits.lean` only, per `AGENTS.md`.
- The pending log as its own record, with the proofs that read `/pending`; an exhibit that an armed
  node's removal leaves the pending-log entry until its expiry.

## Done when

`SPN-41` names the predicate; `SPN-42` stays as written and the model satisfies it; the exhibits and
the control pass; the gate is green unpiped.

title: Citation gate accepts false direct possessive quotations
description:
The citation gate accepts a false direct possessive quotation in a Lean docstring. This is a check's ability-to-fail gap discovered while reviewing bps-8s0.29, not a request to change its registration semantics or to file a cosmetic correction.

Reproduction at de452ffcf952aeee34f8c192b0b81d8610723b99 (also present at closure commit 64d457c): tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Ledger.lean's module header attributes the superseded unwind sentence to SPN-29 using the form `SPN-29`'s followed immediately by a quotation. The requirement now says "only a reservation placed by this request MUST be unwound in the same step". The header's old quotation is not recognized by tools/check_citations.py.

In an isolated copy of the tracked tree, with the generated requirement index copied in, the following runs of the actual citation gate established the gap:
- Unmodified tree: exit 0.
- Replace that SPN-29 quotation with "the moon is made of green cheese and nothing else", retaining the direct possessive attribution: exit 0, unchanged verified-attribution count.
- Use the same false text with the attribution written as `SPN-29`: followed immediately by the quotation: exit 1, reporting the false SPN-29 attribution.

ATTRIB recognizes speech verbs, the possessive noun-plus-that form, and colon quotations. It does not recognize a possessive followed directly by a quotation, even though that form attributes exact words just as directly. No change to the check's intentionally excluded summary-verb paraphrases is requested.

Done when the direct possessive quotation form is checked against its named requirement in Markdown and Lean docstrings, a deliberately false quotation in that form fails for the owning requirement, valid quotations still pass, and a workflow negative control demonstrates the new failure. Preserve existing historical-quotation exemptions, attribution ownership, nested-quotation behavior, and the unquoted baseline. Run the full repository gate unpiped and the affected workflow controls against the working tree.

This follow-up is outside the fixed bps-8s0.29/.34/.26/.30/.32/.27/.28 sequence and must not be picked by it.

title: Citation gate: a delayed-opener quotation ending in an attribution-shaped phrase, then another quotation, goes unchecked; 0ddae30 rejected it
description:
The citation gate leaves a false quotation green when a quotation with a delayed opener ends in an
attribution-shaped phrase and another quotation follows in the same chunk. The gate at `0ddae30`
rejects it.

Measured at `9a9a9d5` against `0ddae30`. `<false>` is a phrase OVR-1 and POL-18 do not contain.

| Chunk | `0ddae30` | `9a9a9d5` |
|---|---|---|
| `` `OVR-1` reads, in full, "<false> when `DOM-1` reads" and later "some other words of it here" `` | red, OVR-1 | green |
| `` `OVR-1` reads that "<false> when `DOM-1` reads" and `POL-18` says "<false>" `` | red, OVR-1 and POL-18 | green |
| `` `OVR-1` reads, in full, "<false> when `DOM-1` reads" and `POL-18`: "<false>" `` | red, OVR-1 and POL-18 | green |
| `` `MAN-2` says that "Unsealed they were not adjustable either — `OPS-1` states" and, later in the text, "The manifest preimage MUST be" `` (genuine) | green | red, blaming OPS-1 |

How it happens:
- `bps-6cz` counts a mark directly after an attribution as that attribution's opener for the
  stray-span test, wherever `ANCHORED_QUOTE` can match at the mark.
- Here, the mark after `` `DOM-1` reads `` is the outer quotation's straight closer. It can still
  open a span of 8 or more characters toward the later quotation's opener, so it counts as an
  opener.
- The outer span is then judged stray and dropped. `DOM-1` restarts pairing. A later attribution
  falls inside the span that `DOM-1` introduces and reads as quoted.

The shape needs all of these:
- a delayed opener: `reads, in full, "`, `reads that "`, or a second quotation `and "`;
- a straight closer (curly quotation marks stay red);
- at least 8 characters between that closer and the next quotation mark.

The module docstring declares this residual. The opener rule was chosen in the `bps-6cz` review by
three reviewers to one, over keeping the opener set to colon and possessive forms. That alternative
avoids this residual but leaves `` `OVR-1`'s "<good>", but the " mark, `DOM-1` says "<false>" ``
green. No chunk on the tree has this shape.

Done when: the chunks above give the `0ddae30` result, or an owner-chosen narrower result named in
the closing comment. Every `bps-6cz` case in `gates.yml` keeps its expectation. The docstring no
longer declares the residual. A `gates.yml` case asserts each restored red, and the baseline bytes
are unchanged.

title: Citation controls: no case fails if the refusal of an unclosed colon or possessive quotation skips an attribution that owns a later quote
description:
No citation control fails when the refusal of an unclosed colon or possessive quotation is
skipped for an attribution that owns a later quote.

`bps-1rj` refuses a colon or direct-possessive attribution whose quotation has no closing mark in
its chunk, whether or not it owns a quote. Every `gates.yml` case of that refusal plants a chunk
in which the refused attribution owns no quote. A mutant that moves the refusal into the
no-quote branch of `find()` passes both "Prove the citation gate checks direct possessive
quotations and preserves their contracts" and "Prove the citation gate refuses a quotation that
runs past a sentence end" (found by a reviewer, reproduced by the Manager at `00f9630`).

Under that mutant, `` `OVR-1`: "foo “No signature path MAY bypass the policy checks” and more ``
goes from refused (`00f9630`) back to green with one more verified attribution, as at `b51f795`:
the straight quotation's words outside the curly span are checked by nothing.

Done when: a `gates.yml` case asserts the refusal for an unclosed colon or possessive opener that
owns a later quote; that mutant turns the step red; and the baseline bytes are unchanged.

title: Formal: no hot broadcast while armed over every send, and POL-11's zero outflow for non-hot classes
description:
This bead closes two gaps found in the 2026-10-06 review of the external proposal's composition
section (§5, `Vault.lean`). The review declined `Vault.lean`, because wiring `Evaluate`, `Kernel`
and `Package` together mostly proves that the pipeline calls its own checks. Trial compositions
did find two facts the composed path relies on and nothing proves.

## Findings

1. **The send has no universal arming theorem.** `Kernel.no_hot_partial_while_armed` is stated
   over `step r env w .firePass` alone. The send, where `SPN-39` puts "the linearization point
   between arming and sending", is held only by `Exhibits.race_refused_with_current` (one trace)
   and `Exhibits.bounded_from_ready`, which its docstring calls "An exhibit over a stated bound,
   with no completeness claim". `Kernel.send` re-reads `releaseAuthorized` when `r.reauth =
   .beforeSend`, so the universal statement should be short.

2. **`POL-11`'s zero outflow for non-hot classes has no declaration.** `POL-11` says "refresh and
   escape sweeps have zero outflow by construction". The kernel's freeze guards only `c.hot`, and
   `Ledger.refusedByBudget` meters only `sp.hot`, so `hot = false` must mean zero hot outflow.
   Nothing proves that for the classes `Classification.classify` returns. Two reviewers
   independently changed `Classification.outputClass`'s last arm from `none` to `some .escape`, so
   an output no descriptor recognises reads as escape-class, and the whole layer still built
   green. `CHN-30` says a spend "with any output that derives from nothing, has no class and MUST
   be refused".

## Scope

- **`Kernel.lean`:** a theorem over every reachable world, under `r.reauth = .beforeSend`: on an
  armed node, every effect of `step r env w (.send cid)` is the broadcast of a non-hot candidate
  with that id. A sketch:

  ```lean
  theorem no_hot_broadcast_while_armed (r : Rules) (hr : r.reauth = .beforeSend) (env : Env)
      (w : World) (hw : Reachable r w) (ha : w.node.armed = true) (cid : Nat) :
      ∀ eff ∈ (step r env w (.send cid)).2,
        ∃ c ∈ w.node.cands, c.id = cid ∧ c.hot = false ∧ eff = .broadcast c.tx.id
  ```

  Instantiate it over `current` in `Exhibits.lean`, so the existing `DUR-29` reauth flip goes red
  there too, then re-measure that step's pinned count.
- **`Exhibits.lean`:** `@[req "POL-11"]` a lemma that a spend `classify` puts in the escape or
  refresh class has zero `hotOutflow`. It lives in `Exhibits.lean`, not `Classification.lean`:
  `DEF-15`'s fault of the mixed arm makes it false, and `Classification.lean`'s header says
  "every theorem the mixed arm of `classify` decides (`DEF-15`), lives in `Exhibits.lean`, so
  flipping the rule or faulting the arm goes red there and nowhere else". The DEF-15 step's
  comment gives the reason: "`Classification.lean` must still build, or the exhibits that decide
  the arm are never read". Add the request-shape corollary (`validateRequestShape` members carry
  zero outflow) only if it stays short.
- **`gates.yml`:**
  - one planted-mutation step that changes `outputClass`'s `else none` to `else some .escape`,
    and pins the exact error count, files and declaration names. A reviewer measured that this
    plant leaves the whole layer green today, and only the new lemma goes red.
  - The DEF-15 step will gain the new lemma as an error (a reviewer measured 2 to 3). Re-pin its
    count and add the name to its checks.
  - Put the new step on a shard other than 3.
- **`Cand.hot`'s docstring:** it is `SPN-28`'s recorded class, and `accept` takes it as given, so
  a `hot = false` candidate with positive outflow lies outside these theorems. Name that boundary
  in one sentence.

## Out of scope

`Vault.lean`; binding `Evaluate`'s computed outflow to `Kernel.Tx.outflow`; `Package.validate`
inside the kernel.

## Done when

`nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0 unpiped, the new step passes under
`nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py '<step name>'`, and every `gates.yml`
step that edits `Kernel.lean`, `Classification.lean` or `Exhibits.lean` passes with its
re-measured counts (at least DUR-29's reauth flip and DEF-15).
