title: Receipts carry their sender: Carrier.holders becomes distinct relay senders (F65, DUR-5, DUR-6)
description:
Direction chosen 2026-09-21, unanimous across a three-reader panel. None of the three
accepted the first proposal (keying exposure by recipient); all three kept `ADR-0023`
decision 9 intact.

WHAT TO BUILD. Give the receipt event its authenticated sender and replace the Carrier's
holder count with relay sender identities.

    | receipt (cid : Nat) (sender : Nat)      -- the wire's sender_node_id

    structure Carrier where
      ...
      relaySenders : List Nat                 -- replaces holders : Nat

    -- holder count = 1 + (eraseDups relaySenders).length; self stays implicit

WHY IT IS FORCED, not cosmetic. `DUR-5` counts "each distinct peer whose authenticated
relay of the same Carrier this node receives"; `DUR-6` requires "a sender already counted,
an uncommitted duplicate, or a committed intent MUST be an idempotent no-op". A `Nat`
cannot express "already counted", so one peer relaying twice reaches `t` and opens
`DUR-8`'s release gate a relay early, under either PIN. `ADR-0012` already specifies the
mechanism: a node "counts ITSELF ... plus the distinct `sender_node_id`s that relay it
back, and arms once that holder set reaches t".

WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY. Not a new safety result. `ADR-0012`: the count "is a timing/liveness
mechanism, NOT the safety proof"; the proof is the release gate, already carried by
`Kernel.no_hot_partial_while_armed`. Expect fidelity to `DUR-5` and `DUR-6`, plus a new
negative exhibit — one peer relaying twice arming a node below threshold.

DO NOT TOUCH decision 9 or `Exp`. Exposure is world level by execution, not omission:
"a commitment-keyed or node-local history loses the authority a partial released under one
commitment carries for a second over the same transaction, in both readers' probes".
`Exhibits.ReleaseKernel.exposure_key_exhibit` is that probe retained as a trap and
`no_resident_release_does_not_mean_safe` is the false statement a node-local reading proves.
`CONTEXT.md`: exposed authority "outlives everything node-local". `CONTEXT.md` also bans
"peer id" under *Node id*.

SILENCE. All three readers expect the two-run relation to survive: `Silence.Input.pinless`
feeds one common event to both runs and `pubCarrier` erases only `duress`, so sender
history stays coupled without widening `Obs`. The senders must be COUPLED, not erased —
equal counts with different holder sets diverge on the next duplicate. Repairs reach
`commits_pub`, `receipt_pub`, `pubCarrier`, the event cases and the marker/work proofs;
expected local and wide, not structural. Nobody could build, so this is unverified.

BLAST RADIUS. `Kernel`: `Carrier`, `Event.receipt`, `commits`, `receipt`, the `inv_step`
case (which never reads holders). `Silence`: the lemmas above. `Ledger.afterEvent`: new
arity. `Exhibits`: ~20 `.receipt` constructions. Decision 9, `Exp`, `finalizable`,
`Ledger`'s POL-18/POL-20 exhibits: untouched.

STILL OPEN, not part of this ticket. `Kernel.finalizable` decides `packageAccepted` from
world-level availability, so the model admits a node assembling a package from partials it
never received. One reader would split it — a global predicate still reading the exposure
so the trap keeps its subject, and a local one reading possession on `Cand` so candidate
pruning removes possession while world exposure stays forever — which needs an explicit
authenticated partial-receive event, since `adversaryExposes` must not imply delivery. The
other two would document the boundary and wait for delivery semantics. Decide separately.

PLACEMENT. Not milestone 8 (bps-8s0.11 is WTC reorg, OPR-49..51 outbound delivery
knowledge, STO trace adapters). `ADR-0023` decision 10 has no item for this; record a dated
scope extension referencing milestones 4 and 7 rather than rewriting their acceptance.

PRIMARY SOURCES, out of main. `prototype/federation-invariant` 2214a5f — `BtcPolicy/Fed.lean`
lifts `Kernel.Inv` to `Fin n -> Node` in nine lines of proof over an arbitrary interleaving,
for all n, axioms [propext, Quot.sound]. Its `finalizable_without_receiving` proves no
reachable execution — the premise supplies the count — so cite it as a statement about the
predicate, never as a trace. `prototype/quint-vs-decide` c176c67 — the retracted tool
measurement, four defects in `RESULTS.md`; tag `quint-prototype-as-reviewed` holds the
hashes an external companion cites.
close_reason:
Landed in d0245f7. Event.receipt carries sender_node_id; Carrier.relaySenders replaces holders : Nat; holderCount adds this node.

Two deviations from the ticket, both narrowing:

1. The ticket says 'holder count = 1 + (eraseDups relaySenders).length'. addSender dedups on INSERT instead, so the field is already a set and holderCount is length + 1. Stronger: DUR-6's 'idempotent no-op' becomes the identity on the Carrier, not a count that happens not to move (duplicate_relay_changes_nothing reads the clause literally). eraseDups on read was probed and has no usable core-Lean lemma for (l ++ [s]).eraseDups.length without Mathlib; addSender_nodup proves the set property the length rests on instead.

2. addSender also refuses this node's own id, which the ticket did not call out. DUR-5 counts 'each distinct PEER' and this node is already the +1, so without it a relay carrying the node's own sender_node_id counted the node twice and reached t a relay early — the same defect as the duplicate. Found by the code-review Standards axis. self_relay_is_not_a_second_holder is the exhibit.

Negative exhibit: duplicate_relay_is_one_holder. The withdrawn count is written out beside the holder set; the quorum conjunct is what goes red if the count comes back (the withdrawn count itself is trace arithmetic and runs no kernel term).

Untouched as instructed: ADR-0023 decision 9, Exp, finalizable, Ledger's POL-18/POL-20 exhibits. SILENCE preserved with the sender coupled, Obs not widened.

ADR-0023 decision 10 carries the dated scope extension against milestones 4 and 7. F65 stays OPEN on the finalizable half only.

title: Citation gate skips every quote in a sentence whose prose contains a history marker as a substring, such as "it reads"
description:
The citation gate cannot fail on a quote in a sentence whose prose outside its quotes contains one
of its history markers, even when that prose is ordinary current wording.

`tools/check_citations.py` skips a chunk whole when `HISTORICAL.search(prose)` matches ("Recognise
the sentence, do not check it"). The regex has no word boundaries, and several alternatives are
common present-tense prose: `it read` matches "it reads", and `no longer`, `amended`, `corrected`,
`retired`, `used to`, `rewritten`, `previously` and `the original` all occur in current
requirements. A sentence that says "whose close it reads" or "the registry no longer holds it" is
treated as quoting withdrawn wording, and every quote in it goes unchecked.

Probed 2026-10-11 in a clone of `b3de1b6`, during `bps-l5b`'s review. `NCH-41`
(`06-node-channel.md`) has the sentence "`SPN-38` adds the HotClock check "…" beside the fire
window, whose close it reads "at `max(ratchet, effective)`", and `SPN-30` says "Its fire window is
`[fire_at, min(expiry, fire_at + combine_slack_secs)]`"". Changing `min` to `max` inside the
`SPN-30` quote left the gate at exit 0. Rewording "it reads" to "is read" turned the same
corruption red ("attributes to SPN-30 a phrase SPN-30 does not contain"). The quote is correct
today; the gap is the check. `bps-l5b`'s rounds hit the same trap twice in new text (a `Kernel.prune`
docstring with "the windows it reads"), caught only by corruption probes.

Done when: a history marker exempts a sentence only where it actually marks quoted withdrawn
wording (whole-word matching at least, and present-tense forms such as "it reads" never exempt);
every chunk the narrowed rule newly checks passes or is corrected; and a `gates.yml` negative
control plants a wrong quote in a sentence that also says "it reads" and asserts the refusal.
close_reason: Accepted: no history marker exempts a quote; HISTORICAL, whole-word, governs only the unquoted rule; controls in gates.yml; follow-ups bps-2jz, bps-6cz, bps-uwy

title: Formal: POL-6's checks over one decoded PSBT, acceptance exact and hint-independent
description:
`Policy.lean` models only which code each `POL-6` row returns: its docstring says "the checks
themselves (`POL-7` to `POL-12`) are not modelled". This bead models them, over one decoded PSBT.
It meets `ADR-0025`'s four points:

1. It ranges over every decoded PSBT and every sealed configuration.
2. An evaluator that admits a stranger output signs a theft. `POL-4`: membership is decided
   "never by trusting a PSBT's `bip32_derivation` hint".
3. The rules are this set's (`POL-6` to `POL-12`). Derivation stays the assumed boundary
   `derive`, as in `Membership.lean`.
4. Its control is a planted hint-trust mutation, below.

## Spec amendment (lands on `POL-10` and `CNF-17`)

`POL-10` does not say which output's hint decides the code when several outputs do neither, and
the two codes differ. Add to `POL-10`: when several outputs do neither, the first of them in
transaction order decides the code. Add the same case to `CNF-17`. Owner's decision of
2026-10-05.

## Scope

- New `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Evaluate.lean`, imported by `tools/formal/BtcPolicy.lean`.
- The decoded PSBT, as the pure checks read it and nothing more:

  ```lean
  structure Psbt where
    txInputs    : List Encode.Input           -- the unsigned transaction's inputs
    txOutputs   : List Encode.Output          -- its outputs: script and amount
    inputMaps   : List (Option Encode.Output) -- each input map's witness_utxo
    outputHints : List Bool                   -- each output map: bip32_derivation non-empty
  ```

  The maps are lists of their own, so `POL-7`'s count rows can be represented. No
  `non_witness_utxo` (`F48` is open). Nothing reads `nVersion`, `nLockTime` or `nSequence`,
  and counts are read only for `POL-7`'s emptiness and equality rows, never bounded (`POL-15`).
- `Cfg` holds `derive`, `max`, `vault`, `escape`, `allow : List Membership.Descriptor` and
  `hotMaxPerTx`.
- `request : Cfg → Psbt → Policy.Request` computes the five flags from `POL-7`, `POL-9`, `POL-10`,
  `POL-11` and `POL-12`. Define `evaluate cfg p := Policy.evaluateSpend (request cfg p)`. `POL-6`'s
  order then exists once, and `dest_outranks_budget`, `budget_outranks_fee` and
  `evaluate_in_reachable` apply unchanged.
- Each output becomes a `Classification.Output` whose `kind` is `Membership.kindOf …` of its
  script. `allowlisted`, `hotBudgetOk` and `member_discharged` are reused, not restated.
- The fee row is a three-way `Policy.Fee` built from the totals, with two lemmas:
  `fee = .ok ↔ feeCapOk totalIn totalOut` and `fee = .inconsistent ↔ totalIn < totalOut`.
- When a `POL-7` row fails, the later flags read defaults. Nothing is proved about them, since
  row 1 hides them.

## Theorems (each `@[req]` on its owner; no `sorry`, no axiom, no `native_decide`)

0. **One characterisation lemma per `request` field**, each an iff against concrete predicates
   over the PSBT and `Cfg`, never against another flag. Without these, a `request` that refuses
   too eagerly or files a defect under the wrong row satisfies theorems 1–3. That is lost recovery,
   since the same evaluation runs over Escapes (`POL-13`), and a wrong code, since `POL-6` calls
   the order load-bearing.
   - `psbtInconsistent = true` ↔ one of `POL-7`'s five rows fails.
   - Assuming `POL-7` holds, `unknownInput = true` ↔ some `witness_utxo` script does not
     `matchesScript` the vault descriptor (`POL-9`).
   - Assuming `POL-7` holds, `dest` is `.allowed` ↔ no output's kind is `.unknown`. Otherwise it is
     `.changeNotDerivable` or `.notAllowed`, according to the hint of the first `.unknown` output in
     transaction order (`POL-10`).
   - Assuming `POL-7` holds, `overHotCap = true` ↔ `hotBudgetOk` fails (`POL-11`).
   - Assuming `POL-7` holds, `fee` is `.inconsistent` ↔ `totalIn < totalOut`, and `.ok` ↔
     `feeCapOk totalIn totalOut` (`POL-12`).
1. **Acceptance is exact** (`POL-6`). `evaluate cfg p = none` holds exactly when all of these hold:
   - `POL-7` holds: inputs and outputs are non-empty, both map counts equal their transaction
     counts, and every input map has a `witness_utxo`;
   - every `witness_utxo` script `matchesScript`es the vault descriptor (`POL-9`);
   - no output's kind is `.unknown`, which is `allowlisted` over the computed outputs (`POL-10`);
   - `hotBudgetOk` holds (`POL-11`), and so does `feeCapOk` (`POL-12`).
2. **Hints never admit** (`POL-10`). Take two PSBTs that differ only in `outputHints` (lists of
   the same length). They get the same result once `CHANGE_NOT_DERIVABLE` is read as
   `DEST_NOT_ALLOWED`. In particular, one is accepted exactly when the other is.
3. **The first failing output decides** (`POL-10` as amended). Suppose `POL-7` and `POL-9` hold,
   stated as concrete predicates rather than flag values, and some output's kind is `.unknown`.
   Then `evaluate` returns `CHANGE_NOT_DERIVABLE` if the first such output in transaction order
   has a hint, and `DEST_NOT_ALLOWED` if it does not.
4. **Exhibits**, all by `decide`, over a toy `derive` with a small `max` and a definite vault
   descriptor (`CHN-3`), so that no exhibit relies on a vault script past the bound:
   - one accepting PSBT;
   - one PSBT failing each `POL-7` row;
   - one PSBT for each of `POL-6` rows 2–4, and two for row 5 (one `.inconsistent`, one
     `.overCap`);
   - a stranger output with a hint, refused `CHANGE_NOT_DERIVABLE`;
   - two strangers with hints `[false, true]` and `[true, false]`, refused by the first.

## Control (`ADR-0025` point 4)

Add one `.github/workflows/gates.yml` step, in exactly one shard, shaped like the `DEF-15` step:
- `sed` plants the hint-trust mutation, so the destination check counts an output with a hint as
  recognised;
- `grep` confirms the `sed` applied;
- `lake build` runs, and the step asserts it fails with the measured exact error count, naming
  theorem 2 and the hinted-stranger exhibit.

Mark the line the `sed` targets with a trailing comment, as the `DEF-15` control's `-- mixed` is
marked. Run the step locally with
`nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py <name>`.

## Spec text

- Add the `POL-10` and `CNF-17` amendment above.
- In `POL-6`, add a formal-home sentence naming `BtcPolicy.Evaluate.evaluate` and theorems 1–3,
  as `POL-4` names its own.
- In `Policy.lean`'s module docstring, replace "the checks themselves (`POL-7` to `POL-12`) are
  not modelled" with a pointer to `Evaluate.lean`.

## Out of scope

- Classification and request shapes (`CHN-30`, `CHN-32`, `CHN-35`), already modelled over
  `Classification.Output`.
- `SPN-47`: `POL-15` says "no refresh interval or feerate".
- `SPN-25`'s chain comparison, signatures, `POL-13`'s `escape:` twin, and `check` strings.
- Any new guard parameter or new `CNF` item.

## Done when

- Theorems 0–4 have landed.
- The `POL-10`, `CNF-17`, `POL-6` and `Policy.lean` text is changed as above.
- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, run unpiped.
- The new control step passes locally.
- Every existing `gates.yml` control whose exact count moves (at least the `DEF-15` and `F57`
  steps) is re-run with `run-steps.py` and updated to the measured value.

title: Citation baseline: nothing enforces may-shrink-never-grow, and main() rewrites a baseline it cannot read
description:
Nothing enforces the citation baseline's "may shrink, never grow", and the gate rewrites a baseline
it cannot read.

`tools/citation-baseline.json` lists the unquoted attributions the gate admits. Its rule, "Ratchet:
may shrink, never grow", lives only in the file's note:
- no `gates.yml` step compares the file with the previous commit or asserts that it is empty, so a
  commit that adds a signature admits a new unquoted attribution and every gate stays green;
- `main()` replaces the file with the current findings whenever it fails to load (any exception
  from opening or parsing it), so a missing, corrupted or truncated baseline admits every unquoted
  attribution then on the tree, and the run exits 0.

`bps-efh` offered a control for this as an alternative. The triage of `bps-efh` (2026-10-15) chose
the per-chunk fix instead, applying the owner's `bps-0wv` decision ("fail a quotation if either
reading finds it false, cut, or unquoted"). That fix makes the two-reading guarantee independent of
the baseline but leaves the ratchet itself unenforced (recorded at the close of `bps-efh`).

Decided 2026-10-17: retire the baseline, so that any unquoted attribution fails the gate outright.
The decision, its tally and the contract are in the Agent Brief comment.

Done when the Agent Brief's acceptance criteria hold.

the gate reports fails it, `tools/citation-baseline.json` and the code that reads or rewrites it are

the current findings as the new baseline and exits 0. The module docstring's UNQUOTED rule says

title: Formal: API-25's fault list for the pure checks in Evaluate.lean
description:
This bead models `API-25`'s fault list for the pure checks in `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Evaluate.lean`. The
previous bead adds `API-25` and amends `POL-7`, `POL-9` and `POL-10` to define their entries; this
bead depends on it.

It passes `ADR-0025`'s four points:
- It ranges over every decoded PSBT.
- A wrong list either names the wrong output, so an operator debugging a production
  disagreement is misled, or contradicts the top-level code, which `POL-6`'s order makes
  load-bearing.
- The rules are this set's own.
- It has a planted control, below.

## Scope

- **A fault entry and its list.**
  - A `Fault` is an index and a `Policy.Code`, tagged input or output.
  - `faults : Cfg → Psbt → List Fault` gives the complete list for the first refusing check among
    `POL-7`'s `witness_utxo` row, `POL-9` and `POL-10`, and is empty otherwise.
  - The 32-entry cap is a `take 32` over the complete list, and `truncated` is `32 < length`.
  - Reuse `recognised`, `owned` and `firstUnknown`'s scan rather than restating them.
- **Theorems in `Evaluate.lean`, each tagged `@[req]` on its owner:**
  - when `faults` is non-empty, `evaluate` returns its head's code;
  - for each listed check, the list is empty exactly when that check passes;
  - replacing the hints with an equal-length list changes only entry codes, never the indices;
  - the indices are strictly ascending;
  - the transmitted list is a prefix of the complete one, and `truncated` is exact.
- **Exhibits in `Exhibits.lean`:**
  - mixed hints over two strangers with a recognised prefix;
  - two foreign inputs;
  - a missing `witness_utxo` on the second of two inputs;
  - a list longer than 32, truncated.
- **Control (`ADR-0025` point 4):**
  - plant a mutation in `faults` that scans outputs in reverse, marked with a trailing comment;
  - `.github/workflows/gates.yml` asserts that the build fails at the head-code theorem, with an
    exact count measured by `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py <name>`;
  - the step lives in exactly one shard;
  - re-measure the existing hint-trust control, since `faults` reads the same scan.
- **Formal-home sentence.** Add one sentence to `API-25` naming the theorems.

## Out of scope

- The chain-dependent rows (`SPN-25`, `SPN-43`/`SPN-50`, `SPN-46`), which have no pure model.
- `Silence.lean`: `DUR-1` already covers the member as response bytes.
- Any change to `request` or `evaluate`'s verdicts.

## Done when

- The theorems, exhibits and control have landed, with no `sorry`, no axiom and no
  `native_decide`.
- The gate is green, run unpiped.
- Every control whose count moves is re-measured and updated.

title: F68: a coercer times Lockdown by presenting an old spend commitment — fix in two tickets
description:
Close `F68` (`16-open-findings.md`): a coercer holding the coordinator can make Lockdown due at will,
and so learn the PIN class at the scene, by presenting an old spend commitment.

## Decision (the owner's, 2026-10-11/12, after a four-reader design review over four rounds)

`F68` is fixed, in two tickets, and `SEC-37` stays an accepted residual, restated.

1. **Ticket 1 — what starts the countdown.** Only records whose own duress bit is set contribute a
   `first_seen` to `DUR-13`'s minimum, and the minimum is seeded at `max(ratchet, now)`.
2. **Ticket 2 — which hot spends cap `T`.** `earliest_hot` and `DUR-14` read only hot candidates
   not broadcast whose fire window is not closed at `max(ratchet, now)`, and `DUR-14` reads the
   resident candidate's `fire_at` on a repeat acceptance. Ticket 2 writes the one ADR for both and
   withdraws `F68`.
3. **`SEC-37` stays accepted** and is restated: a hot spend accepted before the first duress-PIN
   ingress, not broadcast, whose window is not closed at the arm — whether or not it can still fire
   — brings Lockdown to its `fire_at − epsilon_secs` or to `now`, and a coercer who knows the owner's
   payment times can choose that moment.

Every SpendRequest's spend is hot (`CHN-32`: "A SpendRequest whose spend is any class other than hot
MUST be refused"), so `F68`'s old commitment is always a hot spend. That adds two routes to the one
`F68` names, which ticket 1 alone leaves open; hence ticket 2.

Evidence (reviewer letters A–D; built scratch modules and answers): `/var/tmp/f68-evidence/`.
close_reason: Both tickets closed: bps-pxp.1 (duress-bit start seeded at the ratchet) and bps-pxp.2 (the hot domain); F68 withdrawn, ADR-0028

title: F68 ticket 1: only duress-bit records start DUR-13's countdown, seeded at max(ratchet, now)
description:
`F68` ticket 1: only duress-bit records start `DUR-13`'s countdown, seeded at `max(ratchet, now)`.

## The defect

`DUR-13` takes "the earliest `first_seen` among this intent, every resident intent and every
retained nonce tombstone (`NCH-40`) naming the same spend commitment, under **both** PINs", then
`T = max(t_ceiling, now)`. So an ORDINARY record can start the hostage window before any duress PIN
was presented:

- **`F68`'s route.** A fresh-nonce resubmission of an old ordinary commitment under the PIN the
  victim gives inherits the old `first_seen`; `T` lands at `now` in the duress run only.
- **Late ordinary decisions** (found in the review, reachable today). Any holder decision landing
  more than `duress_delay_secs` after its own ingress on an armed node computes a past `T` and the
  clamp writes `now`: an unbound wrong-PIN Carrier staged early and decided late (reviewers B, C: a
  `BAD_PIN` refusal records an intent at gate 12 and stages), or an ordinary decision delayed by an
  offline peer. Relays go peer to peer (`NCH-2`: "Transport is HTTP POST to
  `http://<endpoint>/channel` at each peer's manifest-pinned endpoints"), so honest late traffic does
  this too.

## Decision (the owner's; four reviewers built it, `silence` and `silence_initial` re-prove unchanged)

1. **Record clause.** A record contributes its `first_seen` only if its own duress bit is set: this
   intent, every resident intent and every retained nonce tombstone naming the same spend commitment,
   under both PINs, as a constant-time mask. An unbound intent reads only its own record. The pair
   duress bit (`DUR-5`) is unchanged: it still ORs every record.
2. **Seed.** The minimum is seeded at `max(ratchet, now)` (`DUR-7`'s time ratchet); a decision with
   no duress-bit record starts there. `t_ceiling = start + duress_delay_secs`, still capped by
   `earliest_hot − epsilon_secs`. The owner approved the extra ratchet reader on 2026-10-12, amending
   the 2026-10-09 read set (`DUR-7`'s "exactly two", `ADR-0026`). Reviewer B argued, without building
   it, that an ordinary decision inside the horizon on an armed node then leaves `T` unchanged: make
   that a required exhibit, before and after a backward step, rather than a stated property.
3. **The outer floor and `F64`'s clamp stay on effective `now`**: a ratcheted floor writes no
   earlier deadline and moves a selected Escape's window later (`ADR-0026`'s Escape-close example).

Why these and not the alternatives (record them in ticket 2's ADR):
- **Seed at `now`** fails after a backward step: a duress hot ingress at 1000 with the ratchet at
  1000, a decision at effective 100, delay 200 → `T = 300`, due at once under `DUR-7`'s driver
  (B, C, D reproduced). Today's rule gives 1200 there.
- **Fallback `max(now, latest first_seen naming the pair)`** fails the next ordinary decision on
  another pair after that step: 310, written by the clamp (B, C).
- **The 2026-10-02 objection** ("Taking the earliest of the duress intents only would make `T`
  depend on the PIN"): its real content is `NodeInv.unarmed` (an armed run's `T` at or below a
  pin-uniform bound), which the seeded mask keeps; the written `T` already differs between runs
  since `F64`.

## Text

- `DUR-13`: the record clause, the unbound clause, the seed, the formal scope.
- `DUR-7`: the seed is a third reader of the time ratchet; "Its readers are exactly two" changes.
  Keep "No other comparison reads the ratchet" true (it is quoted by `SPN-41`, `ADR-0027` and
  `ADR-0026`). `ADR-0026` quotes "exactly two" (`ADR-0026`:29) and says "`DUR-13`'s and `DUR-14`'s
  computations, `first_seen`, `D` … stay on effective time": amend both in place (its stated
  reason, a stretch from reading ingress at the ratchet, does not apply: the seed reads no ingress).
- `SPN-41` and `ADR-0027`: "whenever the spend's own holder decision lands by `first_seen +
  duress_delay_secs`" no longer describes an unarmed `T`; derive and verify the new condition.
- **`F68`'s own row** (`16-open-findings.md`) quotes `DUR-13`'s clause word for word and narrates
  `f68_resubmission_pulls_T_in`'s trace; both stop being true here. Restate the row: the
  ordinary-record route is closed by this ticket, the two hot routes (ticket 2) are still open,
  quoting the new words. `F68` is withdrawn by ticket 2, not here.
- Every other quote of the old clause (grep "earliest `first_seen`", "earliest same-spend",
  "earliest pair ingress", "earliest ingress"; found 2026-10-12): `CNF-47` (`15-conformance-checklist.md`),
  `CONTEXT.md` *Arm intent*, `ADR-0023` ("`DUR-13` owns "the earliest `first_seen`""), and the
  docstrings of `Kernel.pairFirstSeen`, `Clocks` (the pair's earliest ingress sample) and the `F68`
  exhibit in `Exhibits.lean`. Quotes of `DUR-7`'s "exactly two": `ADR-0026`, an `Exhibits.lean`
  docstring, and `Silence.lean`'s module docstring ("both of the ratchet's readers"). Re-grep
  before closing; the list is a starting point, not the scope.

## Formal

Guard parameters with `current` values (owning module holds the trace under each value; theorems
over `current` in `Exhibits.lean`; each flip red in `Exhibits.lean` only, count measured locally,
control in `.github/workflows/gates.yml`):
- `IngressTime`: `duressOnly` current; `earliestPair` and `ownIngress` withdrawn.
- A seed parameter (e.g. `ReadTime`): `ratchet` current; `effective` withdrawn.

Exhibits that must exist and go red under the flips:
- `F68`'s resubmission with a HOT pair: `T` holds (`earliestPair` red). The current
  `f68_resubmission_pulls_T_in` uses a non-hot SpendRequest (`sp3`), which `CHN-32` refuses — fix the
  fixture.
- A late ordinary decision on an armed node (an unbound wrong-PIN Carrier staged early): `T` holds
  (`earliestPair`, `ownIngress` red).
- The backward-step pair (a) and (b) above (`effective` seed red; (b) also red under a pair-local
  fallback).

Existing exhibits whose figures change (reviewers measured, re-measure): `earliest_pair_ingress`
(80 → 90), `f68_resubmission_pulls_T_in`, `traversal_leaks_with_onlyWhenMoved`,
`chained_commit_keeps_T`, `f64_commits_grow_T_with_withdrawn`, `first_arm_writes_computed`,
`other_windows_close_on_effective_time`, `unarmed_spend_fires_past_close`; the `IngressTime` control
in `gates.yml` is rewritten.

Stated residual (not fixed here): a duress ingress stamped after a backward step carries the
rolled-back `first_seen`, so its decision can land at once (reviewer A, `backResub`).

Evidence: `/var/tmp/f68-evidence/` (`B-n`, `A-n`: built kernels; `B-r3`, `A-r3`, `C-r3`: the seed
traces).

## Done when

`DUR-13`, `DUR-7` and the texts above state the rule; the Kernel computes it; the exhibits and both
flip controls pass; `silence` and `silence_initial` prove with no new premise; the gate is green
unpiped.

title: F68 ticket 2: only hot spends still in play cap T; SEC-37 restated; ADR; F68 withdrawn
description:

Depends on ticket 1.

## The defect

- **Replay after the arm.** `SPN-23` says a repeat "re-applies its schedule", and
  `Kernel.shrunkDeadline` reads the EVENT candidate's `fireAt` on a repeat, so `DUR-14` writes
  `max(min(T, old fire_at − epsilon_secs), now) = now` (reviewers B, D: 700 → 520).
- **First arm.** `earliest_hot` ("candidate is hot, not broadcast, expiry ≥ now") still holds a hot
  spend whose window shut unfired, which can never fire in the normal run, so the first arm writes
  `now` (B: 510).

## Decision (the owner's)

1. **The domain.** `earliest_hot` and `DUR-14`'s shrink read only hot candidates not broadcast whose
   fire window is not closed at `max(ratchet, now)` (`SPN-38`'s close; "not closed" includes before
   `fire_at`). On a repeat acceptance `DUR-14` reads the RESIDENT candidate's `fire_at`. A candidate
   outside the domain leaves `T` as it is. `DUR-20`'s traversal still runs on every hot acceptance.
2. **`SEC-37` stays accepted, restated.** Not excluded: a hot spend settled (`SPN-33`) or made
   terminal by a claw-back while its window is still open. It caps `T` at the value it had while
   live, so excluding it removes no route a coercer has (A `sliver_eq_live`; B). `SEC-37` says, in
   substance: a hot spend accepted before the first duress-PIN ingress, not broadcast, whose window
   is not closed at the arm — whether or not it can still fire — brings Lockdown to its `fire_at −
   epsilon_secs` or to `now`, and a coercer who knows the owner's payment times can choose that
   moment. Beside it, the floor the fix buys, absent a backward step: once armed, `T` stays at or
   above `F + min(duress_delay_secs, hold_secs − epsilon_secs)`, `F` the first duress-PIN ingress,
   except through such a spend. Verify the sentence against the built exhibits before writing it.
3. **Not built (record in the ADR):** releasing pre-duress hot spends on an armed node (breaks
   `DUR-8`'s "a hot partial is released only when the node is NOT armed", `Kernel.Inv`,
   `hot_release_provenance`; releases a spend coerced earlier under the real PIN; breaks the sweep's
   inputs); postponing every waiting hot spend at each holder decision under both PINs (a floor of
   the full delay, but no payment fires within `duress_delay_secs + epsilon_secs` of any commit, a
   wrong-PIN Carrier becomes a PIN-less veto, and a backward step still leaves a gap); a repeat
   acceptance that retains `T` alone (a subset of the domain rule; misses the first arm); freezing
   `T` once armed (misses the first arm, reopens the stretch); accepting `F68`.

## Text

`DUR-13` (`earliest_hot`'s domain), `DUR-14` (domain; "pending at arm time"), `SPN-23` and `SPN-32`'s
schedule sentence (a repeat's `fire_at` is the resident's), `DUR-7` (the domain reads the ratchet:
name it in the reader list or show it is `SPN-38`'s close), `SEC-37`, `MAN-29` if its "ceiling"
sentence needs the residual, CNF items. Quotes of `DUR-14`'s "a hot spend pending at arm time"
(found 2026-10-12; re-grep before closing): `SEC-37`, `ADR-0012`'s accepted residuals, `CONTEXT.md`
(the hostage-window entry), and `Silence.lean`'s module docstring. The owner approved the domain's
ratchet read on 2026-10-12 with ticket 1's seed. **One new ADR for `F68`**, both tickets: the decisions,
the considered options above and ticket 1's rejected seeds. Withdraw `F68` (tombstone row in
*Withdrawn findings*).

## Formal

Guard parameter: hot domain, `live` current, today's `unexpired` withdrawn (one parameter governs
both scans and the acceptance read). Reviewer B built it on top of ticket 1's ratchet seed — the
combination being landed — with `silence` and `silence_initial` re-proving and no `sorry`. Reviewer
A built it over a plain `now` seed, also without `sorry`, and needed a scan that reads a selected
entry's close as `fire_at + combine_slack_secs` through the `unarmedT` override, because
`c.windowClose` there is pin-dependent; check whether B's build needed the same.

Exhibits that must go red under the flip: the replay holds `T`; the first arm with a shut-unfired hot
spend holds `T`; a backward step past the ratchet does not revive a shut window; one second past the
close; the floor sentence's instance. Existing: `clamp_reads_effective_below_ratchet` needs a new
discriminating trace (cited at `DUR-13` and `ADR-0026`); `ratchet_moves_only_at_its_events`'s figure
changes. Re-measure every count.

Evidence: `/var/tmp/f68-evidence/` (`B-n`, `A-n`; answers `r2-*`, `r3-*`, `r4-*`).

## Done when

The domain rule is stated and modelled; the exhibits and the flip control pass; `SEC-37` is
restated; the ADR records both tickets; `F68` is withdrawn; the gate is green unpiped.

title: SPN-34 does not say which first_seen and remaining_secs an accepted request with changed PSBT bytes returns
description:
The text does not say which `first_seen` and `remaining_secs` a node returns for a request whose
commitments match an earlier `Accepted` while its PSBT bytes differ.

`SPN-23` says a request whose acceptance key — "the spend commitment and bytes, the Escape
commitment and bytes, and every rung" — matches an earlier `Accepted` "returns that verdict
verbatim", and that "Changed PSBT bytes MUST undergo fresh evaluation even if the commitment is
unchanged". `SPN-32` says "valid changed PSBT bytes preserving the transactions remain compatible
after fresh evaluation" and "an already resident compatible pair is left exactly as is". So such a
request is evaluated afresh, registration keeps the resident pair, and gate 30 of `SPN-5` answers
`Accepted`.

`SPN-34` says the response's members are "fixed at first acceptance and replayed verbatim
thereafter", with `first_seen` "the ingress time" and `remaining_secs = fire_at − first_seen`.
`DOM-20` gives the replay log "verdicts indexed by commitment id, with matching keys owned by
`SPN-23`". Two readings follow, with different responses:

- per commitment: the second `Accepted` carries the first acceptance's `first_seen` and
  `remaining_secs`, which agree with the resident's fire time that `DUR-14` says a repeat reads;
- per acceptance key: it is a new first acceptance, carrying its own ingress time and a full
  `hold_secs` of `remaining_secs`, while the resident it leaves keeps the first acceptance's
  `fire_at`.

Nor does the text say which verdict the replay log holds for the commitment afterwards (bytes A,
then bytes B, then bytes A again).

Found while picking `bps-svf`. The formal model takes no side: it carries no PSBT bytes, so its
accepted repeat is the resident pair's (`Kernel.pairAdmits`), and `SPN-34`'s formal scope says so.
Both readings are PIN-uniform, so no SILENCE claim is affected.

Done when: the specification owner has chosen a reading, and `SPN-34` (or `SPN-23`) states it in
words a conformance item can test.

comments.text:
Decision, 2026-10-14, the owner's: one ticket, three parts, as below. Reached through a four-reviewer
review in two rounds (briefs and answers in `/var/tmp/rz5-evidence/`, one file per reviewer letter
and round). Round 1: all four chose the per-commitment reading. Round 2: all four chose to keep every
acceptance key (two had chosen keep-first in round 1), and all four judged gate 27 a behaviour gap.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** While a compatible pair is resident, an accepted request for its commitment answers the
first acceptance's instants, every key it was accepted under stays in the replay log, and gate 27
tests the resident's fire time.

**Current behavior:**
- `SPN-34` says the response members are "fixed at first acceptance and replayed verbatim
  thereafter" without saying which acceptance is first when changed PSBT bytes are accepted after
  fresh evaluation (`SPN-23`: "Changed PSBT bytes MUST undergo fresh evaluation even if the commitment
  is unchanged"; `SPN-32`: "an already resident compatible pair is left exactly as is").
- Nothing says whether such an acceptance's key joins or replaces the earlier entry in the replay
  log (`DOM-20`: "verdicts indexed by commitment id, with matching keys owned by `SPN-23`"). The
  choice is observable: a request that misses the log is evaluated afresh and can be refused (gate 21
  on a backend failure, gate 27) where a hit answers `Accepted` (`SPN-21`: "A still-fresh cached
  acceptance therefore wins over the fetch-error result").
- Gate 27 tests the request's own fire time, `ingress_now + hold_secs` (`SPN-30`), which no
  candidate carries when the pair is resident. Example: accepted at 12:00 with a one-hour Hold and
  `expiry = 13:10 + combine_slack_secs`; a re-signed request at 12:20 is refused `EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT`
  (its own 13:20 fails) while the resident still fires at 13:00. A coordinator reading the refusal
  as failure may rebuild the payment.

**Desired behavior:**
1. **Response.** A request accepted while a compatible pair from an earlier acceptance of its
   commitment is resident answers that earlier acceptance's `first_seen` and `remaining_secs`, whether
   it matched the log or its changed PSBT bytes were evaluated afresh. `SPN-34`'s lower bound is
   measured from that `first_seen`. The kernel already answers this way and `SPN-34`'s formal scope
   already says so ("a request whose PSBT bytes changed is answered as such a repeat").
2. **Replay log.** The log keeps every acceptance key a commitment was accepted under until the
   commitment's expiry, all answering the commitment's first `Accepted`; a later acceptance adds its
   key and replaces nothing. After bytes A, then B, both A and B are verbatim hits. `SPN-23`'s
   "matches an earlier `Accepted`" must read as any retained one. The number of keys per commitment
   is bounded by the nonce log, not by a new limit: each acceptance consumes a fresh live nonce
   (`SPN-11`'s 4 096 live entries; `SPN-14`: "Capacity **refuses; it never evicts.**"; `SPN-13`'s
   high-water). If you state the bound, cite those; do not add a new cap.
3. **Gate 27.** When the request's registration would retain a compatible resident pair (`SPN-32`),
   gate 27's `expiry ≥ fire_at + combine_slack_secs` reads the resident spend's `fire_at`; otherwise
   `ingress_now + hold_secs` as today. State it in `SPN-30`'s prose; leave `SPN-5`'s row 27 as it is
   (that table is rendered from `BtcPolicy.Render.spn5Gates`).

**Key interfaces:** `SPN-34` (part 1 and the lower bound's anchor), `SPN-23` and `SPN-24` (part 2),
`SPN-30` (part 3), `15-conformance-checklist.md`'s `CNF-34` changed-bytes case. Check every sentence
that restates `first_seen`, `remaining_secs` or the replay log's keys for agreement (`API-12`'s
"`first_seen` is the node's ingress time", `DOM-20`, `STO-6`, `API-4`, the wire contract's `Accepted`
example), and change only what disagrees.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `SPN-34` states part 1 in words a conformance item can test, including where the lower bound
      is measured from.
- [ ] `SPN-23`/`SPN-24` state part 2; no sentence anywhere says a later acceptance replaces an
      earlier key.
- [ ] `SPN-30` states part 3 for a resident compatible pair; row 27 of `SPN-5` is unchanged.
- [ ] `CNF-34`'s changed-bytes case is extended: accept bytes A at `t0`; accept re-signed bytes B at
      `t0 + Δ` with `expiry` chosen so B's own `ingress_now + hold_secs` would fail gate 27 and the
      resident's passes, asserting `Accepted` with A's `first_seen` and `remaining_secs`; then send A
      and B again with the backend failing, asserting the cached `Accepted` for both; the candidate
      fires at A's `fire_at`.
- [ ] No Lean statement changes. `SPN-34`'s formal scope stays true as written or is corrected in
      words only.
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, run unpiped.

**HARD STOPS** (verify each before committing; stop the Run and report rather than continue):
1. Part 3 needs a change to a Lean declaration's statement, or to `SPN-5`'s rendered table.
2. The text cannot make gate 27 and gate 29 read the same residency for one request (the registry
   sits under the channel store lock, `DOM-21`; `SPN-5`'s table puts rows 15 to 30,
   27 and 29 among them, in `SPN-20`'s registration hold, which is the sign lock). Report what the text says; do not invent a lock or an ordering.
3. Any part needs a new requirement identifier or a new limit.

**Out of scope:** refresh and claw-back responses (`remaining_secs` is zero for them); gates 13 and
16, which test the request's expiry against now by design (`SPN-21`: "even though an earlier request
was accepted"); the kernel's registration; the three independent expiries in the model.

title: Citation gate resolves BtcPolicy names, full and short form, in Markdown and Lean docstrings, against every project declaration
description:
The citation gate cannot fail on a `BtcPolicy.*` name in a Lean docstring.

`tools/check_citations.py` checks quotes in root Markdown, `docs/adr/` and Lean docstrings, but
`unresolved(docs)` resolves `BtcPolicy.*` names only over the Markdown documents: `main()` calls it
with `docs`, never with the docstrings `load()` returns as `lean`. A made-up name cited from a Lean
docstring stays green. Probed in `bps-2k5.7`'s review: renaming `BtcPolicy.Silence.sysStep_unarmedT`
to a name that does not exist, inside `Kernel.Node.unarmedT`'s docstring, left the gate at exit 0.

A second limit sits behind it: `lean_names()` reads `.lake/index.jsonl`, which holds tagged
declarations, their namespaces and the imported modules. An untagged theorem
(`BtcPolicy.Silence.silence_initial`, `sysStep_unarmedT`, `obsPair_unarmedT` and most exhibits'
helpers) is not in it, so Markdown cannot cite one without the gate refusing a real name, and a
docstring citation of one could not be resolved either.

The gate's own summary line claims "BtcPolicy.* names", and the clock family's instructions rely on

`check_citations.py` row, and move every `gates.yml` expectation that asserts the old string.

title: The model's response to an accepted repeat carries the request's own fire time, where SPN-23 returns the first verdict
description:
The model's response to an accepted repeat carries the request's own fire time, where `SPN-23` returns the first verdict.

`SPN-23` says a request whose acceptance key matches an earlier `Accepted` "returns that verdict
verbatim". `Silence.respond`, the projection `Silence.silence` compares, builds the response to an
accepted repeat from the incoming request record's `fireAt`.

Measured at `b203177` by the reviewer of `bps-860`
(`/var/tmp/cross-evidence/request-fields/Traces.lean`, `respond_reads_request_fireAt_on_repeat`, by
`decide +kernel`): `fU 300` accepted at 10 answers with fire time 310. A repeat at 30 answers with
310, 330 or none, as its own record says, while the step's resulting system is the same in all
three and the resident keeps 310. On an armed node the same repeat leaves `T` at 700.

Only the modelled response differs, and it differs the same way under both PINs, so no proved
equality is affected. What is off is the model's fidelity to `SPN-23` and `SPN-34`: the response the
theorem compares on a repeat is not the one the text returns. `Silence.respond` is unchanged since
before `bps-pxp`, so the published tree has it too.

Done when: the modelled response to an accepted repeat is the first verdict's, read from the
resident and not from the request record (say in the closing comment which fields that fixes and
which, if any, the model does not carry); an exhibit shows a repeat whose record carries a different
fire time answering as the first acceptance did; a planted-mutation control restores the old read
and goes red in `Exhibits.lean` only; `Silence.silence` and `Silence.silence_initial` keep their
statements; the gate is green unpiped.

title: Finding: a compromised node release can write the normal PIN into state the coordinator persists
description:
Record an open finding in `16-open-findings.md`, using the next unused finding number, from the
design review of `API-25`'s fault list (2026-10-05, four readers). This bead records the finding
and leaves it open: no requirement changes. Write it as an open finding in the file's existing
format, with provenance by reviewer letter or role.

## The finding

The SILENCE adversary holds the coordinator and the physical scene but no node (`OVR-13`,
`SEC-10`, `DUR-1`). `DOM-2` describes it as a coordinator "holding the coordinator auth key but no
history of the normal PIN". `OVR-13` puts a compromised node out of scope for silence, because
"A node sees the submitted PIN in plaintext".

That boundary assumes nothing PIN-derived reaches what the coordinator retains. A node can break
the assumption without colluding with the wrench holder: a backdoored node release, whose encoding
anyone holding the release can recover, writes the normal PIN into node-chosen values that the
operator program persists. Whoever later seizes the coordinator reads those values while holding
no node, which is exactly the adversary the guarantee covers, and gains the PIN history `DOM-2`
says it lacks.

The channels exist today, without `API-25`:
- `OPR-60` persists each node's returned `/events` cursor. `API-18` makes it an integer the node
  assigns, up to 2⁵³ − 1 under `WIR-1`.
- `OPR-60` also persists events whose txids, outpoints and scripts the node chooses (`API-18`).

`OPS-47`'s reproducible, signed releases reduce the backdoor risk but do not exclude it.
`ADR-0012` already accepts that a compromised node "can hand the harvested normal pin to a
hostile-at-wrench coordinator". The difference here is that the hand-off needs no coordinated
adversary.

## The open question to record

Either state the premise the guarantee actually rests on, that no node runs a compromised
release, or constrain what the operator program persists from node-chosen values. Name both
options, and the requirements each would touch (`OVR-13`, `SEC-10`, `DOM-2`, `OPR-60`,
`API-18`). Do not choose between them.

## Done when

- The finding has landed, with every quotation verbatim; the citation gate checks them.
- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, run unpiped.

title: Conformance and CI: CNF-143 splits a rung's inputs, a planted mutation guards receivePartial's input-0 check, and HonestExposureProvenance names its class residual
description:
This bead lands three small items from the 2026-10-06 review of the external vault-properties
proposal's per-input (§4.1) and federation (§4.3) sections. The review kept both boundaries: the
kernel gets no per-input or per-rung possession model and no federation model. It found two
checks those boundaries leave untested and one premise whose docstring hides a condition.

## Findings

1. **`CNF-143` never splits a rung's inputs.** `SPN-39` finalizes "at the highest rung at or
   below the latch that carries at least `t` distinct valid partials on every input, walking
   downward". A rung's inputs can legitimately hold different signer sets: `NCH-23` sends "one
   message per released rung per signed input", `NCH-25` keys the store "per `(rung, input,
   signer)`", and `NCH-15`'s quota decides which messages get through. `CNF-143` states the rule
   but demonstrates only the arming/send ordering, and `CNF-149` arranges delivery of "every base
   partial to every node". No item demonstrates either of these:
   - a rung at or below the latch holding `t` on input 0 and `t − 1` on input 1 is skipped for a
     lower rung complete on every input;
   - with `t = 2`, a rung holding A+B on input 0 and B+C on input 1 is finalized: each input meets
     `t` on its own, and no identical signer subset across inputs is required.

   The Lean kernel keeps input 0 standing for every input (`Kernel.Cand.heldSigners`), so this is
   conformance evidence, not a Lean claim.

2. **`receivePartial`'s input-0 guard has no CI control.** `Kernel.receivePartial` stores a peer
   partial only when `c.id == cid && input == 0 && msg == sighash c.tx 0`. Its docstring says "the
   store admits exactly the row `exposedQuorum` counts, and `released_held_exposed` rests on it".
   Deleting `input == 0 &&` breaks the build (a reviewer's scratch run failed at
   `Kernel.heldExposed_step`'s `receivePartial` case), but `gates.yml` plants no mutation there.

3. **`HonestExposureProvenance` hides a class condition.** It quantifies over every exposed row
   on the message at input 0, and `no_exposed_quorum_without_normal`'s docstring says it counts
   them "with no commitment or hot-class filter". `hot_release_provenance` supplies normal-release
   evidence for hot effects only, and `firePass` also queues non-hot (Escape) partials at
   `sighash c.tx 0`. So the premise also assumes that no honest non-hot row shares the target
   message. In the system distinct transactions have distinct messages, which is message binding
   (`CHN-11`'s `SIGHASH_ALL` BIP143 sighash), Bitcoin Core's authority under `ADR-0025` point 3. A
   reviewer's scratch exhibit, with a non-hot candidate on the same `tx.id`, falsifies the premise
   while unforgeability holds.

## Scope

- **`CNF-143`** gains the two demonstrations above, quoting `SPN-39` and adding `SPN-39`, `NCH-23`
  and `NCH-25` to its trailing list.
- **`gates.yml`** gains one planted-mutation step, shaped like the existing ones. In a temp copy, a
  `sed` deletes `input == 0 && ` from `receivePartial`'s guard, a `grep -qxF` proves the edit
  landed, `lake build` must fail, and the step pins the exact error count, files and declaration
  names. Measure them with `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py '<step
  name>'`. Put the step on a shard other than 3, which is already the heaviest.
- **`HonestExposureProvenance`'s docstring** gains a sentence naming the residual: the premise

title: Citation gate skips every quote in a sentence containing "for example", inside a quotation included (TEACHING)
description:
The citation gate skips every quote in a sentence that contains "for example" anywhere, including
inside a quotation.

`TEACHING` in `tools/check_citations.py` (`is an assertion|is a claim, and|checkable;|for example`)
is searched over the whole chunk, quotes included, with no word boundaries, and a match skips the
chunk whole: no quote in it is checked and no unquoted attribution counted. It exists so `AGENTS.md`
can show the mistake the rule forbids, and at `4ddca43` that is the only chunk it exempts. But "for
example" is common current prose, and a quoted body containing it exempts the sentence that quotes
it -- the shape `HISTORICAL` had before it read only the prose outside quotes, and that `bps-mmt`
removed for history markers.

Probe: `` For example, `OVR-1` says "a phrase OVR-1 has never contained anywhere". `` and
`` `OVR-1` says "x for example y z w" `` (false) are both green.

Done when: the teaching exemption applies only to a sentence that actually teaches the rule (the
`AGENTS.md` example), never through a quoted body and never through ordinary prose; every chunk the
narrowed rule newly checks passes or is corrected; and a `gates.yml` control plants a false quote in
a sentence that says "for example" and asserts the refusal.

title: Operator program: batched refresh, up to 24 old-enough coins merged into one, ages read from block headers, maturity by BIP68 time
description:
The owner decided this in a grill on 2026-10-06, after a four-reader review of the age check.
`refresh` stops composing one transaction per coin. It batches up to 24 coins into one
transaction with a single vault output, and it chooses the coins from its own age check against
`SPN-46`'s rule.

## Why

`OPR-65` composes "**one one-input, one-output transaction per coin**". It gives two reasons, and
both lapse once the program can read ages itself:
- "It does NOT pre-check `SPN-46`'s interval: that needs the confirming block's
  median-time-past, which none of the calls listed in `OPR-32` returns".
- "The one-coin shape follows `OPR-9`". The never-act rule governs "a fault list or a comparison
  derived from it". Choosing coins from the program's own chain reads is not that.

A vault with 30 coins today needs 30 signings and 30 fees per refresh cycle, and with
"reporting and stopping" one fresh deposit early in the run stalls the rest. The node already
takes batches: `SPN-44` allows "at most **24** inputs" and says "a vault with more coins
refreshes in batches".

## Decisions

1. **Merge.** A batch spends up to 24 coins into ONE output paying the vault script. Every
   `spend` already spends every coin (`OPR-33`) into one change output, and the vault has one
   script, so merging reveals nothing new. The watch keeps reading output 0 (`OPR-51`).
   "consolidation is not offered" goes.
2. **Age check: one new read-only call.** `OPR-32`'s set grows from eight to nine calls with
   `getblockheader(blockhash, true)`, the same read the node uses (`WTC-2`: "what `SPN-46` reads
   for both the tip and a coin's confirming block"). For each coin:
   - take the scan's height, then `getblockhash(height)`, then block-qualified
     `getrawtransaction(txid, false, blockhash)`. This binds the confirming block to the creating
     transaction by txid, as `SPN-46` requires ("found from the input's creating transaction by
     txid ... NEVER from the prevout read's confirmed flag");
   - then `getblockheader` on that hash. Require `confirmations ≥ 1` and a height equal to the
     scanned height, and read `mediantime`.

   The tip's median time comes from `getblockheader` on the before-tip hash the pass already
   agrees on, not from `getblockchaininfo`. All header reads happen before the closing tip read,
   so `OPR-33`'s "accepts only if every tip read agrees" keeps its words. A failed read is
   terminal, never an omission (`OPR-33`: "every other error is terminal"). A height-based
   estimate was rejected: `ADR-0019` says "Two age rules in two units would be a trap".
3. **Margin.** The program batches a coin only if `MTP(tip) − MTP(confirming) ≥ I +
   min(86 400, I)`, with `I` = `refresh_min_interval_secs` and equality passing. On the default
   vault that is one day above the interval. On a short test interval the margin is the interval
   itself, since the manifest only refuses `refresh_min_interval_secs = 0`. Median-time-past never
   falls along a chain, so every honest node less than the margin behind the program's tip
   admits the coin. This is a program constant, and no node reads it. `SPN-46` is unchanged.
4. **Order.** Eligible coins are sorted oldest first (earliest confirming median-time-past, so
   earliest maturity), with ties broken by canonical outpoint order, and cut into consecutive
   batches of at most 24. The batches are composed from one accepted inventory pass. Each batch
   is its own transaction and its own `RefreshAuthorization` (one PSBT, as today).
5. **Dust.** Every eligible coin goes in, with no value threshold. The merge absorbs a dust coin
   once, and `SPN-47`'s cap bounds each batch's fee.
6. **Refusal.** On a refusal the program reports and stops, as `OPR-65` does today. Batches not
   yet sent stay unsent. It never drops a coin, splits a batch or retries from a refusal
   (`OPR-9`). Held-back coins (too young, or inside the margin) are reported by count only, since
   `OPR-8` redacts outpoints.

7. **Maturity from median time.** `CHN-4`'s recovery lock is "a **per-vault** BIP68 time-based
   relative lock", but `OPR-62` computes maturity "from its confirmation height". Counting blocks
   reports maturity late whenever blocks run slow, so `OPR-63`'s nags can fire after a coin has
   matured. `OPR-62` instead computes each coin's maturity with BIP68's time-based semantics, from
   the same header reads. Under BIP68 a time-based lock counts from the median-time-past of the
   block BEFORE the one that confirmed the coin, not from `SPN-46`'s `MTP(confirming)`. Verify that
   against BIP68 and BIP112 and state it exactly. `OPR-63`'s fractions stay as they are.

## Scope

- `17-operator-program.md`:
  - **`OPR-32`:** nine calls, with the new one's exact signature.
  - **`OPR-33`:**
    - scope "there is no coin selection and no omission" to the spend and claw-back composers, and
      point refresh at `OPR-65`'s age filter, which leaves no Escape under-covered;
    - add the header reads to the pass list, before the closing tip read.
  - **`OPR-50`:** "the seven ordinary backend reads" becomes eight.
  - **`OPR-51`:** confine "no new backend method" to the watch.
  - **`OPR-62`:** maturity per decision 7. Keep "readable without the coordinator being trusted
    or alive, from the descriptor and a chain view alone".
  - **`OPR-65`:** rewrite it to carry decisions 1–6. Delete "It does NOT pre-check", "The one-coin
    shape follows" and "refresh in place, per coin". Keep "This diagnostic feature adds no chain
    calls": it refers to fault lists. `OPR-34` is unchanged, since age filtering happens after
    whole-inventory validation.
- `15-conformance-checklist.md`:
  - **`CNF-93`:** "exactly the eight read-only methods".
  - **`CNF-122`:** "one-input, one-output transaction per coin ... without pre-checking the
    interval".
  - **`CNF-150`:** "Refresh remains one transaction per coin".
  - **`CNF-125`:** maturity follows BIP68 time semantics. Include a case where block-count maturity
    and time maturity disagree.
  - **A new conformance item** covering:
    - a coin one second either side of the margin boundary;
    - a missing or stale header (fails closed);
    - a reorg between reads;
    - deterministic oldest-first batches of 24, 24 and 2;
    - one young coin held back while the rest batch;
    - refusal of batch 2 leaving batch 3 unsent;
    - the held-back count;
    - selection independent of any fault list.
- **`CONTEXT.md`:** *Refresh* reads "resets a coin's recovery timelock". Make it "resets the
  recovery timelock of the coins it spends".
- **`docs/archive/closed-findings.md`,** if a withdrawn row or narrative records the one-coin
  rationale: add a line saying it no longer holds.

## Out of scope

- Node rules: `SPN-43`–`SPN-47`, `WTC-2`, `OPR-9`.
- A block-denominated interval at the node.
- One signing for several batches.

## Done when

`nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0 unpiped, `tools/check_ids.py` accepts the
new conformance id, and a grep finds no remaining "eight calls", "one transaction per coin" or
"does NOT pre-check" anywhere in the set.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Owner decisions of 2026-10-07, after a four-reader review of the questions the first Run's Manager raised (all four readers agreed):

1. **Maturity evidence is independent of the composer.** A new requirement `OPR-82`, placed after `OPR-33`, owns one header-validation contract, run over a coin set the caller supplies inside one tip bracket. It covers the block-qualified creating transaction, `getblockhash`, and `getblockheader` with its confirmations, height and MTP checks for the confirming block, the predecessor `P` and the tip. Any missing, stale, inactive, mismatched or failed evidence fails the whole evidence set, never by skipping a coin. It makes NO mempool-inclusive `gettxout` call, because that read hides mempool-spent coins and brings back `OPR-34`'s refusal. Do not move `ed1798d`'s two header paragraphs into it verbatim: their "opening value" refers to the composer's `gettxout`. The composer (`OPR-33`) runs `OPR-82` inside its own pass and keeps its empty-set check, Escape preflight, open/close step, coinbase rule and `OPR-34`. `balance`/`OPR-58`, `OPR-62` and `recover`/`OPR-72` run `OPR-82` without the composer's preconditions, and `OPR-74` ("no manifest at all") holds. An empty vault lists zero coins under `balance`, not a refusal. `OPR-32`'s "composer's chain backend" becomes the program's chain backend.
2. **Mempool-spent coins count.** Maturity's unspent set is the confirmed chain UTXO set (`scantxoutset`). A coin whose vault spend sits in the mempool keeps counting until that spend confirms. Eviction changes nothing, and a residency of days changes nothing.
3. **Zero eligible coins:** `refresh` sends nothing and writes no authorization. It reports on stdout that nothing is eligible, with the held-back count, and exits 0. Widen `OPR-4`'s `0` clause, and `OPR-2`'s success wording if needed, to cover this case explicitly. Add the case to the existing conformance items (`CNF-116`, `CNF-122`, `CNF-151`).
4. **Batches fill:** 24, 24, then the remainder (already accepted). `OPR-65` must require filling each batch before starting the next, so only the last can be shorter. `CNF-151`'s "24, 24 and 2" must quote that rule.

Conformance: `CNF-151`'s `OPR-33` owner and its quotes move to `OPR-82` where they now live there. `CNF-124` adds remaining chain time and the empty vault. `CNF-125` adds the case where the earliest coin is mempool-spent, then evicted, then confirmed, with no jump in the figure. `CNF-126` adds maturity with no manifest. Open and unverified, so state the boundary rather than invent a rule: where `balance` and `recover` get the network `WTC-3` checks when there is no manifest.

title: Gate 27 tests a re-signed request own fire time while its pair is resident; reading the resident fire time races NCH-24 eviction
description:
Gate 27 tests a re-signed request's own fire time, which no candidate carries while its pair is
resident, so a late re-signed request is refused while the payment still fires. Testing the
resident's fire time instead lets the pair leave between gate 27 and registration, which would then
birth a pair whose fire time gate 27 never tested.

The gap. `SPN-30`: "A hot-class spend's fire time is `ingress_now + hold_secs`" and "A hot spend
MUST satisfy `expiry ≥ fire_at + combine_slack_secs`". A request with changed PSBT bytes for a
commitment whose pair is resident is tested on its own `ingress_now + hold_secs`, though
registration keeps the resident (`SPN-32`: "an already resident compatible pair is left exactly as
is"). Accepted at 12:00 with a one-hour Hold and `expiry = 13:10 + combine_slack_secs`, a re-signed
request at 12:20 is refused `EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT` while the resident still fires at 13:00. A
four-reviewer review judged this a behaviour gap, unanimously
(`/var/tmp/rz5-evidence/r2-<reviewer>.md`, Question 2).

The race. The fix (gate 27 reads the resident's fire time) was `bps-rz5`'s part 3; its Run stopped
at that brief's HARD STOP 2 (`/var/tmp/rz5-evidence/run3-blocked.md`). Gate 27 runs in the
registration hold, under the sign lock (`SPN-20`, `SPN-5`'s table), while the candidate registry
sits under the channel store lock (`DOM-21`). The pair gate 27 read can leave before registration
by three routes: `NCH-24`'s lookup ("it is not expired (`expiry < now`, except the delayed-slot
exemption of `SPN-41`), else evict it"), `SPN-41`'s prune at expiry, and `SPN-41`'s removal of a
selected pair on an armed node "regardless of their own expiries". No long registration hold is
needed: a forward wall step does it, of the kind `DEF-1` names ("A transient forward excursion — an
NTP step, a VM restore, an RTC fault"). With both members gone, registration births the pair
(`SPN-32`: "registration MUST admit both distinct ids together when both are absent") with the
request's own fire time, which gate 27 never tested, against `SPN-30`'s MUST.

Decided 2026-10-17: gate 27 tests the fire time of the spend registration would leave registered,
and registration re-decides gate 27 on the registry it registers against, refusing
`EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT` / `commitment_expiry`. The decision, its tally and the contract are in the Agent
Brief comment.

Done when the Agent Brief's acceptance criteria hold.

title: Escape wallet: multisig preferred, single-sig accepted, with a bring-your-own descriptor checked per cosigner
description:
The owner decided on 2026-10-05 that the escape wallet should preferably be multisig, with single-sig
still accepted. `CONTEXT.md` already defines it as "An offline wallet, preferably multisig with
single-sig accepted". The rest of the set still assumes one key.
- `MAN-26` makes `keygen` emit `wpkh([<fingerprint>]<xpub>/*)` for the escape.
- An escape bundle carries one `master_fingerprint`.
- `MAN-28` compares fingerprints as if there were one key.
- `OPS-16`, `OPS-30` and `ADR-0021` say "single-key escape wallet".
- `OPS-60` and `DOM-11` speak of "the escape-wallet key".

## Decisions

1. **The escape wallet SHOULD be multisig, and single-sig stays accepted.** Put the SHOULD in
   `DOM-11`. `keygen`'s escape banner (`MAN-26`) gains one line saying a multisig escape wallet
   is preferred.
2. **The Operator brings their own descriptor.** The ceremony accepts an escape bundle with:
   - a descriptor in `MAN-39`'s grammar whose keys are all ranged extended keys with origin;
   - the master fingerprint of every cosigner.

   It is built with the Operator's own multisig tooling. `keygen` keeps its `wpkh` path for
   single-sig. The spec adds no multisig construction tooling.
3. **The independence check covers every cosigner (`MAN-28`).**
   - Each cosigner's derived and ancestor keys are checked against the user, node, recovery and
     coordinator keys and against the hot wallet.
   - Each cosigner's fingerprint is checked against the hot wallet's.
   - The check refuses two cosigners that share a master fingerprint, since that is a multisig
     in name only.
   - `independence.txt` records every cosigner.
4. **Key-count wording.**
   - `DOM-11`: each escape key is generated on a device that holds no other vault role.
   - `OPS-60`: custody covers a threshold of escape keys and their backups, and duress becomes
     theft when the attacker holds that threshold.
   - `OPS-16`, `OPS-30` and `ADR-0021`: "single-key escape wallet" becomes "escape wallet".
   - `SEC-54`: row 10 and row L6 become thresholds. The coercer needs `k` escape keys; a loss
     needs more than `m − k` keys gone.
5. **Check every other single-key assumption** about the escape, including `CHN-35`'s claw-back,
   `WIR-7`'s fixture comment, the formal exhibits and the conformance items. Change only the
   ones that are wrong for a multisig descriptor. `CHN-34` already counts the actual output
   bytes.
6. **Conformance.** Extend the independence-check conformance item with these cases:
   - a valid 2-of-3 accepted;
   - two cosigners sharing a fingerprint, refused;
   - a cosigner key equal to a node key, refused;
   - a cosigner sharing the hot wallet's fingerprint, refused;
   - a single-sig escape still accepted.

## Out of scope

Requiring multisig; multisig construction or signing tooling; the escape wallet's own spending
policy.

## Done when

- The decisions have landed, with completeness checked by grep for "single-key", "escape-wallet
  key" and "master_fingerprint".
- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, run unpiped.
- Every control whose count moves is re-measured.

## Decided 2026-10-06: the descriptor is the Operator's choice

A Run blocked on this question: `MAN-39`'s grammar admits Miniscript policies that no single
`k`-of-`m` describes. For example, `wsh(or_i(pk(A),and_v(v:pk(B),pk(C))))` lets `A` spend
alone, or `B` and `C` together. Meanwhile `SEC-54` rows 10 and L6, `OPS-60` and `CNF-131` were
written in threshold terms. The owner's answer is to keep the full grammar and not restrict
the escape wallet. An exotic spending policy is the Operator's own concern.
- **The ceremony.** It accepts any escape descriptor that meets the stated grammar and per-key
  checks. Add no eligibility condition, descriptor-analysis engine or policy classifier.
- **`E`** means spending authority under the supplied descriptor.
- **Where the formulas apply.** The `k` and `m − k` formulas are stated for a `k`-of-`m`
  escape wallet, with single-sig as 1-of-1.
- **Other policies.** For any other policy, the set makes no threshold-based coercion, custody
  or loss claim. `OPS-60`'s custody duty becomes: cover the key sets that can spend under the
  descriptor, as the Operator identifies them. It does not require a numeric threshold.
- **`CNF-131`** follows the same boundary.
